definition_zh: 决定；解决；分解；溶解；（症状）消退；解析；决心
definition_en: to decide firmly, to settle a problem or dispute, or to separate something into its parts
core_image: 解开的绳结：把绞紧的结松开，再让它落到一个确定的位置
scene: At the community meeting, the two neighbours finally resolve their dispute over the shared fence and shake hands.
sceneCN: 这里 resolve 是「解决、化解」（第 2 个义项：解决争端）；句意：在社区会议上，两位邻居终于化解了关于共用栅栏的争端并握手。图中可辨识物件：社区会议室、长桌、栅栏图纸、两位邻居、握在一起的手。

pos.zh: 解决；分解；溶解；决定；消退；解析

senses.title: Decide firmly: fix the mind on one course
senses.titleCN: 下定决心：把心思定在一条路上
senses.definition: to decide firmly that you will do something, after a period of doubt or wavering
senses.definitionCN: 经过犹豫或摇摆之后，坚定地决定要做某事
senses.example: She resolved to finish the race even if she came last.
senses.exampleCN: 她下定决心要跑完比赛，哪怕最后一名。
senses.why: Re- means 'back, again' and solvere means 'to loosen'. Doubt is a knot pulled tight in the mind; resolving loosens it and lets the mind settle back onto one fixed point.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示“回、再”，solvere 表示“松开”。犹豫是心里被拉紧的结；下决心就是把结松开，让心思重新落回一个固定的点上。

senses.title: Settle a problem or dispute
senses.titleCN: 解决问题或争端
senses.definition: to find an answer to a problem, or to bring a disagreement to an end
senses.definitionCN: 为问题找到答案，或使分歧结束
senses.example: The two sides resolved their differences without going to court.
senses.exampleCN: 双方没有上法庭就化解了分歧。
senses.why: A problem or dispute is a knot that keeps two things tied together. To resolve it is to loosen that knot so the parties can separate and move on.
senses.whyCN: 问题或争端就是把两方系在一起的结。resolve 就是松开这个结，让双方得以分开、继续前行。

senses.title: Break something into its parts
senses.titleCN: 分解成组成部分
senses.definition: to separate something into its component parts, especially by analysis
senses.definitionCN: 把某物拆分为其组成部分，尤指通过分析
senses.example: The analyst resolved the complex process into five simple steps.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师把这一复杂流程分解成五个简单步骤。
senses.why: This sense is recorded from the 1540s and follows solvere literally: to loosen a compound until its pieces come apart.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从 16 世纪 40 年代起有记录，直接沿用 solvere 的字面义：把复合体松开，直到各部分脱落分开。

senses.title: Dissolve or resolve into in chemistry and optics
senses.titleCN: 化学与光学中的“溶解、解析为”
senses.definition: to change into, or be separated into, different substances or forms, as in resolve into
senses.definitionCN: 转变为或被分离为不同的物质或形态，如 resolve into
senses.example: On heating, the white powder resolves into two simpler compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 加热时，这种白色粉末分解成两种更简单的化合物。
senses.why: Dissolving is the clearest picture of solvere: the bonds that hold a substance together are loosened, and its parts are released into the liquid or the flame.
senses.whyCN: 溶解是 solvere 最清楚的画面：把物质维系的键松开，各部分便释放到液体或火焰中。

senses.title: Of a symptom: gradually disappear
senses.titleCN: 医学上：症状逐渐消退
senses.definition: of a symptom, illness or swelling, to lessen and disappear over time
senses.definitionCN: 指症状、疾病或肿块随着时间减轻并消失
senses.example: The fever resolved on its own after three days.
senses.exampleCN: 三天后，发烧自行消退了。
senses.why: An illness is described as a knot tied in the body. When the knot loosens, the symptom unties itself and the body returns to its usual state.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被比作身体里打下的结。结松开后，症状自行解开，身体回到常态。

senses.title: Music: move from tension to a consonant chord
senses.titleCN: 音乐：从紧张和弦走向协和
senses.definition: in music, to move from a dissonant chord to a consonant one that completes the harmony
senses.definitionCN: 音乐中，从刺耳的不协和和弦进行到完成和声的协和和弦
senses.example: The final chord resolves into the tonic and the piece ends.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个和弦解决到主音，乐曲结束。
senses.why: A dissonant chord is a tightened knot of sound; resolution is the loosening that lets the harmony lie flat and at rest.
senses.whyCN: 不协和和弦是声音里被拉紧的结；解决就是把它松开，让和声平展、落定。

senses.title: Optics: make fine detail distinguishable
senses.titleCN: 光学：分辨出细微细节
senses.definition: to make two close points or fine details separately visible, as a lens or telescope does
senses.definitionCN: 使两个相近的点或细微细节能够被分开看清，如镜头或望远镜所为
senses.example: This telescope can resolve details on the surface of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 这台望远镜能分辨出月球表面的细节。
senses.why: Two points that blur into one are stuck together. To resolve them is to loosen that blur until the eye can hold them apart.
senses.whyCN: 糊成一点的两个点原本黏在一起。resolve 就是把这片模糊松开，直到眼睛能把它们分开握住。

senses.title: Literary: melt into tears or laughter
senses.titleCN: 文学用法：化为泪水或笑声
senses.definition: in literary style, to pass into another state, especially to dissolve into tears or laughter
senses.definitionCN: 文学笔法中转入另一种状态，尤指化为泪水或笑声
senses.example: At the news, she resolved into tears and could not speak.
senses.exampleCN: 听到消息，她一下子化为泪水，说不出话来。
senses.why: The self is pictured as a held shape; the grip loosens and the person flows out of that shape into weeping, just as a solid loosens into liquid.
senses.whyCN: 自我被想象成一个被握住的形状；握力一松，人就从那个形状流出，变成哭泣，正如固体松开成液体。

senses.title: Noun: a firm decision or determination
senses.titleCN: 名词：决心、坚定的决定
senses.definition: a firm decision to do something; determination
senses.definitionCN: 要做某事的坚定决定；决心
senses.example: He made a resolve to study for an hour every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他下定决心每天早上学习一小时。
senses.why: The noun, recorded from the 1590s, names the fixed point that remains after the mind has loosened its doubt and settled.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词从 16 世纪 90 年代起有记录，指的正是心思松开犹豫、落定之后留下的那个固定点。

intro.en: Resolve came through French from Latin resolvere, literally 'to loosen back'. The 'loosen' image survives in every modern sense, from deciding to dissolving. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resolve 经由法语来自拉丁 resolvere，字面是“往回松开”。从“决定”到“溶解”，每个现代义项都保留着“松开”这个意象。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as the verb resolven, meaning 'to dissolve, melt, disintegrate' and also 'to settle, determine'. The earliest uses still describe something physically coming apart.
items.cn: 最早以动词 resolven 记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“溶解、融化、瓦解”，也有“确定、决定”之义。最早的用法仍在描述某物在物理上散开。

items.en: The word was borrowed through Old French resoudre from Latin resolvere. English later fixed the spelling as resolve.
items.cn: 这个词经由古法语 resoudre 借入，源自拉丁 resolvere。英语后来把拼写固定为 resolve。

items.en: The sense 'to decide or determine' is recorded from the 1520s: the mind stops wavering and fixes on one course.
items.cn: “决定、下决心”的义项从 16 世纪 20 年代起有记录：心思停止摇摆，固定到一条路线上。

items.en: The sense 'reduce to parts, analyze' appears in the 1540s, matching the Latin image of loosening a compound into its pieces.
items.cn: “分解为部分、分析”的义项出现于 16 世纪 40 年代，对应拉丁语中把复合体松开成各部分的意象。

items.en: The noun resolve, meaning 'a firm decision', is recorded from the 1590s and was formed directly from the verb.
items.cn: 名词 resolve 意为“坚定的决定”，从 16 世纪 90 年代起有记录，直接由动词构成。

items.en: Latin resolvere is re- 'back, again' + solvere 'to loosen, untie'. Solvere is usually traced to PIE *se-lu-, from the reflexive *s(w)e- 'self' plus *leu- 'to loosen, cut apart'.
items.cn: 拉丁 resolvere = re-“回、再”+ solvere“松开、解开”。solvere 通常上溯至原始印欧语 *se-lu-，由反身代词 *s(w)e-“自己”加 *leu-“松开、切开”构成。

note.en: The first group collects spelling neighbours and word-family members; the second collects words that share part of the meaning but not the root.
note.cn: 第一组收集拼写相近的词和同族词；第二组收集义近但词根不同的词。

entries.definition: to find the answer to a problem. It is the bare Latin solvere without the re- prefix, so it keeps only the 'loosen the knot' part.
entries.definitionCN: 找到问题的答案。它是去掉 re- 前缀的纯拉丁 solvere，只保留“松开结”的部分。

entries.definition: firm and determined in character. It comes from the same Latin participle but describes a settled person, not the act of settling.
entries.definitionCN: 性格坚定果断的。它出自同一个拉丁分词，但描述的是一个已定下来的人，而不是“定下来”这个动作。

entries.definition: what is left over after a process. It looks like resolve but comes from Latin residere 'to remain behind', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 过程结束后剩下的东西。它看起来像 resolve，却来自拉丁 residere“留在后面”，词根不同。

entries.definition: to decide something after consideration. It stresses the final boundary set, while resolve stresses the inner firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 经过考虑后决定。它强调最终划定的界限，而 resolve 强调内心的坚定。

entries.definition: to end a disagreement or arrange something finally. It is the everyday word for the result that resolve produces.
entries.definitionCN: 结束分歧或最终安排好某事。它是 resolve 所产生结果的口语化说法。

entries.definition: to mix into a liquid and disappear as a solid. It is the same solvere with dis- 'apart', the chemical branch made explicit.
entries.definitionCN: 溶入液体、作为固体消失。它是同一个 solvere 加 dis-“分开”，把化学分支说得更明白。

entries.definition: to separate threads or solve a complicated matter. It uses a thread image rather than a knot image.
entries.definitionCN: 拆开线，或弄清复杂的事。它用的是线团意象，而不是绳结意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations based on the real Latin image of loosening a knot, plus real derivatives and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 基于拉丁语“松开绳结”这一真实意象的正常联想，再加上真实派生词与搭配。

normal.en: re- 'back' + solvere 'loosen' = loosen back. A doubt is a tight knot; resolving loosens it and the mind settles back.
normal.cn: re-“回”+ solvere“松开”＝往回松开。犹豫是紧结；resolve 把它松开，心思便落回去。

normal.en: Solve is the same root without re-, so solving a puzzle and resolving a dispute are both 'untying'.
normal.cn: solve 是去掉 re- 的同一词根，所以解谜和化解争端都是在“解结”。

normal.en: Dissolve adds dis- 'apart': the bonds are loosened apart until the solid disappears into the liquid.
normal.cn: dissolve 加 dis-“分开”：键被松向两边，直到固体消失在液体里。

normal.en: In music, a dissonant chord is a tightened knot; it resolves into a consonant chord that lies flat.
normal.cn: 音乐里，不协和和弦是拉紧的结；它解决到协和和弦后就平展了。

normal.en: Resolution is the noun for all branches at once: a decision, a settlement, a screen's resolution, or a chemical separation.
normal.cn: resolution 一个名词同时覆盖各分支：决心、解决、屏幕分辨率、化学分离。

abstract.en: See a hand pulling a knot tight, then releasing it: the rope keeps its shape but stops fighting itself. That release is resolve.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把结拉紧，然后松开：绳子保持形状，却不再与自己较劲。这次松开就是 resolve。

abstract.en: The same loosening can happen in the mind (doubt), between people (dispute), inside matter (chemistry), or in a chord (music).
abstract.cn: 同一次松开可以发生在心里（犹豫）、人与人之间（争端）、物质内部（化学）或和弦里（音乐）。

abstract.en: Optical resolution is the same gesture at the smallest scale: loosening two blurred points until they can be held apart.
abstract.cn: 光学分辨率是同一动作的最小尺度版本：把两个糊在一起的点松开，直到能被分开握住。

examples.en: After months of hesitation, he resolved to open his own workshop.
examples.cn: 犹豫了几个月后，他下定决心开自己的工作室。

examples.en: The mediator helped the families resolve the disagreement about the land.
examples.cn: 调解人帮助几家人化解了关于这块土地的争执。

examples.en: The lens resolves the tiny letters that the naked eye cannot see.
examples.cn: 这枚镜头能分辨出肉眼看不见的细小字母。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞草”（re-solve）——瑞草一出现，心里的死结就松开了 → resolve 松开结、下决心、解决问题

root: 拉丁 resolvere：re-“回、再”+ solvere“松开、解开”；solvere 通常上溯至原始印欧语 *se-lu-（*s(w)e-“自己”+ *leu-“松开、切开”）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of resolve all perform one action: a tightened knot is loosened. The knot may be a doubt, a dispute, a compound, a symptom, a chord, or two blurred points of light.
sensesIntro.cn: resolve 的九个义项都在做同一件事：把拉紧的结松开。这个结可以是犹豫、争端、化合物、症状、和弦，或两个模糊的光点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand loosens a tight knot and lets it settle into a fixed shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开拉紧的结，让它落成一个确定的形状。

branches.en: MIND: loosening doubt lets the mind settle on one course; the settled state is the noun resolve.
branches.cn: 心智：松开犹豫让心思落定在一条路上；落定后的状态就是名词 resolve。

branches.en: BETWEEN PEOPLE AND WITHIN THE SELF: a dispute is a knot between two parties, and grief is a knot inside a person; both are loosened.
branches.cn: 人与人、人与自身：争端是两方之间的结，悲痛是人体内的结；两者都被松开。

branches.en: MATTER: analysis and chemical change both loosen a compound until its parts are released.
branches.cn: 物质：分析与化学变化都把复合体松开，直到各部分释放出来。

branches.en: BODY AND SOUND: a symptom unties itself, and a tense chord is released into a resting harmony.
branches.cn: 身体与声音：症状自行解结，紧张的和弦被释放到安定的和声。

branches.en: SIGHT: resolution separates two blurred points, the same loosening at the smallest visible scale.
branches.cn: 视觉：分辨率把两个模糊的点分开，是同一动作在最小可见尺度上的版本。

intro.en: Resolve is built from the prefix re- plus the Latin verb solvere. English adds productive suffixes to make nouns, adjectives and negations, all of which keep the 'loosen' core.
intro.cn: resolve 由前缀 re- 加拉丁动词 solvere 构成。英语再叠加能产的后缀，造出名词、形容词和否定形式，这些都保留“松开”的核心。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on solvere 'to loosen': solutio gives solution, resolvere gives resolve, and the participle resolutus gives resolute.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 solvere“松开”上：solutio 给出 solution，resolvere 给出 resolve，分词 resolutus 给出 resolute。

items.meaning: a decision, a settlement, or the clarity of an image
items.meaningCN: 决议；解决；分辨率（-tion 构成行为名词）
items.example: The committee passed a resolution to ban single-use plastics.
items.exampleCN: 委员会通过了一项禁止一次性塑料的决议。

items.structure: Latin resolutus (past participle) used as an adjective
items.meaning: firm and determined, not easily moved
items.meaningCN: 坚决的；果断的（拉丁分词转为形容词）
items.example: She remained resolute despite the criticism.
items.exampleCN: 尽管受到批评，她依然坚决。

items.meaning: able to be solved or separated
items.meaningCN: 可解决的；可分解的（-able 表示“能被……”）
items.example: The conflict is resolvable if both sides listen.
items.exampleCN: 只要双方肯听，这场冲突是可以解决的。

items.meaning: not yet settled or solved
items.meaningCN: 未解决的；未决定的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Several questions remain unresolved.
items.exampleCN: 还有几个问题没有解决。

items.meaning: hesitating, unable to decide
items.meaningCN: 犹豫不决的（ir- 为 in- 在 r 前的变体）
items.example: He was irresolute and missed the chance.
items.exampleCN: 他犹豫不决，错过了机会。

items.meaning: to break up and mix into a liquid
items.meaningCN: 溶解；解散（dis- 表示“分开”）
items.example: Stir until the sugar dissolves in the water.
items.exampleCN: 搅拌到糖在水中溶解。

items.meaning: an answer to a problem, or a liquid mixture
items.meaningCN: 解决办法；溶液（“被松开的结果”）
items.example: They found a simple solution to the noise problem.
items.exampleCN: 他们找到了解决噪音问题的简单办法。

items.meaning: a person or system that solves problems
items.meaningCN: 解决者；求解器（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: The software includes an equation solver.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件带有方程求解器。

items.meaning: the quality of being firmly determined
items.meaningCN: 坚决；果断（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Her resoluteness impressed the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 她的坚决给整个团队留下深刻印象。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb: se- (self) + luere (loosen), commonly analysed as 'to loosen, untie, dissolve'
latinEntries.meaning: to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay a debt
latinEntries.meaningCN: 松开、解开、溶解、清偿（拉丁动词）

latinEntries.meaning: to loosen back, untie again, dissolve
latinEntries.meaningCN: 往回松开、再解开、溶解（resolve 的直接来源）

latinEntries.meaning: loosened, untied; hence settled and determined
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被松开的、被解开的；引申为已定下的、坚定的

latinEntries.meaning: a loosening, a solution, a payment
latinEntries.meaningCN: 松开、解答、清偿（solution 的拉丁源头）

definition_zh: 资源；物力财力；机智；可求助之物；应急办法；计算机资源
definition_en: a supply of something useful that can be drawn on when needed, or the ability to find a way through difficulty
core_image: 退去后又再涌起的泉眼：需要时能重新升上来供人取用
scene: The island community treats the coral reef as its most precious resource and sets strict rules on who may harvest from it.
sceneCN: 这里 resource 是「自然资源」（第 1 个义项：自然界可供利用的物资）；句意：岛上社区把珊瑚礁视为最珍贵的资源，并严格规定谁可以从中采捕。图中可辨识物件：珊瑚礁、渔船、海面、社区公告牌、采捕工具。

pos.zh: 资源；物力；财力；机智；应急办法；计算机资源
向……提供资源（技术用语，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 足智多谋的；善于应变的

senses.title: Natural resources: useful things taken from the earth
senses.titleCN: 自然资源：取自自然的有用之物
senses.definition: materials or energy found in nature, such as water, minerals, forests, fish or sunlight, that people can use
senses.definitionCN: 自然界中存在、可供人利用的物质或能量，如水、矿物、森林、鱼群或阳光
senses.example: The region is rich in natural resources but short of fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区自然资源丰富，却缺少淡水。
senses.why: Re- means 'again' and surgere means 'to rise'. A resource is something that rises up again when you draw on it, like a spring that refills after being used.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示“再”，surgere 表示“升起”。资源就是被取用之后还能再升上来的东西，像一口用过后又会重新蓄满的泉。

senses.title: Money, supplies and equipment
senses.titleCN: 财力、物资与设备
senses.definition: money, materials, staff or equipment that can be used to carry out an activity
senses.definitionCN: 可用于开展某项活动的钱、材料、人员或设备
senses.example: The school lacks the resources to buy new computers.
senses.exampleCN: 学校缺少购买新电脑的资金。
senses.why: The spring image is applied to money and goods: they are the stored supply that can be drawn up again and again to keep work going.
senses.whyCN: 泉水的意象被用到钱和物上：它们是被储存起来的供给，可以一次次再取上来维持工作。

senses.title: Personal resource: initiative and ingenuity
senses.titleCN: 个人资源：机智与应变
senses.definition: the ability to deal with a difficult situation by finding your own way, often shown in the phrase a man or woman of resource
senses.definitionCN: 靠自己想办法应对困境的能力，常见于 a man/woman of resource 这一说法
senses.example: With no map and no radio, she relied on her own resource.
senses.exampleCN: 没有地图也没有无线电，她只能靠自己的机智。
senses.why: The supply is now inside a person: the mind keeps rising again with new plans, so resource comes to mean inner reserve rather than outer material.
senses.whyCN: 供给现在被放进人身上：心智不断重新涌出新的办法，于是 resource 从外在物资转指内在的储备。

senses.title: A person or thing you can turn to
senses.titleCN: 可求助的人或物
senses.definition: a person, book, website or other thing that gives you help or information when you need it
senses.definitionCN: 在你需要时提供帮助或信息的人、书、网站或其他事物
senses.example: The old librarian is a wonderful resource for local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老图书管理员是了解本地历史的极好资源。
senses.why: Something you draw on repeatedly is a resource. A helpful person is a living spring you can return to whenever a question rises.
senses.whyCN: 能反复取用的东西就是 resource。一个愿意帮忙的人，就是一口你随时可以回去打水的活泉。

senses.title: Computing: a usable file, device or service
senses.titleCN: 计算机资源：可调用的文件、设备或服务
senses.definition: a file, device, memory area, network address or service that a computer program can use
senses.definitionCN: 计算机程序可以使用的文件、设备、内存区域、网络地址或服务
senses.example: The program crashed because it could not open the network resource.
senses.exampleCN: 程序因为无法打开网络资源而崩溃。
senses.why: The 'supply that rises when needed' becomes a pool of memory, disk or bandwidth that the system draws on during a task.
senses.whyCN: “需要时升上来的供给”变成了内存、磁盘或带宽的资源池，系统在任务中随时从中取用。

senses.title: Allocation: who gets which share
senses.titleCN: 资源分配：谁分到多少
senses.definition: the act of supplying and distributing resources among people, projects or departments
senses.definitionCN: 在人员、项目或部门之间提供并分配资源的行为
senses.example: Resource allocation was the main argument at the budget meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 资源分配是预算会上争论的主要问题。
senses.why: Once a spring serves many fields, someone must decide how much water each field may draw; allocation is the rule for dividing that rising supply.
senses.whyCN: 当一口泉要供许多块田时，总得有人决定每块田能取多少水；分配就是划分这股再涌之水的规则。

senses.title: Last expedient: the only thing left to try
senses.titleCN: 最后的应急办法
senses.definition: in formal or older use, a means of escape or a course of action used when nothing else is available
senses.definitionCN: 正式或较早用法中，别无他法时采用的脱身之计或行动方案
senses.example: With the roads closed, a boat was his only resource.
senses.exampleCN: 道路封闭后，一条船成了他唯一的办法。
senses.why: When every stored supply is gone, the mind must still make one more thing rise up. That final rising is the resource of last resort.
senses.whyCN: 当所有储备都用尽，心智仍得再让一样东西升起来。这最后一次“升起”，就是最后的办法。

senses.title: Verb: supply with resources
senses.titleCN: 动词：向……提供资源
senses.definition: to provide a person, project or organization with money, staff or equipment; used mainly in technical or management writing
senses.definitionCN: 向个人、项目或组织提供资金、人员或设备；主要用于技术或管理文本
senses.example: The lab was resourced with new instruments and two technicians.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室获得了新仪器和两名技术员的资源配备。
senses.why: To resource something is to put a supply behind it, so that help can rise up whenever the work needs it. The verb keeps the spring image intact.
senses.whyCN: 给某事 resource，就是在其背后放上一份供给，让工作在需要时随时有东西升上来支援。这个动词完整保留了泉水的意象。

intro.en: Resource began as a word for 'a means of getting out of difficulty' and grew into the modern sense of supplies and wealth. It comes through French from Latin resurgere, 'to rise again'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resource 最初指“摆脱困境的手段”，后来发展为“物资、财富”的现代义。它经由法语来自拉丁 resurgere“再升起”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in the 1610s as 'a means of supplying a want; an expedient'. The emphasis was on something you could turn to in difficulty, not on wealth.
items.cn: 最早于 17 世纪 10 年代记录，意为“满足需要的办法；应急手段”。重点是在困境中可求助之物，而不是财富。

items.en: Borrowed from French resourse, from Old French resourdre 'to rise again, recover, spring up again'.
items.cn: 借自法语 resourse，源自古法语 resourdre“再升起、恢复、重新涌起”。

items.en: Latin resurgere is re- 'again' + surgere 'to rise'. Surgere is generally analysed as sub- 'from below' + regere 'to guide, direct', so the picture is something rising up from below.
items.cn: 拉丁 resurgere = re-“再”+ surgere“升起”。surgere 一般分析为 sub-“从下方”+ regere“引导、指挥”，画面是某物从下方升上来。

items.en: The modern sense of natural resources and national wealth develops in the 18th and 19th centuries, when land, coal, water and forests are counted as supplies a country can draw on.
items.cn: “自然资源、国家财富”的现代义在 18、19 世纪发展起来，此时土地、煤炭、水与森林被算作一国可动用的储备。

items.en: Computing extends the word to memory, disk space and network services in the mid-20th century, and human resources becomes a standard term for staff.
items.cn: 20 世纪中期，计算机领域把该词扩展到内存、磁盘空间和网络服务；human resources 也成为指称员工的标准术语。

items.en: Modern English uses resource for materials, money, personal ingenuity and allocation. The rare verb resource, 'to supply with resources', is 20th-century management vocabulary.
items.cn: 现代英语用 resource 指物资、金钱、个人机智与分配。罕用的动词 resource“向……提供资源”是 20 世纪的管理词汇。

note.en: The first group separates true spelling neighbours from words of the same family; the second group compares words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分真正的形近词与同族词；第二组比较意思上有重叠的词。

entries.definition: the place where something begins or comes from. It shares Latin surgere 'to rise' with resource, but has no re- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 事物开始或来源之处。它与 resource 共享拉丁 surgere“升起”，但没有 re- 前缀。

entries.definition: the act of turning to someone or something for help. It looks close but comes from Latin recurrere 'to run back', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 向某人某物求助的行为。它形近，却来自拉丁 recurrere“跑回去”，词根不同。

entries.definition: rising again after a period of decline. It shows the bare re- + surgere image that resource also contains.
entries.definitionCN: 衰落之后再度兴起的。它直接呈现 resource 同样含有的 re- + surgere 意象。

entries.definition: something valuable that a person or company owns. It is countable property, while resource stresses what can be drawn on.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的有价值之物。它强调可计数的财产，而 resource 强调可动用的供给。

entries.definition: a supply kept for future use. It emphasizes storage, while resource emphasizes availability when needed.
entries.definitionCN: 留待将来使用的储备。它强调储存，而 resource 强调需要时可取用。

entries.definition: a quick practical way of dealing with a problem, often not ideal. It matches the older 'resource in difficulty' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 应付问题的快速实用办法，常不理想。它对应 resource 较早的“困境中的手段”义。

entries.definition: money used to start or run a business. It is one kind of resource, narrowed to finance.
entries.definitionCN: 用于开办或经营企业的资金。它是资源的一种，范围收窄到财务。

entries.definition: the money or equipment needed for a purpose. It is informal and usually financial, while resource is broader.
entries.definitionCN: 达成目的所需的钱或设备。它偏口语且多指财力，而 resource 范围更广。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real Latin image of a spring rising again, plus real compounds and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 基于拉丁语“泉水再涌起”这一真实意象的正常联想，加上真实复合词与搭配。

normal.en: re- 'again' + surgere 'rise': a resource is a supply that rises again when you draw on it.
normal.cn: re-“再”+ surgere“升起”：resource 就是取用后还能再升上来的供给。

normal.en: Source is the same root without re-: the place something rises from. Resource adds the idea of rising again and again.
normal.cn: source 是去掉 re- 的同一词根，指事物升起的来源；resource 多了“一次次再升起”的意思。

normal.en: Human resources treats people as a supply the organization draws on; natural resources treats land, water and minerals that way.
normal.cn: human resources 把人当作组织可动用的供给；natural resources 把土地、水和矿产同样看待。

normal.en: A resourceful person carries the spring inside: new plans keep rising when the old ones fail.
normal.cn: resourceful 的人把泉眼带在身上：旧办法失效时，新办法会不断涌出。

normal.en: In computing, resource is the pool of memory, disk and bandwidth a program draws from while it runs.
normal.cn: 计算机里的 resource 是程序运行时从中取用的内存、磁盘与带宽池。

abstract.en: Picture a dry field beside a spring: every time the farmer draws water, the spring fills again. That refilling is the core of resource.
abstract.cn: 想象一块干田旁有一口泉：农夫每次取水，泉眼又会重新蓄满。这次“重新蓄满”就是 resource 的核心。

abstract.en: The spring can be outside you (land, money) or inside you (ingenuity); the gesture of drawing on a supply is the same.
abstract.cn: 泉可以在你身外（土地、金钱），也可以在你身内（机智）；从中取用供给的动作是一样的。

abstract.en: Allocation is deciding how to divide one spring among many fields; scarcity is what makes that decision hard.
abstract.cn: 分配就是决定一口泉如何分给许多块田；稀缺才让这个决定变得困难。

examples.en: Fresh water is the resource that the whole valley depends on.
examples.cn: 淡水是整个山谷赖以生存的资源。

examples.en: The village school has few resources but very committed teachers.
examples.cn: 这所乡村学校资源很少，但老师们非常投入。

examples.en: She is a resource for anyone trying to learn the local dialect.
examples.cn: 对任何想学当地方言的人来说，她都是可以求助的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞索斯”——瑞索斯岛的泉水退去又再涌起，怎么取都用不完，成了岛上最重要的资源 → resource 资源、办法

root: 拉丁 resurgere：re-“再”+ surgere“升起”（surgere 一般分析为 sub-“从下方”+ regere“引导”），核心是“再次升上来的供给”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of resource all draw on one picture: a spring that rises again whenever someone needs it. What rises may be water, money, memory, a helpful person or a last idea.
sensesIntro.cn: resource 的八个义项都取用同一个画面：一口在有人需要时就会再涌起的泉。涌上来的可以是水、钱、内存、一位肯帮忙的人，或最后一个主意。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring refills itself after being drawn from.
core.cn: 核心意象：一口被取用之后又会重新蓄满的泉。

branches.en: MATERIAL SUPPLY: water, minerals, money and equipment are the stored water of the spring.
branches.cn: 物质供给：水、矿产、金钱与设备就是泉里储存的水。

branches.en: HUMAN SUPPLY: ingenuity rises inside a person, and a helpful person is a living spring others return to.
branches.cn: 人的供给：机智在人心里涌出，肯帮忙的人则是他人会一再回来的活泉。

branches.en: SYSTEM SUPPLY: a computer draws on memory and bandwidth, and allocation decides each task's share of that pool.
branches.cn: 系统供给：计算机取用内存与带宽，分配则决定每个任务从池中分到多少。

branches.en: SCARCITY: when the stored supply is gone, the mind must make one more thing rise.
branches.cn: 稀缺：储备耗尽时，心智必须再让一样东西升起来。

branches.en: SUPPLYING: the verb puts a supply behind a project so that help can rise when needed.
branches.cn: 供给动作：动词形式在项目背后放上一份供给，让援助需要时能升上来。

intro.en: Resource takes the productive suffix -ful and -ness, and combines freely in compounds such as resource-rich and under-resourced. The prefix re- belongs to the Latin base, not to English word formation.
intro.cn: resource 可加能产后缀 -ful、-ness，也能自由构成 resource-rich、under-resourced 这类复合词。前缀 re- 属于拉丁词基，不是英语构词成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on surgere 'to rise': resurgere gives resource and resurgent, while the bare surgere also gives source and surge.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 surgere“升起”上：resurgere 给出 resource 与 resurgent，纯 surgere 还给出 source 与 surge。

items.meaning: good at finding ways to deal with problems
items.meaningCN: 足智多谋的；善于应变的（-ful 表示“充满”）
items.example: A resourceful guide found dry wood in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 一位机敏的向导在雨中找到了干柴。

items.meaning: the quality of finding practical solutions
items.meaningCN: 机智；应变能力（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Her resourcefulness saved the expedition.
items.exampleCN: 她的机智救了这次探险。

items.meaning: the act of supplying money, staff or equipment
items.meaningCN: 资源配备（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: The resourcing of rural clinics remains a challenge.
items.exampleCN: 乡村诊所的资源配备仍是一项挑战。

items.meaning: given too little money, staff or equipment
items.meaningCN: 资源不足的（under- 表示“不足”）
items.example: Many schools in the area are under-resourced.
items.exampleCN: 该地区许多学校资源不足。

items.meaning: given more money or staff than is needed
items.meaningCN: 资源过剩的（over- 表示“过度”）
items.example: The project was over-resourced and finished early.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目资源过剩，提前完成了。

items.meaning: having plenty of natural resources
items.meaningCN: 资源丰富的（复合形容词）
items.example: Resource-rich countries often depend on exports.
items.exampleCN: 资源丰富的国家常常依赖出口。

items.meaning: having very few natural resources
items.meaningCN: 资源贫乏的（复合形容词）
items.example: The island is resource-poor but strategically important.
items.exampleCN: 这座岛资源贫乏，但战略位置重要。

items.meaning: needing a lot of energy, money or materials
items.meaningCN: 资源密集的；耗费大量资源的（复合形容词）
items.example: Desalination is an energy-intensive, resource-intensive process.
items.exampleCN: 海水淡化是一个能耗高、资源密集的工艺。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb: sub- (from below) + regere (to guide, direct)
latinEntries.meaning: to rise, spring up, get up
latinEntries.meaningCN: 升起、涌起、起身（拉丁动词）
再升起、恢复（resource 的直接来源）
再度兴起的；复苏的（同根形容词）

definition_zh: 回答；回复；作出反应；响应；应和
definition_en: to answer someone, or to react to something that happens, is said or is done
core_image: 把收到的话重新递回去：像把一枚承诺掷回投来的人手里
scene: When the alarm sounded, the night nurse responded within seconds and ran to the ward.
sceneCN: 这里 respond 是「响应、出动」（第 5 个义项：对紧急情况作出响应）；句意：警报响起时，夜班护士几秒内就作出响应，跑向病房。图中可辨识物件：警报灯、护士站、走廊、病房门、跑动的护士。

pos.zh: 回答；回复；反应；响应；应和

derivatives.zh: 回答者；调查对象；答辩人
反应灵敏的；积极回应的

senses.title: Answer in speech
senses.titleCN: 口头回答
senses.definition: to answer someone directly in speech, especially after they have spoken to you
senses.definitionCN: 在对方说话之后，直接用言语回答对方
senses.example: When I asked where the station was, he responded with a wave of his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 我问车站在哪里时，他挥手作了回答。
senses.why: Re- means 'back' and spondere means 'to promise, pledge'. A spoken answer is a word handed back to the speaker, as if returning the pledge that was offered.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示“回”，spondere 表示“承诺、立誓”。口头回答就是把话递回说话人手里，像是把对方递来的承诺还回去。

senses.title: Reply in writing
senses.titleCN: 书面回复
senses.definition: to answer a letter, email or message in writing, especially in a formal context
senses.definitionCN: 以书面形式回答信件、邮件或讯息，尤指正式场合
senses.example: The bank responded to my complaint within two days.
senses.exampleCN: 银行两天内就回复了我的投诉。
senses.why: The same 'word given back' now travels on paper. The reply is still a pledge returned, only the medium has changed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“把话递回去”的动作现在落在纸上。回复仍是把承诺送回，只是媒介换了。

senses.title: React to a stimulus or change
senses.titleCN: 对刺激或变化作出反应
senses.definition: to react to something that happens, such as light, heat, a sound or a change in conditions
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的事情作出反应，如光、热、声音或条件变化
senses.example: The leaves respond to the first cold nights by turning red.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子对最初的寒夜作出反应，变成红色。
senses.why: Even without words, a living thing gives something back to what reaches it. The reaction is its 'answer', so the promise-returning image extends to the body.
senses.whyCN: 即使不用语言，生物也会对触及它的东西回敬些什么。这个反应就是它的“回答”，于是“把承诺递回”的意象延伸到身体。

senses.title: Of a patient or illness: improve under treatment
senses.titleCN: 医学上：对治疗有反应、好转
senses.definition: of a patient, tumour or illness, to improve or change as a result of medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 指病人、肿瘤或疾病因治疗而好转或发生变化
senses.example: The infection responded quickly to the antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 感染对抗生素很快有了反应。
senses.why: The drug makes a claim on the body, and the body answers. A good response is the body returning the right pledge; no response means it stays silent.
senses.whyCN: 药物对身体提出一个“要求”，身体则给出“回答”。反应好就是身体回了一个合适的承诺；无反应就是它保持沉默。

senses.title: Act quickly in an emergency
senses.titleCN: 对紧急情况迅速响应出勤
senses.definition: of emergency services or people, to act quickly when called to deal with danger
senses.definitionCN: 指急救部门或人员在接到危险呼叫时迅速行动
senses.example: Fire crews responded to the call in under four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 消防队不到四分钟就响应了呼叫。
senses.why: An alarm is an urgent pledge sent out. To respond is to send back action instead of words, returning the call with your presence.
senses.whyCN: 警报是发出的紧急承诺。respond 就是回以行动而不是言语，用自己的到场把这次呼叫接回去。

senses.title: Answer an appeal, tender or invitation
senses.titleCN: 回应呼吁、招标或邀请
senses.definition: to give a formal answer to an appeal, invitation or tender, often publicly
senses.definitionCN: 对呼吁、邀请或招标作出正式答复，常为公开答复
senses.example: Several firms responded to the government's tender.
senses.exampleCN: 有几家企业响应了政府的招标。
senses.why: A call for help or a tender is a public pledge. Those who respond hand back their own pledge in the form of an offer or an answer.
senses.whyCN: 求助或招标是公开的承诺。回应者以自己的报价或答复，把手里的承诺递回去。

senses.title: Of a building or design: answer its setting
senses.titleCN: 建筑或设计“呼应环境”
senses.definition: of a building, design or artwork, to be shaped in a way that answers the needs of its site, users or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 指建筑、设计或艺术品的形式对场地、使用者或环境的需要作出呼应
senses.example: The facade responds to the changing angle of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙对太阳角度的变化作出呼应。
senses.why: The site makes a silent claim, and the design gives back a shaped answer. Responding here means the form returns what the place asked for.
senses.whyCN: 场地提出一个无声的“要求”，设计则给出一个有形的“回答”。这里的 respond 指形式把场所所求之物回敬过去。

senses.title: Liturgical response in worship
senses.titleCN: 礼拜中的应和
senses.definition: in a church service, to say or sing the set words that answer the leader or congregation
senses.definitionCN: 在教堂礼拜中，念出或唱出回应主礼者或会众的固定词句
senses.example: The congregation responded, 'Amen.'
senses.exampleCN: 会众应和道：“阿们。”
senses.why: The priest's words are a pledge offered to the congregation; the fixed reply is the pledge returned in unison, the clearest surviving example of the original sense.
senses.whyCN: 主礼者的话是向会众发出的承诺；固定答词就是众人齐齐递回的承诺，这是原义保存得最清楚的例子。

senses.title: Take part in a survey by answering
senses.titleCN: 参与调查、作答问卷
senses.definition: to give answers to a questionnaire, interview or research request
senses.definitionCN: 对问卷、访谈或研究请求作出回答
senses.example: Only a third of the households responded to the survey.
senses.exampleCN: 只有三分之一的家庭回答了这份调查。
senses.why: A survey sends out a question like a small pledge; every completed form is a pledge handed back, which is why non-response is treated as silence.
senses.whyCN: 调查发出的问题像一份小小的承诺；每一份填好的问卷都是递回的承诺，所以“未回应”才被视为沉默。

intro.en: Respond is a borrowing of Latin respondere, 'to promise in return'. Its oldest English senses are legal and religious, and the everyday 'answer' sense grew from there. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: respond 借自拉丁 respondere“回以承诺”。它最早的英语义项用于法律与宗教，日常“回答”义由此生长出来。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded around 1300, meaning 'to make a statement in reply', especially in legal and religious settings.
items.cn: 约 1300 年首次记录，意为“作答复陈述”，尤用于法律与宗教场合。

items.en: Borrowed from Old French respondre, which already carried both 'answer' and 'answer for a promise'.
items.cn: 借自古法语 respondre，该词已同时含有“回答”与“为承诺作保”两层意思。

items.en: Latin respondere is re- 'back' + spondere 'to promise, pledge, promise solemnly'. The original picture is giving a pledge back to the person who asked.
items.cn: 拉丁 respondere = re-“回”+ spondere“承诺、立誓、郑重许诺”。最初的画面是把承诺递回给提出要求的人。

items.en: Spondere is traced to PIE *spend- 'to make an offering, perform a rite, vow'. A promise was originally something offered solemnly, like a sacrifice.
items.cn: spondere 上溯至原始印欧语 *spend-“献祭、举行仪式、许愿”。承诺最初是郑重献上的东西，如同祭品。

items.en: The word extends from verbal answers to reactions of the body and of nature, so that plants, patients and materials can 'respond' to light, drugs or stress.
items.cn: 词义从口头回答扩展到身体与自然的反应，于是植物、病人和材料都能对光、药物或压力“作出反应”。

items.en: Modern English adds emergency response, survey response and design response. The noun response and the adjective responsive carry the same 'give back' core.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上应急响应、问卷作答与设计呼应。名词 response 与形容词 responsive 都保留同一个“回递”核心。

note.en: The first group checks form and word family; the second compares verbs that all involve answering or reacting.
note.cn: 第一组检查词形与同族关系；第二组比较都含“回答、反应”之意的动词。

entries.definition: the noun from respond: an answer or a reaction. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: respond 派生的名词：回答或反应。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to match, or to exchange letters. It adds cor- 'together' to spondere, so two things promise each other.
entries.definitionCN: 相符合，或通信。它在 spondere 前加 cor-“共同”，表示两方互相承诺。

entries.definition: a person or firm that pays for an event or supports a proposal. It comes from the same spondere 'pledge' family, not from respond.
entries.definitionCN: 为活动出资或支持提案的个人或公司。它出自同一个 spondere“承诺”词族，而非 respond。

entries.definition: to answer in words. It is the everyday neutral word, while respond is more formal and covers reactions too.
entries.definitionCN: 用言语回答。它是最日常的中性词，而 respond 更正式，且涵盖反应。

entries.definition: to say something back to a question. It is broader in grammar but narrower in range than respond.
entries.definitionCN: 对问题作出言语回应。它语法上更宽，但语义范围比 respond 窄。

entries.definition: to act because something has happened. It stresses the action itself, while respond often implies an answer given back.
entries.definitionCN: 因某事发生而行动。它强调行动本身，而 respond 常含“回递答复”之意。

entries.definition: to answer quickly and sharply. It is a narrowed, emotional kind of response.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而尖锐地反驳。它是 respond 收窄后带情绪的一种。

entries.definition: to show that you have received or noticed something. It confirms receipt rather than giving a full answer.
entries.definitionCN: 表明已收到或注意到某事。它只确认“收到”，并不给出完整答复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real Latin pieces re- 'back' and spondere 'pledge', plus real derivatives.
normalIntro.cn: 基于拉丁语真实成分 re-“回”与 spondere“承诺”的正常联想，加上真实派生词。

normal.en: re- 'back' + spondere 'promise' = promise back. Every answer is a pledge returned to the one who asked.
normal.cn: re-“回”+ spondere“承诺”＝把承诺递回。每个回答都是把承诺还给提问者。

normal.en: Correspond adds cor- 'together': two things or two letters promise each other, which is why it means match or exchange mail.
normal.cn: correspond 加 cor-“共同”：两物或两封信互相承诺，所以它表示“相符”或“通信”。

normal.en: Sponsor and spouse belong to the same pledge family: a sponsor promises support, a spouse is bound by a vow.
normal.cn: sponsor 与 spouse 属于同一个“承诺”词族：sponsor 承诺资助，spouse 由誓言结合。

normal.en: In medicine, a drug asks and the body answers; a tumour that responds is returning the right pledge.
normal.cn: 医学里，药物提出要求，身体给出回答；有反应的肿瘤就是回了一个正确的承诺。

normal.en: Emergency response returns action instead of words: the alarm calls, and the crew answers with its presence.
normal.cn: 应急响应回的是行动而不是言语：警报呼叫，队伍用到场来回答。

abstract.en: Picture two people facing each other: one holds out a small stone as a pledge, the other hands back a stone of the same kind. That return is respond.
abstract.cn: 想象两人相对：一人递出一块小石头作承诺，另一人递回一块同样的石头。这次递回就是 respond。

abstract.en: Words are not required. A plant bending to light, a patient improving on a drug, a building facing the sun all hand something back.
abstract.cn: 不一定需要语言。植物向光弯曲、病人因药好转、建筑朝向太阳，都在递回些什么。

abstract.en: The word keeps a courtroom and a church in its memory: an answer given formally, and a congregation answering the leader in unison.
abstract.cn: 这个词的记忆里留着法庭与教堂：正式作出的答辩，以及会众齐声应和主礼者。

examples.en: She responded to the email the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 她当天下午就回复了那封邮件。

examples.en: The seedlings respond to even a small increase in light.
examples.cn: 幼苗对哪怕很小的光照增强也会作出反应。

examples.en: Rescue teams responded within minutes of the landslide.
examples.cn: 山体滑坡发生后几分钟内，救援队就作出了响应。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞斯邦的”——在山谷里喊一声“瑞斯邦的”，对面立刻回话 → respond 回答、回应

root: 拉丁 respondere：re-“回”+ spondere“承诺、立誓”；spondere 上溯至原始印欧语 *spend-“献祭、举行仪式”，核心是“把承诺递回去”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of respond all give something back: a word, a letter, a reaction, a recovery, a rescue, a bid, a shape, a sung Amen, or a filled-in form.
sensesIntro.cn: respond 的九个义项都在“递回”某样东西：一句话、一封信、一个反应、一次好转、一次救援、一份投标、一个形状、一声应和的“阿们”，或一张填好的问卷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pledge is handed back to the one who offered it.
core.cn: 核心意象：把承诺递回给当初递出它的人。

branches.en: WORDS RETURNED: speech and writing are the plainest forms of giving a pledge back.
branches.cn: 递回言语：口头与书面是“把承诺还回去”最朴素的形式。

branches.en: BODY RETURNED: a plant or patient answers light or medicine with a change, a reaction instead of words.
branches.cn: 递回身体反应：植物或病人以变化回应光或药物，用反应代替言语。

branches.en: ACTION RETURNED: alarms and public calls are answered by presence, crews or bids.
branches.cn: 递回行动：警报与公开呼吁由到场、救援队或投标来回答。

branches.en: FORM RETURNED: a design answers its site, and a congregation answers its leader in set words.
branches.cn: 递回形式与仪式：设计回应场地，会众用固定词句应和主礼者。

branches.en: DATA RETURNED: a survey question is answered by a completed form.
branches.cn: 递回数据：调查问题由一份填好的问卷作出回答。

intro.en: Respond takes the noun suffix -se and the adjective suffix -ive, and the negative prefix un- attaches to the derived adjective. The re- belongs to the Latin base.
intro.cn: respond 可加名词后缀 -se 与形容词后缀 -ive，否定前缀 un- 加在派生形容词上。re- 属于拉丁词基。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on spondere 'to pledge': respondere gives respond and response, correspondere gives correspond, and sponsio gives sponsor and spouse.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 spondere“承诺”上：respondere 给出 respond 与 response，correspondere 给出 correspond，sponsio 给出 sponsor 与 spouse。

items.meaning: an answer or a reaction
items.meaningCN: 回答；回应；反应（名词形式）
items.example: Her response to the offer was a polite silence.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份提议的回应是礼貌的沉默。

items.meaning: a person who answers, especially in a survey or a court case
items.meaningCN: 回答者；调查对象；答辩人（-ent 表示施动者）
items.example: Most respondents preferred the shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 多数受访者更喜欢较短的版本。

items.meaning: quick to react or answer
items.meaningCN: 反应灵敏的；积极回应的（-ive 表示倾向）
items.example: The staff were friendly and responsive.
items.exampleCN: 员工友好且回应积极。

items.meaning: the quality of reacting quickly and well
items.meaningCN: 响应性；灵敏度（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Users praised the app's responsiveness.
items.exampleCN: 用户称赞这款应用响应迅速。

items.meaning: a person who responds, or an automatic answering device
items.meaningCN: 回应者；应答器（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: First responders reached the scene at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 急救人员天亮时到达现场。

items.meaning: not reacting or answering
items.meaningCN: 无反应的；不响应的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The patient was unresponsive to the drug.
items.exampleCN: 病人对该药没有反应。

items.meaning: to match, or to exchange letters
items.meaningCN: 相符；通信（cor- 表示“共同”）
items.example: The two accounts do not correspond.
items.exampleCN: 这两份陈述并不相符。

items.meaning: letters exchanged, or a close match
items.meaningCN: 通信；往来信件；相符（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: She kept all the correspondence from that year.
items.exampleCN: 她把那一年的往来信件都留着。

latinEntries.meaning: to answer, to promise in return
latinEntries.meaningCN: 回答；回以承诺（respond 的直接来源）

latinEntries.structure: past participle of respondere, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 回答；答复（response 的拉丁源头）

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb, from PIE *spend- 'make an offering'
latinEntries.meaningCN: 郑重承诺、立誓（这一词族的核心动词）
郑重承诺；担保（sponsor、spouse 的拉丁源头）

definition_zh: 恢复；修复；归还；使复职；复原数据；重建
definition_en: to bring something back to its former place, condition or owner, so that it stands as it did before
core_image: 把倒下的石柱重新立回原来的基座：让它再次站住
scene: Craftsmen spent five years restoring the collapsed cloister to its original form.
sceneCN: 这里 restore 是「修复、复原」（第 1 个义项：使建筑恢复原状）；句意：工匠们花了五年时间，把坍塌的回廊修复成原来的样子。图中可辨识物件：脚手架、石柱、旧图纸、凿子与灰浆桶、修复中的回廊。

pos.zh: 恢复；修复；归还；使复职；复原（数据）

derivatives.zh: 使人恢复健康的；滋补的

senses.title: Bring a building or object back to its former condition
senses.titleCN: 使建筑或物件恢复原状
senses.definition: to repair or rebuild something so that it looks and works as it did in its original state
senses.definitionCN: 修理或重建某物，使其外观与功能回到最初的状态
senses.example: The trust restored the eighteenth-century mill wheel by wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 信托机构一个轮子一个轮子地修复了那座 18 世纪的水磨。
senses.why: Re- means 'again' and the Latin base is tied to *sta- 'to stand'. Restoring a building is making it stand again as it once stood.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示“再”，拉丁词基与 *sta-“站立”相关。修复建筑就是让它像从前那样重新站起来。

senses.title: Give back something lost or taken
senses.titleCN: 归还失物或被取走之物
senses.definition: to return something to the person it belongs to, especially something lost, stolen or taken away
senses.definitionCN: 把属于某人的东西还给他，尤指丢失、被偷或被拿走之物
senses.example: The hiker restored the dropped camera to its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 徒步者把捡到的相机还给了失主。
senses.why: The object had a place in someone's hands. To restore it is to put it back where it stood before it was lost.
senses.whyCN: 这件东西原本在某人手里有个位置。restore 就是把它放回丢失之前所在的位置。

senses.title: Put someone back in a former position
senses.titleCN: 使某人复职、复位
senses.definition: to bring a person back to a job, rank or office they previously held
senses.definitionCN: 让某人回到其先前担任的职位、级别或公职
senses.example: After the inquiry cleared her, the board restored her to the post.
senses.exampleCN: 调查还她清白后，董事会让她恢复了原职。
senses.why: A position is a place where a person stands. To restore someone is to set that person upright in the same slot again.
senses.whyCN: 职位是一个人站立的位子。restore 某人，就是把他重新立回同一个位置上。

senses.title: Bring back health or strength
senses.titleCN: 恢复健康与体力
senses.definition: to make a person healthy, strong or energetic again after illness or exhaustion
senses.definitionCN: 使人在病后或疲惫之后重新变得健康、有力、有精神
senses.example: A week of sleep and good food restored her strength.
senses.exampleCN: 一周的睡眠和好饭菜让她恢复了体力。
senses.why: Illness is a body that has lost its upright stance. To restore is to let the body stand up again on its own feet.
senses.whyCN: 疾病是身体失去了直立的姿态。restore 就是让身体重新靠自己的双脚站起来。

senses.title: Bring back order, calm or confidence
senses.titleCN: 恢复秩序、平静或信心
senses.definition: to make order, calm, trust or confidence exist again after it has been lost
senses.definitionCN: 在秩序、平静、信任或信心失去之后，使其重新存在
senses.example: The head teacher restored calm after the argument in the playground.
senses.exampleCN: 操场上的争吵之后，校长恢复了平静。
senses.why: Order is things standing in their proper places. When a disturbance knocks them over, restoring puts each thing back on its feet.
senses.whyCN: 秩序就是万物各站在其应在的位置。骚动把它们撞倒后，restore 就是把每样东西重新扶正。

senses.title: Computing: copy data back after loss
senses.titleCN: 计算机：把数据还原回去
senses.definition: to copy data, files or a system back to a device after they have been deleted or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 在数据、文件或系统被删除或损坏后，把它们复制回设备
senses.example: She restored the deleted folder from a backup drive.
senses.exampleCN: 她从一个备份盘里还原了被删除的文件夹。
senses.why: Each file had its slot on the disk. Restoring puts the bits back where they stood before the loss, so the system stands complete again.
senses.whyCN: 每个文件在磁盘上都有原本的位置。还原就是把这些数据位放回丢失前的位置，让系统重新完整地“立”起来。

senses.title: Bring back a monarchy or a system
senses.titleCN: 恢复君主制或某种制度
senses.definition: to bring back a ruler, government or social system that had been removed or abolished
senses.definitionCN: 使被废除或推翻的统治者、政府或社会制度重新回来
senses.example: The monarchy was restored in 1660 after eleven years without a king.
senses.exampleCN: 没有国王的十一年之后，君主制于 1660 年恢复。
senses.why: A throne is the most literal standing place. Restoring a monarchy is putting the crown back on the seat where it stood before.
senses.whyCN: 王座是最字面意义上的“站立之处”。恢复君主制，就是把王冠放回它此前所在的座位上。

senses.title: Restore belief or trust
senses.titleCN: 重建信念与信任
senses.definition: to make people believe in someone or something again after doubt or damage
senses.definitionCN: 在怀疑或损害之后，让人们重新相信某人或某事
senses.example: The published accounts restored public trust in the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 公开的账目重建了公众对该基金的信任。
senses.why: Trust is something that stands between people. Once it is knocked down, restoring means setting that standing relation upright again.
senses.whyCN: 信任是立在人与人之间的一样东西。它一旦被撞倒，restore 就是把这段直立的关系重新扶起来。

senses.title: Put back a missing part so the whole is complete
senses.titleCN: 补回缺失部分，使整体完整
senses.definition: to replace a part that has been removed or lost so that something is complete again
senses.definitionCN: 把被移走或丢失的部分补回去，使某物重新完整
senses.example: The missing panel was restored to the painting after careful cleaning.
senses.exampleCN: 经过仔细清理，缺失的画板被补回了这幅画中。
senses.why: A missing part leaves a gap in the structure. Restoring it is standing that piece back in the empty slot so the whole can bear weight again.
senses.whyCN: 缺失的部分在结构上留下一个空位。restore 就是把这块构件重新立回空槽，让整体重新承重。

intro.en: Restore came through Old French from Latin restaurare, 'to rebuild, renew'. The base -staurare is not an independent common classical verb, and restaurare is the recorded form; its link to *sta- 'to stand' is generally accepted but the deeper detail is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: restore 经由古法语来自拉丁 restaurare“重建、更新”。词基 -staurare 并非古典拉丁中独立的常用动词，restaurare 才是被记录的形式；它与 *sta-“站立”的联系一般被接受，但更深层的细节来源不确定。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded around 1300 as 'to give back, return', and soon also 'to build up again, repair'.
items.cn: 约 1300 年首次记录，意为“归还、送回”，很快又有了“重建、修理”之义。

items.en: Borrowed from Old French restorer, which already meant both 'give back' and 'rebuild, cure'.
items.cn: 借自古法语 restorer，该词已同时表示“归还”与“重建、治愈”。

items.en: Latin restaurare 'to repair, rebuild, renew' is re- 'again' + -staurare. The element -staurare is not attested as a free classical verb; restaurare is the recorded form, and its internal make-up is source uncertain beyond the re- prefix.
items.cn: 拉丁 restaurare“修理、重建、更新”＝re-“再”+ -staurare。其中 -staurare 并未作为独立的古典动词被记录，restaurare 才是记录形式；除 re- 前缀外，其内部构成来源不确定。

items.en: The -staurare element is generally connected with PIE *sta- 'to stand, stand firm', the same base behind stand, state, stable and statue. The picture is something made to stand again.
items.cn: -staurare 这一成分一般与原始印欧语 *sta-“站立、站稳”联系起来，stand、state、stable、statue 也出自同一词基。画面是让某物重新站住。

items.en: By the 17th century restore covers health, order, buildings and thrones. The Restoration in English history specifically names the return of Charles II in 1660.
items.cn: 到 17 世纪，restore 已覆盖健康、秩序、建筑与王位。英国史上的 the Restoration 专指 1660 年查理二世复位。

items.en: Modern English adds restore a backup, restore factory settings and restore a deleted file, applying the same 'put it back where it stood' image to data.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上 restore a backup、restore factory settings、restore a deleted file，把同一个“放回原处”的意象用到数据上。

note.en: The first group separates derived forms from a misleading spelling neighbour; the second compares verbs of putting something back.
note.cn: 第一组把派生形式与一个易误认的形近词分开；第二组比较表示“放回去”的动词。

entries.definition: the act or result of restoring. It is the noun from restore, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 修复或恢复的行为与结果。它是 restore 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: able to bring back health or strength. It is formed from restore and describes a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 能恢复健康或体力的。它由 restore 构成，描述一种性质。

entries.definition: impatient, restless and hard to control. It looks like restore but comes from Old French restif 'stubborn', not from restaurare.
entries.definitionCN: 焦躁的、不安分的、难以驾驭的。它看似 restore，却来自古法语 restif“固执”，并非 restaurare。

entries.definition: to put someone back in a job or position. It narrows restore to the employment sense.
entries.definitionCN: 让某人回到职位上。它把 restore 收窄到任职义。

entries.definition: to give something back or go back. It is the everyday word for the 'give back' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 归还某物，或返回。它是“归还”义的日常用词。

entries.definition: to bring something back to life, use or popularity. It stresses new life, while restore stresses the former state.
entries.definitionCN: 使复活、重新流行。它强调“新生命”，而 restore 强调“原来状态”。

entries.definition: to clean and repair a building or room, often modernizing it. It may change the look rather than return to the original.
entries.definitionCN: 清洁并整修建筑或房间，常作现代化改造。它可能改变外观，而不是回到原貌。

entries.definition: to build something again after it was destroyed. It is limited to physical structures, while restore also covers states and rights.
entries.definitionCN: 在毁坏之后重新建造。它限于实体结构，而 restore 还涵盖状态与权利。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real re- 'again' plus the *sta- 'stand' base, and on real derivatives and collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 基于真实的 re-“再”与 *sta-“站立”词基，加上真实派生词与搭配的正常联想。

normal.en: re- 'again' + a base tied to 'stand': to restore is to make something stand again where it stood.
normal.cn: re-“再”+ 与“站立”相关的词基：restore 就是让某物重新站在它原来的位置。

normal.en: Stand, stable, statue, state and restore share the *sta- base: all point to something holding its place upright.
normal.cn: stand、stable、statue、state、restore 共享 *sta- 词基：都指向某物直立在自己的位置上。

normal.en: The Restoration with a capital R is the return of Charles II in 1660, the most famous English example of restoring a throne.
normal.cn: 大写的 the Restoration 指 1660 年查理二世复位，是英语史上最著名的“恢复王位”例子。

normal.en: Restorative describes food, sleep or medicine that makes the body stand up again.
normal.cn: restorative 形容让人重新站起来的食物、睡眠或药物。

normal.en: In computing, restoring a backup puts every file back in the slot it stood in before it was lost.
normal.cn: 计算机里还原备份，就是把每个文件放回丢失前所在的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a fallen column beside its base: workers lift it and set it upright again. The moment it stands is restore.
abstract.cn: 想象一根倒下的柱子躺在基座旁：工人把它抬起来，重新立正。它站住的那一刻就是 restore。

abstract.en: The 'standing again' image can apply to a building, a person's health, a right, a throne, a file or trust itself.
abstract.cn: “重新站住”这个意象可以用于建筑、人的健康、一项权利、一个王座、一个文件，甚至信任本身。

abstract.en: Restoring is not simply adding something new: it puts a thing back into the exact place and condition it had before.
abstract.cn: restore 并不是简单添新，而是把某物放回它此前确切的位置与状态。

examples.en: Volunteers restored the old station roof before the winter rains.
examples.cn: 志愿者在冬雨来临前修复了老车站的屋顶。

examples.en: The medal was restored to the family after sixty years.
examples.cn: 六十年后，那枚奖章被归还给这个家族。

examples.en: He restored the corrupted database from last night's backup.
examples.cn: 他用昨晚的备份还原了损坏的数据库。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞斯托”——瑞斯托把倒下的石柱一根根扶正，让老房子重新站起来 → restore 恢复、修复

root: 拉丁 restaurare（re-“再”+ -staurare）：-staurare 并非独立的古典常用动词，其内部构成来源不确定，但一般与原始印欧语 *sta-“站立”相联系，核心是“让某物重新站回原位”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of restore share one act: putting something upright again in the place or condition it had before. The thing may be a building, an object, a person, a throne, a file, or trust.
sensesIntro.cn: restore 的九个义项共享同一个动作：把某物重新立回它此前的位置或状态。这个“某物”可以是建筑、物件、人、王座、文件或信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fallen column is lifted back onto its base and stands again.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒下的柱子被抬回基座，重新站住。

branches.en: OBJECTS AND PLACES: a building or a lost object is returned to the exact form or hands it had before.
branches.cn: 物件与场所：建筑或失物回到此前的确切形态或主人手中。

branches.en: STANDING AMONG PEOPLE: a post and a relationship of trust are both places a person stands; restoring sets them upright again.
branches.cn: 人与人之间的站立：职位与信任关系都是人站立的位置；restore 把它们重新扶正。

branches.en: BODY AND ORDER: health is the body standing, and order is things standing in their proper rows.
branches.cn: 身体与秩序：健康是身体站住，秩序是万物站在各自应在的行列里。

branches.en: DATA: every file has a slot on the disk; restoring puts the bits back into that slot.
branches.cn: 数据：每个文件在磁盘上都有槽位；还原就是把数据位放回那个槽。

branches.en: THRONE AND GAP: a crown is returned to its seat, and a missing panel is returned to its empty slot so the whole stands.
branches.cn: 王座与空缺：王冠回到座位，缺失的构件回到空槽，整体才重新站得住。

intro.en: Restore forms nouns with -ation, adjectives with -ative and -able, and accepts the negative prefix un-. Compounds such as restore point extend it into computing.
intro.cn: restore 用 -ation 构成名词，用 -ative、-able 构成形容词，也可加否定前缀 un-。restore point 这类复合词把它带入计算机领域。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on restaurare: restauratio gives restoration, restaurator gives restorer, and instaurare 'set up, establish' is a related recorded verb.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 restaurare 上：restauratio 给出 restoration，restaurator 给出 restorer；instaurare“设立、建立”是相关的记录动词。

items.meaning: the act or result of bringing something back
items.meaningCN: 修复；恢复；复位（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The restoration of the chapel took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 这座小教堂的修复花了十年。

items.meaning: able to bring back health or strength
items.meaningCN: 使人恢复健康的；滋补的（-ative 表示倾向）
items.example: She took a restorative nap after the long flight.
items.exampleCN: 长途飞行后她小睡了一会儿恢复精神。

items.meaning: a person who repairs old buildings, paintings or furniture
items.meaningCN: 修复者；修补者（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: The restorer worked on the fresco for months.
items.exampleCN: 修复师在这幅壁画上工作了好几个月。

items.meaning: having been brought back to a former state
items.meaningCN: 已修复的；已恢复的（-ed 构成过去分词／形容词）
items.example: The restored garden opened to the public.
items.exampleCN: 修复后的花园向公众开放。

items.meaning: able to be brought back or repaired
items.meaningCN: 可恢复的；可修复的（-able 表示“能被……”）
items.example: The wetland is still restorable if the water returns.
items.exampleCN: 如果水回来，这片湿地仍然可以恢复。

items.meaning: not repaired or returned to its original state
items.meaningCN: 未修复的；保持原状的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The unrestored wing still shows the old paint.
items.exampleCN: 未修复的那一翼仍留着旧漆。

items.meaning: a saved system state that can be restored later
items.meaningCN: 还原点（可稍后恢复的系统状态快照，复合名词）
items.example: Create a restore point before installing the update.
items.exampleCN: 安装更新前先创建一个还原点。

items.meaning: a person who wants to bring back an earlier system or style
items.meaningCN: 复辟主义者；复古派（-ist 表示主张者）
items.example: The restorationists wanted the old charter revived.
items.exampleCN: 复古派希望恢复旧宪章。

items.meaning: in a way that brings back strength
items.meaningCN: 以恢复健康的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The week was spent restoratively, with long walks and early nights.
items.exampleCN: 那一周过得很养生，长时间散步、早睡。

latinEntries.structure: re- (again) + -staurare (make to stand; not an independent classical verb)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 重建、修理、更新（restore 的直接来源）
重建、更新（restoration 的拉丁源头）
重建者、修复者（restorer 的拉丁对应）
设立、建立、重新开始（同词基的记录动词）

definition_zh: 限制；限定；约束；管制；使局限
definition_en: to keep something within a limit, or to stop it from spreading beyond a set boundary
core_image: 把绳子往回一拉、收紧：活动范围被收成一个小圈
scene: A red sign on the door says access is restricted to laboratory staff.
sceneCN: 这里 restrict 是「限制进入」（第 1 个义项：限制进入或使用）；句意：门上的红色标牌写着，只有实验室人员才能进入。图中可辨识物件：红色标牌、实验室门、门禁读卡器、白大褂、玻璃窗。

senses.title: Limit who may enter or what may be used
senses.titleCN: 限制进入或使用
senses.definition: to control who is allowed to enter a place or who may use something
senses.definitionCN: 控制谁可以进入某地，或谁可以使用某物
senses.example: Access to the archive is restricted to researchers with a pass.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持通行证的研究人员才能进入档案馆。
senses.why: Re- means 'back' and stringere means 'to draw tight, bind'. A restriction pulls the rope back around a smaller circle, so fewer people stand inside it.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示“往回”，stringere 表示“拉紧、捆住”。限制就是把绳子往回收紧，围出更小的圈，能站在圈里的人就更少。

senses.title: Keep a number or amount below a level
senses.titleCN: 把数量或规模压在一定水平下
senses.definition: to set an upper limit on a number, amount or size
senses.definitionCN: 为数量、金额或规模设定上限
senses.example: The city restricts the number of cars entering the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市限制进入老城的车辆数量。
senses.why: A number that could grow without end is a loose rope. Restricting draws it tight at a chosen point, so the quantity cannot pass that knot.
senses.whyCN: 会无限增长的数量是一根松绳。restrict 在选定的一点把绳拉紧，数量便无法越过这个结。

senses.title: Confine something to a particular range
senses.titleCN: 把……限定在某个范围
senses.definition: to keep something inside a stated area, topic or set, especially in the pattern restrict something to something
senses.definitionCN: 使某物保持在指定的区域、话题或集合内，尤用于 restrict something to something 结构
senses.example: Please restrict your questions to the topic of the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 请把提问限定在讲座主题之内。
senses.why: The rope is tied around one small area and marked with a line. Everything inside the line is allowed; everything outside is kept back.
senses.whyCN: 绳子被系在一个小范围上，并划出一道界线。线内允许，线外一律被拦回去。

senses.title: Limit freedom or rights
senses.titleCN: 限制自由与权利
senses.definition: to limit what a person or group is free to do, say or decide
senses.definitionCN: 限制个人或群体行动、言论或决定的自由
senses.example: The new rules restrict what members may publish online.
senses.exampleCN: 新规限制了成员可在网上发布的内容。
senses.why: Freedom is an open space; restricting winds the rope inward and fences that space, so the person can move only within the tightened loop.
senses.whyCN: 自由是一片开阔地；restrict 把绳子向内收，围起这片地，人只能在收紧的圈内活动。

senses.title: Impose a legal limit on an activity
senses.titleCN: 以法律或法规施加限制
senses.definition: to impose a legal or official limit on an activity, sale or practice
senses.definitionCN: 对某项活动、销售或做法施加法律或官方的限制
senses.example: The law restricts the sale of fireworks to licensed shops.
senses.exampleCN: 法律把烟花销售限制在持证商店。
senses.why: Law is the official hand that pulls the rope. The binding is public and enforced, so the tightened circle becomes a legal boundary.
senses.whyCN: 法律就是那只官方的、拉绳的手。这种捆缚是公开且强制的，收紧的圈便成了法律边界。

senses.title: Limit diet or activity for health reasons
senses.titleCN: 因健康原因限制饮食或活动
senses.definition: to limit what someone eats or does, usually on medical advice
senses.definitionCN: 通常遵医嘱限制某人的饮食或活动
senses.example: The doctor restricted her to light exercise for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 医生限制她一个月内只能做轻度运动。
senses.why: The body's range is drawn in for its own protection: the rope is tightened so that harmful food or strain cannot get through.
senses.whyCN: 身体的活动范围为了保护自己而被收窄：绳子拉紧，让有害的食物或劳损进不来。

senses.title: Hold back growth, trade or development
senses.titleCN: 抑制增长、贸易或发展
senses.definition: to prevent something from growing, expanding or developing at its natural pace
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物按自然速度增长、扩张或发展
senses.example: High tariffs restrict trade between the two countries.
senses.exampleCN: 高关税限制了两国之间的贸易。
senses.why: Growth is a rope being paid out. To restrict is to pull it back, so the line cannot extend as far or as fast as it would.
senses.whyCN: 增长是一根被放出去的绳。restrict 就是把它往回拉，于是这条线伸不了那么远、那么快。

senses.title: Restricted information: limited to certain people
senses.titleCN: 限定知情人：保密级别
senses.definition: of documents or information, officially limited to people with special permission
senses.definitionCN: 指文件或信息被官方限定为只有获特别许可者才能接触
senses.example: The report is marked restricted and stays in the secure room.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告标为受限级，保存在保密室。
senses.why: The rope is pulled tight around a very small group. Those outside cannot reach the content, so restricted becomes the label on the sealed circle.
senses.whyCN: 绳子被收得极紧，圈住极少数人。圈外的人接触不到内容，于是 restricted 成了这个封闭圈上的标签。

intro.en: Restrict came straight from Latin restrictus, the past participle of restringere, 'to bind back tightly'. The cord image is present in every sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: restrict 直接来自拉丁 restrictus，即 restringere“往回紧紧捆住”的过去分词。每一个义项里都留着这条绳子的意象。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in the 1530s as 'to confine, limit'. The word enters English learnedly, directly from the Latin participle rather than through French.
items.cn: 16 世纪 30 年代首次记录，意为“限制、限定”。这个词是学术性地直接借自拉丁分词进入英语的，而不是经由法语。

items.en: Restrictus is the past participle of restringere: re- 'back' + stringere 'to draw tight, bind, compress'. Literally 'bound back'.
items.cn: restrictus 是 restringere 的过去分词：re-“往回”+ stringere“拉紧、捆、压缩”，字面即“被往回捆紧”。

items.en: Stringere is traced to PIE *streng- 'tight, narrow, string'. The same base underlies strict, stringent, strain and strong, all words of tension.
items.cn: stringere 上溯至原始印欧语 *streng-“紧、窄、绳”。同一词基也生出 strict、stringent、strain、strong，都是“张力”之词。

items.en: Early modern English extends the word from physical confinement to rules, rights and trade. 'Restricted' begins to mark places and privileges reserved for some.
items.cn: 近代英语早期把该词从实体圈禁扩展到规则、权利与贸易。restricted 开始标记只留给某些人的场所与特权。

items.en: The 20th century fixes the official sense of restricted documents and restricted areas, and the word becomes common in medicine and economics.
items.cn: 20 世纪固定了 restricted documents（受限文件）与 restricted areas（限制区）的官方义，该词也在医学与经济学中常见。

items.en: Modern English uses restrict for access, numbers, rights, law, health, growth and information. Restriction and restrictive keep the tightened-cord image.
items.cn: 现代英语用 restrict 涵盖进入、数量、权利、法律、健康、增长与信息。restriction 与 restrictive 都保留着“收紧绳索”的意象。

note.en: The first group collects same-root neighbours and one misleading district; the second compares verbs of limiting.
note.cn: 第一组收集同根词，并指出一个易误认的 district；第二组比较表示“限制”的动词。

entries.definition: demanding obedience and exact rules. It is the bare Latin strictus 'drawn tight' without the re- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 要求服从与严格遵守的规则。它是去掉 re- 前缀的纯拉丁 strictus“被拉紧”。

entries.definition: a rule or limit that restricts something. It is the noun from restrict, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 限制某事的规则或界限。它是 restrict 派生的名词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: an administrative area. It looks like restrict but comes from Latin districtus, from distringere 'to draw apart', a different prefix and sense.
entries.definitionCN: 行政区。它看似 restrict，却来自拉丁 districtus，出自动词 distringere“拉开”，前缀和含义都不同。

entries.definition: to keep something below a maximum. It is the neutral general word, while restrict often implies an authority doing the limiting.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不超过上限。它是最中性的通用词，而 restrict 常含“由权威施加”之意。

entries.definition: to keep something inside a space or subject. It stresses the boundary itself more than the tightening.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物限制在某个空间或话题内。它比 restrict 更强调边界本身，而非“收紧”。

entries.definition: to keep something unwanted in check, especially spending or growth. It carries the image of a horse's rein.
entries.definitionCN: 控制不想要的东西，尤指开支或增长。它带的是马缰绳的意象。

entries.definition: to hold someone or something back from acting. It shares stringere but stresses physical holding rather than setting a limit.
entries.definitionCN: 阻止某人某物行动。它与 stringere 同源，但强调身体上的拉住，而非划定限度。

entries.definition: to limit someone's freedom, or to force them to act in a certain way. It often adds pressure and compulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 限制某人的自由，或迫使其按某种方式行动。它常带有压力与强迫。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations built on the real Latin pieces re- 'back' and stringere 'draw tight', plus the real same-root family.
normalIntro.cn: 基于拉丁语真实成分 re-“往回”与 stringere“拉紧”的正常联想，加上真实的同根词族。

normal.en: re- 'back' + stringere 'draw tight' = pull the rope back tight. Every restriction makes the circle smaller.
normal.cn: re-“往回”+ stringere“拉紧”＝把绳往回拉紧。每一次限制都让圈变小。

normal.en: Strict is the same base without re-: a strict rule is simply a tightly drawn line.
normal.cn: strict 是去掉 re- 的同一词基：严格的规则就是一条被拉紧的线。

normal.en: Restrain and constrain share stringere: restrain pulls you back, constrain ties you down.
normal.cn: restrain 与 constrain 共享 stringere：restrain 把你往回拉，constrain 把你捆住。

normal.en: A restricted document is a rope drawn around a very small group, leaving everyone else outside.
normal.cn: restricted document 就是把绳收在极小的圈上，其余人都被留在圈外。

normal.en: Restrict a diet or an exercise plan and the allowed range shrinks to what the body can safely take.
normal.cn: 限制饮食或运动计划，就是把允许范围缩到身体能安全承受的那一小块。

abstract.en: Picture a stake in the ground with a rope tied to it: the more you pull the rope back, the smaller the circle you may walk in. That pull is restrict.
abstract.cn: 想象地上钉着一根桩、系着一根绳：你把绳往回拉得越多，能走的圈就越小。这次往回拉就是 restrict。

abstract.en: The same tightened circle can be drawn around a door, a number, a topic, a right, a law, a diet, an economy or a document.
abstract.cn: 同一个收紧的圈可以围住一扇门、一个数字、一个话题、一项权利、一条法律、一份饮食、一个经济体或一份文件。

abstract.en: Unlike a wall, a restriction is a rope: it is set by someone with authority and can be loosened again by that same authority.
abstract.cn: 限制不是墙，而是绳：它由有权力的人拉紧，也能被同一权力松开。

examples.en: The museum restricts photography in the manuscript room.
examples.cn: 博物馆限制在手稿室拍照。

examples.en: Please restrict your comments to the design itself.
examples.cn: 请把意见限定在设计本身。

examples.en: The new law restricts how much water farms may pump.
examples.cn: 新法律限制了农场可抽取的水量。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞斯吹克特”——瑞斯吹克特把绳子往回一拉，能活动的圈子立刻缩小 → restrict 限制、限定

root: 拉丁 restringere（restringere 的过去分词 restrictus）：re-“往回”+ stringere“拉紧、捆住”；stringere 上溯至原始印欧语 *streng-“紧、窄、绳”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of restrict are eight places where one rope is pulled tight: the door, the number, the topic, the right, the law, the diet, the growth, and the sealed file.
sensesIntro.cn: restrict 的八个义项，就是同一根绳被拉紧的八个地方：门口、数量、话题、权利、法律、饮食、增长，以及那份封存的文件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope is pulled back and the permitted circle shrinks.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子被往回拉紧，允许活动的圈随之缩小。

branches.en: ENTRY AND AMOUNT: the rope is drawn around a door or around a maximum number.
branches.cn: 进入与数量：绳子围在一扇门上，或围在一个数量上限上。

branches.en: CHOSEN RANGE: a topic or a diet is kept inside a marked line drawn for safety or clarity.
branches.cn: 选定范围：话题或饮食被围在一条为清晰或安全而划出的界线内。

branches.en: POWER: freedom and law are the two hands that hold the rope, one private, one official.
branches.cn: 权力：自由与法律是握绳的两只手，一只私人，一只官方。

branches.en: GROWTH: trade and development are a rope being paid out too fast, and restriction pulls it back.
branches.cn: 增长：贸易与发展是一根放得太快的绳，限制把它往回拉。

branches.en: SECRECY: the tightest circle encloses a few cleared people and leaves the document sealed.
branches.cn: 保密：最紧的圈只围住少数获准者，文件被封闭在内。

intro.en: Restrict forms a noun with -ion, adjectives with -ive and -ed, and takes the negative prefix un-. Same-root verbs use con- and dis- with the same strict- base.
intro.cn: restrict 用 -ion 构成名词，用 -ive、-ed 构成形容词，并可加否定前缀 un-。同根动词用 con-、dis- 加同一个 strict- 词基。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on stringere 'to draw tight': restringere gives restrict, strictus gives strict, and constringere gives constrict.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 stringere“拉紧”上：restringere 给出 restrict，strictus 给出 strict，constringere 给出 constrict。

items.meaning: a rule or limit that keeps something within bounds
items.meaningCN: 限制；约束；管制（-ion 构成行为名词）
items.example: Travel restrictions were lifted in June.
items.exampleCN: 旅行限制在六月解除。

items.meaning: limiting what can be done or said
items.meaningCN: 限制性的；约束性的（-ive 表示倾向）
items.example: The club has restrictive membership rules.
items.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部有严格的会员限制规定。

items.meaning: limited, or reserved for certain people
items.meaningCN: 受限制的；限某些人使用的（-ed 构成过去分词／形容词）
items.example: The area is restricted to military traffic.
items.exampleCN: 该区域只限军用车辆通行。

items.meaning: in a way that limits
items.meaningCN: 限制性地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The clause was interpreted restrictively.
items.exampleCN: 这条条款被作了限制性的解释。

items.meaning: the degree to which something limits
items.meaningCN: 限制性；约束程度（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: Critics questioned the restrictiveness of the new code.
items.exampleCN: 批评者质疑新守则的限制程度。

items.meaning: not limited in any way
items.meaningCN: 不受限制的；无约束的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Unrestricted access makes the archive hard to protect.
items.exampleCN: 不受限制的开放让档案馆难以保护。

items.meaning: to squeeze or narrow something
items.meaningCN: 压缩；使收缩（con- 表示“一起”，同根）
items.example: The cold air constricted the blood vessels.
items.exampleCN: 冷空气使血管收缩。

items.meaning: a squeezing or narrowing
items.meaningCN: 收缩；压缩（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The pipes were blocked by a constriction.
items.exampleCN: 管道被一处狭窄处堵住了。

items.meaning: an area marked off for administration
items.meaningCN: 行政区；区域（dis- 表示“分开”，同词基但不同义）
items.example: She works in the business district.
items.exampleCN: 她在商业区工作。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 拉紧、捆住、压缩（这一词族的核心动词）
往回捆紧、限制（restrict 的直接来源）
被往回捆紧的、受限制的（restrict 借入时所取的形式）
被拉紧的、狭窄的、严格的（strict 的拉丁源头）

definition_zh: 保留；保持；留住；记住；聘请（专业人士）
definition_en: to keep something in your possession, keep a quality or fact in place, or secure a person's services by payment
core_image: 合拢的手掌：把东西留在自己手里，不让它滑走
scene: After forty years abroad, he still retained the keys to his childhood home.
sceneCN: 这里 retain 是「保留、留着」（第 1 个义项：继续占有某物）；句意：在国外四十年后，他仍留着童年老宅的钥匙。图中可辨识物件：一串旧钥匙、老宅木门、行李箱、异国的公寓窗。

pos.zh: 保留；保持；留住；记住；聘请

derivatives.zh: 保留；保持；记忆力；（客户、员工）留存
预付聘金；聘用协议；保持者
用于保持的（如 retaining wall 挡土墙）

senses.title: Keep possession: do not let go
senses.titleCN: 继续占有：不放手
senses.definition: to keep something in your possession and continue to have it
senses.definitionCN: 继续占有某物，仍然拥有它
senses.example: The family retained ownership of the land for four generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族四代人都保留着这块地的所有权。
senses.why: Latin re- 'back' plus tenere 'to hold' gives 'hold back'. What you retain is held back from leaving your hand, so possession continues.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 re-“向后”加 tenere“握住”得到“往回握住”。被 retain 的东西被挡在手里、不许离开，因此占有关系持续下去。

senses.title: Keep a quality: it does not fade
senses.titleCN: 保持某种特性：不减退
senses.definition: to continue to have a particular quality, especially after change or use
senses.definitionCN: 继续保有某种特性，尤指经历变化或使用之后
senses.example: The stone walls retain their warmth long after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落很久之后，石墙仍保持着暖意。
senses.why: A quality is held inside the thing itself. If it is retained, the grip is internal: the material keeps what it has instead of giving it off.
senses.whyCN: 特性是被“握”在事物内部的。说它被 retain，意思是这种握持发生在内部：材料把自己拥有的东西留住，而不是释放出去。

senses.title: Keep in the mind: remember
senses.titleCN: 留在脑中：记住
senses.definition: to keep facts or information in your memory
senses.definitionCN: 把事实或信息记在记忆中
senses.example: She can still retain every line of that poem.
senses.exampleCN: 她仍能记住那首诗的每一行。
senses.why: Memory is a mental grip. To retain information is to hold it back from slipping out of the mind, the same gesture as holding an object.
senses.whyCN: 记忆是一种心智上的抓握。retain 信息，就是把它扣在脑中不让它滑出去，和握住一件物品是同一个动作。

senses.title: Keep control or power
senses.titleCN: 保持控制或权力
senses.definition: to keep a position of control, influence, or responsibility
senses.definitionCN: 保住控制地位、影响力或责任
senses.example: The party retained control of the council after the election.
senses.exampleCN: 选举后，该党仍保住了对议会的控制。
senses.why: Power is a grip on institutions and people. Retaining it means the hand does not open, so the hold on the structure continues.
senses.whyCN: 权力是对机构和人的一种抓握。retain 权力意味着这只手不松开，所以对结构的掌控延续下去。

senses.title: Employ a professional: keep their service on call
senses.titleCN: 聘请专业人士：把其服务留在手边
senses.definition: to engage a lawyer, consultant, or other professional by paying for their services
senses.definitionCN: 通过付费聘请律师、顾问等专业人士为自己服务
senses.example: They retained a lawyer to review the contract before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前，他们聘请了一位律师审阅合同。
senses.why: In this branch the thing held is not an object but a person's time. Paying a retainer keeps that time reserved for you, as if held in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这一支里被握住的不是物件，而是人的时间。支付聘金就是把那段时间为你保留下来，仿佛握在你手中。

senses.title: Hold heat or moisture inside
senses.titleCN: 把热量或水分留在内部
senses.definition: to hold heat, water, or moisture inside a material instead of letting it escape
senses.definitionCN: 把热量、水或湿气留在材料内部，不让它逸出
senses.example: A thick wool coat retains body heat in cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 厚羊毛外套在寒风中能保住体温。
senses.why: Here the clenched hand becomes a wall or a lid. The material closes around heat and moisture, so nothing drains away.
senses.whyCN: 这里合拢的手变成了一堵墙或一个盖子。材料把热量和水分围在里面，因此什么都不会流走。

senses.title: Keep money back: deposit, fee, retention
senses.titleCN: 扣留款项：押金、费用、保留金
senses.definition: to keep part of a payment or deposit rather than returning it, often as security
senses.definitionCN: 不退还而扣留部分款项或押金，通常作为担保
senses.example: The landlord may retain part of the deposit for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 房东可以扣留部分押金用于维修。
senses.why: Money is held back from the return trip to the payer. The re- in retain is visible here: what was going back is pulled back into the holder's hand.
senses.whyCN: 钱本来要“回”到付款人手里，却被半路扣下。这里的 re- 最明显：本要返回之物被拉回持有者手中。

senses.title: Retainer: a fee that reserves a service
senses.titleCN: 聘金／保留费：把服务预留给你
senses.definition: a sum paid in advance to reserve a professional's availability, or the agreement that sets it up
senses.definitionCN: 为预留专业人士的服务时间而预付的一笔钱，或设立这种安排的协议
senses.example: The firm charges a monthly retainer for ongoing advice.
senses.exampleCN: 该事务所按月收取聘金，提供持续咨询。
senses.why: This is the hire sense turned into a noun. The fee is the physical grip that keeps the professional's time from being taken by someone else.
senses.whyCN: 这是“聘请”义的名词化。聘金就是那只实际抓住对方时间的“手”，使它不被别人拿走。

senses.title: Do not lose them: customers, staff, readers
senses.titleCN: 不让流失：留住客户、员工、读者
senses.definition: to keep people or things from leaving, especially customers, employees, or users
senses.definitionCN: 使人或物不离开，尤指客户、员工或用户
senses.example: Good design helps the app retain users after the first week.
senses.exampleCN: 好的设计能帮这款应用在头一周之后留住用户。
senses.why: People can leave, and the hand can still close around them. Retention is the same hold applied to loyalty rather than to an object.
senses.whyCN: 人会离开，而这只手仍能合拢。客户留存（retention）就是把同一种握持用在忠诚度上，而不是用在物件上。

intro.en: Retain came into English from French in the late 14c. and goes back to Latin tenere 'to hold'. The dates are approximate; the link to PIE *ten- 'to stretch, hold' is generally accepted.
intro.cn: retain 于 14 世纪晚期经法语进入英语，可上溯到拉丁语 tenere“握住”。年代为大致估计；与原始印欧语 *ten-“拉伸、持握”的联系为一般接受的说法。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'to keep, continue to hold; keep in mind', borrowed through Anglo-French from Old French retenir.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录为“保有、继续握有；记在心里”，经盎格鲁-法语借自古法语 retenir。

items.en: Old French retenir meant 'to keep, hold back; keep in memory; engage a servant or counsel'. Its meanings already covered objects, memory and hired service.
items.cn: 古法语 retenir 意为“保留、扣住；记住；雇用仆人或法律顾问”。它的义项已经覆盖物件、记忆和受雇服务。

items.en: From Latin retinere 'to hold back, keep, detain', built from re- 'back' and tenere 'to hold, grasp'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 retinere“扣住、保留、留住”，由 re-“向后”与 tenere“握住、抓取”构成。

items.en: Tenere 'to hold' is generally traced to PIE *ten- 'to stretch, hold', the same root family as contain, maintain, sustain and tenant. The exact semantic step from 'stretch' to 'hold' is not certain in detail.
items.cn: tenere“握住”一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *ten-“拉伸、持握”，与 contain、maintain、sustain、tenant 同属一个词根家族。“拉伸”到“握住”的具体语义步骤细节并不确定。

items.en: By the 15c. the noun retainer was used for a fee paid to secure a lawyer's or servant's service, and retention for the act of keeping. The legal and financial branch grew out of the same 'hold' image.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，名词 retainer 已指为取得律师或仆人的服务而支付的费用，retention 指“保留”的行为。法律与财务这一支同样生长自“握住”的意象。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense (retain heat, retain water), the mental sense (retain information) and the commercial sense (retain customers, retain staff). It is more formal than keep.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物理义（保温、保水）、心智义（记住信息）和商业义（留住客户、留住员工）。它比 keep 更正式。

note.en: The first group contains words that look or sound like retain; the second contains words that are close in meaning. Check form first, then sense.
note.cn: 第一组是与 retain 形音相近的词；第二组是意思接近的词。先辨词形，再辨词义。

entries.definition: the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. Its ret- comes from Latin rete 'net', not from tenere 'hold'.
entries.definitionCN: 视网膜，眼球后部的感光层。它的 ret- 来自拉丁语 rete“网”，与 tenere“握住”无关。

entries.definition: a group of attendants travelling with an important person. It comes from Old French retenue, a noun from retenir, so it is a distant relative but not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 随行人员；随从。它来自古法语 retenue，是 retenir 的名词形式，因此是远亲，但不是同义词。

entries.definition: to keep someone in official custody or make them wait. It is de- 'away' plus tenere 'hold', the same root with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 拘留；耽搁。它是 de-“离开”加 tenere“握住”，词根相同而前缀不同。

entries.definition: the everyday verb for continuing to have something. It is broader and less formal than retain, which often implies keeping something against a tendency to lose it.
entries.definitionCN: 继续拥有某物的日常动词。它比 retain 更宽、更口语；retain 常暗示顶住“失去”的趋势而保住。

entries.definition: to keep something in its original or good condition over time. It stresses protection from damage rather than mere possession.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物长期保持原状或良好状态。它强调防止损坏，而不只是占有。
