entries.definition: to keep something at the same level or in good repair. It is about continuity of a standard, not holding an object.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物保持在同一水平或处于良好维修状态。它关注标准的延续，而不是握住物件。

entries.definition: to have something in your hand or arms. It is the literal grip that retain only uses as a metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或手臂拿着。它是字面上的抓握，而 retain 只把这种抓握当作比喻。

entries.definition: to refuse to give something that someone expects. It focuses on the refusal, while retain focuses on keeping.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝给某人应得之物。它聚焦于“拒绝”，而 retain 聚焦于“留下”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real parts re- and tenere, real phrases, and real relatives such as contain and tenant.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词成分 re- 与 tenere、真实短语，以及 contain、tenant 等真实同族词。

normal.en: re- 'back' + tenere 'hold' = hold back. Retain is literally 'keep it from going back out of your hand'.
normal.cn: re-“向后”+ tenere“握住”= 往回握住。retain 字面就是“挡住它、不让它从手里出去”。

normal.en: The -tain family all means some kind of holding: contain (hold together), detain (hold away), maintain (hold by the hand), sustain (hold from below), tenant (one who holds land).
normal.cn: -tain 家族都表示某种“握住”：contain（握在一起）、detain（扣住带走）、maintain（用手扶住）、sustain（从下面托住）、tenant（持有土地的人）。

normal.en: Retain is the formal verb for keep: retain documents, retain staff, retain control. Keep is what you say at home; retain is what a contract says.
normal.cn: retain 是 keep 的正式版本：retain documents、retain staff、retain control。keep 是家里说的话，retain 是合同里说的话。

normal.en: A retainer is money that holds a lawyer's time for you, exactly as a hand holds an object.
normal.cn: retainer 是把律师的时间为你“握住”的钱，和手握住物件一模一样。

normal.en: Retention rates in business, memory retention in psychology and heat retention in physics all use the same idea: what is held does not escape.
normal.cn: 商业里的留存率、心理学里的记忆保持、物理里的保温，用的都是同一个想法：被握住的东西不会跑掉。

abstract.en: Picture a fist closing around a coin. The coin is still there because the fingers never opened; that is retain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头合拢，握住一枚硬币。硬币还在，因为手指从未张开——这就是 retain。

abstract.en: The same closed fist can hold a fact, a position of power, a lawyer's time, or the heat inside a brick wall.
abstract.cn: 同一只合拢的手可以握住一个事实、一个权力位置、一位律师的时间，或砖墙里的热量。

abstract.en: The opposite picture is an open palm: what leaves it is lost, so retention is measured by what did not slip away.
abstract.cn: 相反的图景是摊开的手掌：离开它的东西就丢了，所以“留存”衡量的正是没有滑走的部分。

examples.en: The museum retained the original wooden floor during the renovation.
examples.cn: 翻修期间，博物馆保留了原有的木地板。

examples.en: Older adults often retain vocabulary better than they retain names.
examples.cn: 年长者对词汇的保持往往比对姓名的保持更好。

examples.en: The company retained a consultant to redesign its payment system.
examples.cn: 公司聘请了一位顾问重新设计支付系统。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞疼”：奖杯磕出一个小口，他疼得把它揣进怀里不肯撒手 → retain 保留、留住

root: 拉丁 retinere = re-（向后）+ tenere（握住），字面“往回握住、扣住不放”；同族词多与“握、持”有关。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of retain, all one gesture: a hand closes and keeps what it holds — property, a quality, a memory, power, a professional's time, heat, money, a reserved service, or people who might leave.
sensesIntro.cn: retain 的九个义项都源于同一个动作：手合拢，把握住的东西留下——财产、特性、记忆、权力、专业人士的时间、热量、钱款、预留的服务，以及可能离开的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed hand that does not let what it holds slip away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只合拢的手，不让握着的东西滑走。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND QUALITY: an object or a characteristic stays with its holder because the grip is not released.
branches.cn: 财产与特性：物件或特性留在持有者身上，因为握持没有松开。

branches.en: MEMORY: the grip is mental; information is held so that it does not slip out of the mind.
branches.cn: 记忆：握持发生在心智中；信息被扣住，以免滑出脑海。

branches.en: POWER: control over institutions is a grip that must not open.
branches.cn: 权力：对机构的控制是一只不能松开的手。

branches.en: MONEY AND SERVICE: a fee holds a professional's time; a deposit is money held back from its return.
branches.cn: 金钱与服务：聘金握住专业人士的时间；押金是被挡在“返回”路途上的钱。

branches.en: CONTAINMENT: heat stays inside a wall and users stay inside an app, both by the same closing gesture.
branches.cn: 围拢与留存：热量留在墙内，用户留在应用内，靠的都是同一个合拢动作。

intro.en: Retain is re- plus the Latin stem -tain. Neither part is freely productive in modern English: you cannot invent a new word with -tain, though the family of prefixed forms is large.
intro.cn: retain 是 re- 加拉丁词干 -tain。这两部分在现代英语里都不能自由造词：你不能用 -tain 新造一个词，但带不同前缀的同族词很多。

latinIntro.en: All the -tain words descend from Latin tenere 'to hold'. The prefixes change where the holding happens: together, away, by hand, from below.
latinIntro.cn: 所有 -tain 词都源自拉丁语 tenere“握住”。前缀改变的是“握持发生在哪里”：握在一起、扣住带走、用手扶住、从下面托住。

items.meaning: the act of keeping something, or the state of being kept
items.meaningCN: 保留；保持；留存（-tion 构成行为或状态名词）
items.example: The retention of heat in the walls keeps the house warm at night.
items.exampleCN: 墙体对热量的保留让房子在夜里也暖和。

items.meaning: able to keep or remember things well
items.meaningCN: 记性好的；能保持的（-ive 表示倾向）
items.example: She has a wonderfully retentive memory for names.
items.exampleCN: 她对名字的记忆力好得惊人。

items.meaning: a fee that reserves a service, or a person who retains something
items.meaningCN: 聘金；保留费；保留者（-er 表示做该动作的人或物）
items.example: He pays his accountant a small retainer each month.
items.exampleCN: 他每月付给会计一小笔聘金。

items.meaning: able to be kept or retained
items.meaningCN: 可保留的；可留住的（-able 表示能够）
items.example: The data is retainable for seven years under the contract.
items.exampleCN: 按合同，这些数据可以保留七年。

items.meaning: keeping something in place, as in a retaining wall
items.meaningCN: 用于保持的（如挡土墙）；保留（-ing 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: A retaining wall keeps the hillside from sliding.
items.exampleCN: 挡土墙防止山坡滑落。

items.meaning: to hold something inside or keep it under control
items.meaningCN: 包含；容纳；控制（con- 表“共同、在内”+ 握住）
items.example: This box contains all the old photographs.
items.exampleCN: 这个盒子装着所有旧照片。

items.meaning: to hold someone back, especially in custody
items.meaningCN: 拘留；耽搁（de- 表“离开”+ 握住，即“扣住不让走”）
items.example: Police detained the suspect for questioning.
items.exampleCN: 警方拘留嫌疑人问话。

items.meaning: to keep something going or in good condition
items.meaningCN: 维持；保养（main- 与“手”有关 + 握住，即“用手扶住”）
items.example: They maintain the bridge twice a year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年对这座桥维护两次。

items.meaning: to keep something supported or going over time
items.meaningCN: 支撑；维持（sus- 表“从下面”+ 握住，即“从下面托住”）
items.example: The soil sustains a wide range of crops.
items.exampleCN: 这片土壤供养着多种作物。

items.meaning: a person who holds land or property rented from a landlord
items.meaningCN: 租户；承租人（持有土地或房产的人）
items.example: The tenant pays rent on the first of every month.
items.exampleCN: 租户每月一号交房租。

latinEntries.meaning: to hold up from below, sustain

definition_zh: 揭示；显露；透露；揭露；启示
definition_en: to make something visible or known that was previously hidden, covered, or private
core_image: 揭开面纱：遮盖物被拉开，后面的东西第一次被看见
scene: When the fog lifted, it revealed the lighthouse standing alone on the rock.
sceneCN: 这里 reveal 是「使显现、露出」（第 1 个义项：让原本被遮住的东西可见）；句意：雾散之后，它让独自立在礁石上的灯塔显现出来。图中可辨识物件：散开的雾气、白色灯塔、礁石、海面、远处的船。

derivatives.zh: 揭露；被揭露的事实；启示
揭示内情的；发人深省的；暴露的
具有揭示性的；启发性的
暴露内情地；意味深长地

senses.title: Make visible: take the cover away
senses.titleCN: 使可见：把遮盖物拿开
senses.definition: to make something visible that was hidden by a cover, fog, or darkness
senses.definitionCN: 让被遮盖物、雾或黑暗挡住的东西变得可见
senses.example: The curtain rose and revealed a bare stage.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起，露出一个空荡荡的舞台。
senses.why: Latin revelare is re- 'back, away' plus velum 'veil'. The veil is pulled back, and what stood behind it is seen for the first time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revelare 是 re-“向后、移开”加 velum“面纱”。面纱被拉开，原本站在它后面的东西第一次被看见。

senses.title: Disclose a secret
senses.titleCN: 泄露秘密
senses.definition: to tell someone something that was kept secret or private
senses.definitionCN: 把原本保密或私密的事情告诉别人
senses.example: He finally revealed where the money had been hidden.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于透露了钱藏在哪里。
senses.why: A secret is kept under a cover of silence. Revealing it removes that cover, so the hidden fact becomes visible to others.
senses.whyCN: 秘密被盖在“沉默”之下。reveal 就是掀开这层覆盖，让隐藏的事实对别人变得可见。

senses.title: Bring the truth to light
senses.titleCN: 使真相显露
senses.definition: to show a fact or the true nature of something, especially after investigation
senses.definitionCN: 显示事实或事物的真实性质，尤指调查之后
senses.example: The investigation revealed serious flaws in the design.
senses.exampleCN: 调查揭示出设计中的严重缺陷。
senses.why: The cover here is error or concealment. Once the veil is removed, the truth is not created but simply allowed to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 这里的遮盖物是错误或隐瞒。面纱一经揭掉，真相并不是被制造出来，而只是被允许看见。

senses.title: Let an emotion show
senses.titleCN: 流露情感
senses.definition: to let a feeling be seen in your face, voice, or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 让某种情绪从表情、声音或行为中显露出来
senses.example: Her smile revealed how relieved she really was.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑容流露出她其实多么如释重负。
senses.why: Feelings are normally covered by a composed face. When the face reveals them, the inner state becomes visible without being spoken.
senses.whyCN: 情绪通常被镇定的表情遮盖。当表情把它 reveal 出来时，内在状态不必说出口就变得可见。

senses.title: Divine revelation: truth given from above
senses.titleCN: 神启：自上而来的真理
senses.definition: to make a religious truth known to a person, as God or a divine power is said to do
senses.definitionCN: 使人知道宗教真理，据信由上帝或神力所为
senses.example: The prophet said that God had revealed the law to him.
senses.exampleCN: 先知说上帝把律法启示给了他。
senses.why: The veil here belongs to the hidden divine order. Revelation is the act of lifting that veil so a human can see what was beyond reach.
senses.whyCN: 这里的面纱属于隐藏的神圣秩序。启示就是掀开这层面纱，让人看见原本无法触及的东西。

senses.title: Bring out the image: photographic development
senses.titleCN: 显影：让影像浮现
senses.definition: to make a hidden photographic image appear on film or paper through chemical development
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学显影让胶片或相纸上隐藏的影像显现
senses.example: The developing fluid revealed the faces in the old negative.
senses.exampleCN: 显影液让旧底片上的面孔显现出来。
senses.why: The image is already there, hidden in the emulsion. Development removes the chemical cover, so reveal is again 'make the invisible visible'.
senses.whyCN: 影像早已存在，只是藏在感光乳剂里。显影去掉化学层面的遮盖，所以 reveal 仍是“让不可见者可见”。

senses.title: Expose the body or clothing
senses.titleCN: 暴露身体或衣着
senses.definition: to show a part of the body or an undergarment that is usually covered
senses.definitionCN: 露出通常被衣物遮住的身体部位或内衣
senses.example: The wind revealed the edge of the bandage on his wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 风掀开了他手腕上绷带的一角。
senses.why: This is the most literal branch: cloth is the veil, and the body under it becomes visible when the cloth moves aside.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的一支：布料就是面纱，布料一移开，下面的身体就变得可见。

senses.title: Show your hand: reveal intentions
senses.titleCN: 亮出底牌：暴露意图
senses.definition: to make your plans, strengths, or true position known, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 让计划、实力或真实立场为人所知，常含不情愿
senses.example: He revealed his hand by demanding a raise too early.
senses.exampleCN: 他过早要求加薪，暴露了自己的底牌。
senses.why: In cards, the hand is hidden until shown. Revealing it gives away the advantage, just as lifting a veil can leave you exposed.
senses.whyCN: 打牌时手牌本是藏着的，亮出来就失去优势。reveal 底牌就像揭掉自己的面纱，反而把自己暴露了。

senses.title: Show a pattern in data
senses.titleCN: 显示数据中的规律
senses.definition: to show a fact or pattern that becomes clear when information is examined
senses.definitionCN: 在检视信息时显示出来的事实或规律
senses.example: The survey revealed a steady decline in reading time.
senses.exampleCN: 调查显示阅读时间在持续下降。
senses.why: Numbers hide their pattern until they are arranged and read. The chart removes that cover, so the trend is revealed rather than invented.
senses.whyCN: 数字在排列、读取之前藏着规律。图表掀开这层遮盖，因此趋势是被 reveal 出来的，而不是被发明出来的。

intro.en: Reveal entered English around 1400 from Old French, and goes back to Latin revelare 'to remove the veil'. Dates are approximate; the deeper origin of velum is uncertain, and the similar word revel 'make merry' is generally treated as a different word.
intro.cn: reveal 约于 1400 年经古法语进入英语，可上溯到拉丁语 revelare“揭开面纱”。年代为大致估计；velum 更深来源不确定，形近的 revel“狂欢”一般被视为另一个词。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'to disclose, make known', especially in religious writing.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录为“披露、使人知道”，尤见于宗教文本。

items.en: From Old French reveler 'to reveal, disclose', which also carried the sense 'to bring to light'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 reveler“揭示、披露”，也带有“使见光”的意思。

items.en: From Latin revelare 'to reveal, uncover', built from re- 'back, away' and velum 'veil, curtain, covering'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 revelare“揭示、揭开”，由 re-“向后、移开”与 velum“面纱、帘幕、覆盖物”构成。

items.en: Velum meant a cloth curtain or veil, including the awning used over Roman theatres. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is not safely connected to vehere 'to carry'.
items.cn: velum 指布帘或面纱，也包括罗马剧场上的遮阳篷。它更深的来源不确定，不能可靠地与 vehere“运送”相连。

items.en: The religious sense 'divine revelation' dominated early usage. By the 19c. the word was also used for photographic development and for showing hidden facts in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 宗教义“神启”在早期用法中占主导。到 19 世纪，该词也用于摄影显影，并在日常语言中表示“显示隐藏的事实”。

items.en: Modern English uses reveal for secrets, evidence, emotions, data, body parts and intentions. The noun a reveal is informal and recent, as in the final reveal of a show.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reveal 表示秘密、证据、情感、数据、身体部位和意图。名词 a reveal 属非正式且较新的用法，如节目的“最终揭晓”。

note.en: The first group holds look-alike words, including one false friend; the second holds verbs close in meaning. Notice which one keeps the veil metaphor.
note.cn: 第一组是形近词，其中一个是“假朋友”；第二组是近义动词。注意哪一个还保留着“面纱”的比喻。

entries.definition: to enjoy yourself noisily at a party. It is generally traced to Old French reveler 'to rebel, make merry', a different word from reveal despite the spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 在聚会上狂欢作乐。它一般追溯到古法语 reveler“反叛、作乐”，尽管拼写相近，却是与 reveal 不同的词。

entries.definition: the bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning. It comes from French réveillez 'wake up', not from revelare.
entries.definitionCN: 清晨唤醒士兵的起床号。它来自法语 réveillez“醒来”，并非出自 revelare。

entries.definition: the noun from reveal: a surprising disclosure or a divine truth. It is the same word family, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: reveal 派生的名词：令人意外的揭露或神圣启示。它是同族词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to make information known, especially something that was kept private. It is more formal and more factual than reveal.
entries.definitionCN: 公开信息，尤指原本保密的内容。它比 reveal 更正式、更偏事实陈述。

entries.definition: to uncover something so that it is seen, often leaving it unprotected. It stresses vulnerability, not just visibility.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物暴露在外而被看见，常含失去保护之意。它强调脆弱性，而不只是可见。

entries.definition: to remove a physical cover, or to discover something hidden. It is the plain literal version of reveal.
entries.definitionCN: 拿掉实物遮盖，或发现隐藏之物。它是 reveal 最朴素的字面版本。

entries.definition: to give away secret or confidential information, often reluctantly. Its object is nearly always information.
entries.definitionCN: 泄露秘密或机密信息，常含不情愿。它的宾语几乎总是信息。

entries.definition: to remove a veil literally, or to announce a new product or plan. It keeps the same veil metaphor and is often used for official launches.
entries.definitionCN: 字面“揭开头纱”，也指发布新产品或计划。它保留同样的面纱比喻，常用于官方发布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin parts re- and velum, the real relative unveil, and real modern uses such as the big reveal.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁成分 re- 与 velum、真实同族词 unveil，以及 the big reveal 等真实现代用法。

normal.en: re- 'away' + velum 'veil' = take the veil away. Reveal is a stage trick described in one word.
normal.cn: re-“移开”+ velum“面纱”= 把面纱拿开。reveal 就是用一个词描述的舞台揭幕动作。

normal.en: Unveil uses the same veil in English: a new statue or product is unveiled when the cloth is pulled off.
normal.cn: unveil 在英语里用的是同一块“面纱”：新雕像或新产品被揭布，就是 unveiled。

normal.en: Revelation is the noun: in religion it is truth shown from above, in everyday talk it is a surprising fact.
normal.cn: revelation 是名词：在宗教里指自上显现的真理，在日常话语里指令人意外的事实。

normal.en: The big reveal is the moment a TV show or game finally shows what was hidden.
normal.cn: the big reveal 是电视节目或游戏终于亮出隐藏内容的时刻。

normal.en: In a darkroom the image is already on the film; the developer only reveals it. The word never means 'create'.
normal.cn: 暗房里影像早已在胶片上，显影液只是把它 reveal 出来。这个词从来不表示“创造”。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy curtain. Nothing exists behind it until it moves, but the moment it is pulled back, the room is revealed.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅厚重的帘子。它不动时，后面的一切都无从看见；它被拉开的瞬间，房间就被 reveal 了。

abstract.en: A secret, a truth, an emotion and a data trend are all 'behind the curtain' in the same way.
abstract.cn: 秘密、真相、情感和数据趋势，都以同样的方式待在“帘子后面”。

abstract.en: In the exposure sense the curtain is cloth on the body; in the card sense it is your own hidden hand. Both leave you seen.
abstract.cn: 在“暴露身体”义里，帘子是身上的布料；在“亮底牌”义里，帘子是你自己藏着的手牌。两者都让你被看见。

examples.en: The report revealed that the bridge had never been inspected.
examples.cn: 报告披露，这座桥从未接受过检查。

examples.en: Her calm voice revealed nothing about how nervous she was.
examples.cn: 她平静的声音丝毫没流露出她有多紧张。

examples.en: A single photograph can reveal more about a place than a long article.
examples.cn: 一张照片有时比一篇长文更能揭示一个地方的真实面貌。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞薇儿”：瑞薇儿伸手一扯，面纱落下，真容露了出来 → reveal 揭开、显露

root: 拉丁 revelare = re-（向后、移开）+ velum（面纱），字面“把面纱揭开”，核心是“去除遮盖，使可见”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of reveal, all one action: a veil is lifted. The veil may be fog, silence, error, a composed face, the divine order, film emulsion, cloth, a hidden hand, or a table of numbers.
sensesIntro.cn: reveal 的九个义项都源于同一个动作：揭开面纱。这层面纱可以是雾、沉默、错误、镇定的表情、神圣秩序、胶片乳剂、布料、藏着的手牌，或一张数字表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a veil is pulled back and what was behind it is seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：面纱被拉开，后面的东西被看见。

branches.en: VISIBLE: fog, a curtain or clothing is removed, and the eye receives what was covered.
branches.cn: 可见：雾、帘幕或衣物被移开，眼睛接收到原本被遮住的东西。

branches.en: SECRET AND TRUTH: silence or error is the cover; disclosure lets the fact be seen.
branches.cn: 秘密与真相：沉默或错误是遮盖物；披露让事实被看见。

branches.en: INNER STATE: a composed face or a hidden hand is uncovered, exposing feeling or intention.
branches.cn: 内在状态：镇定的表情或藏着的手牌被掀开，情感或意图随之暴露。

branches.en: DIVINE ORDER: the veil is metaphysical, and revelation is truth given from above.
branches.cn: 神圣秩序：面纱是形而上的，启示是自上赐下的真理。

branches.en: IMAGE AND DATA: the hidden pattern is already present in the emulsion or the numbers, and development or analysis makes it appear.
branches.cn: 影像与数据：隐藏的图案本已存在于乳剂或数字中，显影或分析使它显现。

intro.en: Reveal is Latin re- plus velum, but in English the parts no longer work separately. What is productive is the suffix chain: reveal, revealing, revelation, revelatory.
intro.cn: reveal 是拉丁语 re- 加 velum，但在英语里这两个部分已不能独立使用。真正能产的是后缀链：reveal、revealing、revelation、revelatory。

latinIntro.en: Velum 'veil, curtain' is the source of veil and reveal alike. The Latin family also includes velare 'to cover with a veil' and revelatio 'a uncovering'.
latinIntro.cn: velum“面纱、帘幕”既是 veil 也是 reveal 的来源。拉丁同族还有 velare“用面纱覆盖”和 revelatio“揭开”。

items.structure: reveal + -ation (noun of action, with a spelling change)
items.meaning: the act of revealing, or the fact that is revealed
items.meaningCN: 揭露；被揭露的事实；启示（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The revelation that the letter was forged shocked the court.
items.exampleCN: 那封信是伪造的这一揭露震动了法庭。

items.meaning: making something important newly clear
items.meaningCN: 具有揭示性的；启发性的（-ory 表示性质）
items.example: It was a revelatory account of how the decision was made.
items.exampleCN: 那是一份揭示决策如何作出的启发性记述。

items.meaning: showing something that was hidden; informative
items.meaningCN: 揭示内情的；暴露的（-ing 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: She made a revealing remark about the negotiations.
items.exampleCN: 她说了一句暴露谈判内情的话。

items.meaning: a person or thing that reveals something
items.meaningCN: 揭示者；揭发者（-er 表示做该动作者）
items.example: The archive was the real revealer of the family's history.
items.exampleCN: 这座档案馆才是这个家族历史的真正揭示者。

items.meaning: having been made visible or known
items.meaningCN: 已被揭示的；已显露的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The revealed documents changed the public's view.
items.exampleCN: 被披露的文件改变了公众的看法。

items.meaning: not yet made known or seen
items.meaningCN: 未揭示的；未透露的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The cause of the fire remains unrevealed.
items.exampleCN: 火灾原因仍未查明公布。

items.meaning: to remove a covering, or to launch something new publicly
items.meaningCN: 揭幕；公布（un- 表“去除”+ veil“面纱”）
items.example: The company will unveil its new phone next month.
items.exampleCN: 公司下个月将发布新手机。

items.meaning: covered by a veil, or expressed indirectly
items.meaningCN: 蒙着面纱的；含蓄的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: He made a veiled threat about the lawsuit.
items.exampleCN: 他就那场诉讼发出含蓄的威胁。

items.meaning: one who reveals, especially a divine revealer
items.meaningCN: 启示者；揭示者（-or 表示施动者，较罕见）
items.example: The text describes the prophet as a revelator.
items.exampleCN: 文本把这位先知描述为启示者。

definition_zh: 财政收入；税收；营业收入；收入来源
definition_en: money that a government receives from taxes, or money that a business receives from its sales and other activities
core_image: 回流之水：钱从交易的那一头又流回账上
scene: After the bakery started selling coffee, its monthly revenue doubled.
sceneCN: 这里 revenue 是「营业收入」（第 2 个义项：企业销售所得）；句意：面包店开始卖咖啡后，它的月营业收入翻了一倍。图中可辨识物件：收银机、面包、咖啡杯、账本、排队的顾客。

pos.zh: （the revenue）税务部门（英式、爱尔兰用法）

derivatives.zh: 税务官员；缉私人员（美式，非正式）
非收入的；不产生收入的
收入中性的（税改不增减总税收）
收入为正的；带来正收益的

senses.title: Government income from taxes
senses.titleCN: 政府的税收收入
senses.definition: the money a government collects from taxes and other public charges
senses.definitionCN: 政府从税收及其他公共收费中收取的钱
senses.example: The city's tax revenue fell sharply after the factories closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂关闭后，这座城市的税收收入大幅下降。
senses.why: The oldest image is money that comes back. Taxes are paid out into the public system and return to the state as revenue.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意象是“回来的钱”。税款缴入公共体系，又作为 revenue 回到国家手中。

senses.title: Business income from sales
senses.titleCN: 企业的营业收入
senses.definition: the total money a company receives from selling goods or services before costs are subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 公司在扣除成本之前，通过销售商品或服务收到的全部款项
senses.example: The company reported revenue of four million dollars last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司去年报告了四百万美元的营业收入。
senses.why: Every sale sends money out to the customer and back to the seller. Revenue is the stream returning to the business account.
senses.whyCN: 每一笔交易都把钱付给卖方，又从顾客那边回到卖方。revenue 就是回流到企业账户的那股水。

senses.title: A stream or source of income
senses.titleCN: 收入来源；收入流
senses.definition: a particular activity or channel that regularly brings money in
senses.definitionCN: 定期带来收入的某项活动或渠道
senses.example: Advertising is still the newspaper's main revenue stream.
senses.exampleCN: 广告仍是这家报纸的主要收入来源。
senses.why: The return needs a channel. A revenue stream is a riverbed through which money recurrently comes back.
senses.whyCN: 回流需要通道。revenue stream 就是一条河床，钱沿着它反复流回来。

senses.title: Accounting revenue: gross income
senses.titleCN: 会计上的收入：毛收入
senses.definition: in accounting, the gross amount recorded from sales before expenses, taxes and discounts are deducted
senses.definitionCN: 会计上，在扣除费用、税款和折扣之前记录的销售总额
senses.example: Revenue is recorded at the top of the income statement, above expenses.
senses.exampleCN: 收入记在利润表的最上方，位于各项费用之上。
senses.why: Accounting isolates the incoming flow and names it revenue, leaving profit for what remains after the outflow.
senses.whyCN: 会计把“流入的那股水”单独拎出来，命名为 revenue；利润则留给流出之后剩下的部分。

senses.title: The Revenue: the tax authority
senses.titleCN: 税务机关：the Revenue
senses.definition: used with the definite article in British and Irish English for the government department that collects taxes
senses.definitionCN: 在英式及爱尔兰英语中与定冠词连用，指负责征税的政府部门
senses.example: The Revenue sent him a letter about the unpaid tax.
senses.exampleCN: 税务部门给他寄了一封关于欠税的信。
senses.why: This is a metonymy: the office is named after the money it collects. The department is, in effect, the place where returning public money lands.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：机构以它征收的钱命名。税务部门实际上就是公共资金“回流”的落点。

senses.title: Revenue tariff: duty raised for income
senses.titleCN: 财政关税：为增加收入而征的税
senses.definition: a tariff imposed mainly to raise government income rather than to protect domestic industry
senses.definitionCN: 主要为增加政府收入、而非保护本国产业而征收的关税
senses.example: A revenue tariff on imported tea once funded much of the government.
senses.exampleCN: 对进口茶叶征收的财政关税曾供养政府的大部分开支。
senses.why: The duty is not a wall but a sluice: its purpose is to make money flow back into the treasury.
senses.whyCN: 这种关税不是一堵墙，而是一道水闸：它的目的是让钱流回国库。

senses.title: Archaic return: the act of coming back
senses.titleCN: 古义：返回、归来
senses.definition: in older texts, the return of something, especially the return of a season or a period
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文本中指某物的返回，尤指季节或时段的回归
senses.example: In older writing, the revenue of spring meant the return of spring.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，the revenue of spring 指的是春天的回归。
senses.why: This is the literal French sense still visible in the word: revenu is the past participle of revenir, 'to come back'. Income is simply 'that which returns'.
senses.whyCN: 这是词里仍可见的法语字面义：revenu 是 revenir“回来”的过去分词。收入不过是“返回之物”。

senses.title: Total public receipts: annual revenue
senses.titleCN: 总岁入：年度公共收入
senses.definition: the whole of a government's income in a period, including taxes, fees, fines and grants
senses.definitionCN: 政府在一定时期内的全部收入，包括税收、收费、罚款和拨款
senses.example: Public revenue includes taxes, fees and grants from other countries.
senses.exampleCN: 公共岁入包括税收、收费以及来自其他国家的拨款。
senses.why: The image widens from one returning stream to the whole basin: every channel that feeds the public purse is counted as revenue.
senses.whyCN: 意象从一条回流扩展到整个流域：每一条汇入公共钱袋的通道都计入 revenue。

intro.en: Revenue came into English in the early 15c. from French, and its oldest sense is literally 'that which returns'. Dates are approximate; the link of venire to PIE *gʷem- is generally accepted but not certain in every detail.
intro.cn: revenue 于 15 世纪早期经法语进入英语，最古老的意义字面就是“返回之物”。年代为大致估计；venire 与原始印欧语 *gʷem- 的联系为一般接受之说，细节并非全然确定。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'income from land, property or an office', the money that comes back to an owner.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录为“来自土地、财产或官职的收入”，即回到所有者手里的钱。

items.en: From Old French revenu 'return, income', the past participle of revenir 'to come back'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 revenu“返回、收入”，是 revenir“回来”的过去分词。

items.en: Old French revenir goes back to Latin revenire 'to come back', from re- 'back' and venire 'to come'.
items.cn: 古法语 revenir 可上溯到拉丁语 revenire“回来”，由 re-“回”与 venire“来”构成。

items.en: Venire 'to come' is generally traced to PIE *gʷem- 'to go, come', the same deep root that gives English come through Germanic. The paths are different; the connection is very old.
items.cn: venire“来”一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *gʷem-“走、来”，英语 come 经日耳曼语也出自同一深层词根。两条路径不同，联系非常古老。

items.en: With the growth of state finance, revenue became the standard word for public income, and the Revenue came to name the tax authority.
items.cn: 随着国家财政的发展，revenue 成为“公共收入”的标准词，the Revenue 也开始指税务机关。

items.en: Modern usage splits into public revenue (taxes) and business revenue (sales), with accounting rules for revenue recognition and phrases such as revenue stream and revenue sharing.
items.cn: 现代用法分为公共 revenue（税收）与企业 revenue（销售额），并有收入确认等会计规则，以及 revenue stream、revenue sharing 等短语。

note.en: The first group is about form: two words that resemble revenue and one that is built from it. The second group separates income words by what exactly they count.
note.cn: 第一组看词形：两个与 revenue 形近的词，加一个由它派生的词。第二组按“到底在数哪一笔钱”区分同义的收入词。

entries.definition: a wide street, or a possible way of doing something. Its -venue comes from venir 'to come', but with ad- 'to', so it means 'a way to come to'.
entries.definitionCN: 宽阔的街道，或做某事的可能途径。它的 -venue 也来自 venir“来”，但前缀是 ad-“向”，因此意为“通往某处之路”。

entries.definition: to hurt someone in return for a wrong. It looks close but comes from Latin vindicare 'to claim, avenge', not from venire.
entries.definitionCN: 报复；为受到的伤害回击某人。它看起来相近，但来自拉丁语 vindicare“主张、复仇”，并非 venire。

entries.definition: a US informal word for a tax officer or customs agent. It is revenue plus -er, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 美式非正式用语，指税务官员或缉私人员。它是 revenue 加 -er，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: money received regularly by a person or organization. It is the everyday word and covers wages, rent and profit, while revenue is mainly public or corporate.
entries.definitionCN: 个人或组织定期收到的钱。它是日常用词，涵盖工资、租金和利润；revenue 主要用于公共或企业语境。

entries.definition: money made from work or business, often after costs. It is closer to profit than to revenue, which is before costs.
entries.definitionCN: 靠工作或经营赚到的钱，常为扣除成本后。它比 revenue 更接近利润，而 revenue 在成本之前。

entries.definition: the money received from a particular sale, event or disposal. It is narrower and usually refers to one transaction or occasion.
entries.definitionCN: 某次销售、活动或处置所得的钱。它范围更窄，通常指一次交易或一场活动。

entries.definition: the total amounts of money received in a period. It is a bookkeeping word for cash coming in, not the same as earned revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 某时期收到的款项总额。它是记账用语，指流入的现金，与“已赚得的收入”不完全相同。

entries.definition: in British business English, the total sales of a company in a period. It is the closest British equivalent of revenue.
entries.definitionCN: 在英式商务英语中指公司某时期的总销售额。它是最接近 revenue 的英式说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real French participle revenu, the real Latin verb revenire, and real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的法语分词 revenu、真实的拉丁动词 revenire，以及真实的会计短语。

normal.en: Revenir means 'to come back'. Revenue is literally 'the come-back money', the cash that returns after a sale.
normal.cn: revenir 意为“回来”。revenue 字面就是“回流之钱”，即交易之后又回到手里的现金。

normal.en: Income is what a person receives; revenue is what a government or a company receives. Same direction of flow, different container.
normal.cn: income 是个人收到的钱；revenue 是政府或企业收到的钱。流向相同，容器不同。

normal.en: Revenue is before costs, profit is after costs. A shop can have record revenue and still lose money.
normal.cn: revenue 在成本之前，profit 在成本之后。一家店可以有创纪录的营收，仍然亏钱。

normal.en: A revenue stream is a channel, not an amount: subscriptions, ads and licensing can each be a stream.
normal.cn: revenue stream 是通道而不是金额：订阅、广告、授权都可以各算一条收入流。

normal.en: The Revenue, with a capital R, is the tax office in British and Irish usage.
normal.cn: the Revenue（大写 R）在英式与爱尔兰用法里指税务局。

abstract.en: Picture a tide: it leaves the shore, then comes back and fills the harbour. Revenue is the returning tide of money.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水：它离开岸边，又回来灌满港湾。revenue 就是钱的“回潮”。

abstract.en: A business is a network of channels; every channel that carries money back is a revenue stream.
abstract.cn: 企业是一张渠道网；每一条把钱带回来的通道，都是一条 revenue stream。

abstract.en: The tax office is named after the water it collects, so the department and the money share one word.
abstract.cn: 税务局以它收集的“水”命名，所以机构和钱共用一个词。

examples.en: Oil taxes provide most of the country's revenue.
examples.cn: 石油税收提供了这个国家的大部分财政收入。

examples.en: The airline's revenue rose even though its profit fell.
examples.cn: 尽管利润下降，这家航空公司的营业收入仍上升了。

examples.en: They are looking for a second revenue stream to survive the winter.
examples.cn: 他们正在寻找第二条收入来源，以熬过冬天。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞沃纽”：瑞沃纽把卖货收到的钱又一车车拉回自己的钱箱 → revenue 收入、营收

root: 古法语 revenu“回来的（东西）”，源自拉丁 revenire = re-（回）+ venire（来），字面“回流之物”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of revenue, one image: money that comes back. It returns to a government as taxes, to a company as sales, through a channel, into an account, into a treasury, or as the archaic 'return' itself.
sensesIntro.cn: revenue 的八个义项共用一个意象：回来的钱。它以税收回到政府，以销售额回到企业，经某条通道、某个账户、某个国库，或以古义“归来”本身出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money that flows back into the account that spent or supplied it.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱又流回那个支出或供货的账户。

branches.en: PUBLIC MONEY: tax receipts and total annual receipts are the state's returning tide.
branches.cn: 公共资金：税收与年度总岁入，都是国家那股回流的潮水。

branches.en: BUSINESS MONEY: sales income and accounting revenue count the inflow before costs.
branches.cn: 企业资金：销售所得与会计收入，数的都是成本之前的流入。

branches.en: CHANNEL: a revenue stream is a riverbed that carries the returning money.
branches.cn: 通道：收入流是承载回流之钱的河床。

branches.en: COLLECTION: the tax authority and a revenue tariff are the places and sluices where public money is gathered.
branches.cn: 征收：税务机关与财政关税，是公共资金被汇集的地点与水闸。

branches.en: LITERAL RETURN: the archaic sense keeps the original French meaning visible under the finance.
branches.cn: 字面返回：古义让财务外壳下的法语本义仍然可见。

intro.en: Revenue is a French past participle frozen as a noun; re- and venire cannot be split off and used freely in English. Productive formation happens at the edges: plurals, -er, non-, and compounds.
intro.cn: revenue 是一个凝固成名词的法语过去分词；在英语里不能把 re- 和 venire 拆下来自由使用。能产的构词发生在边缘：复数、-er、non- 以及复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb venire 'to come' also gives advent, convene, intervene and provenance. Re- adds the direction 'back', which is exactly what revenue means.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 venire“来”还产生 advent、convene、intervene、provenance。re- 加上“回”的方向，这正是 revenue 的意思。

items.meaning: multiple income streams or amounts received
items.meaningCN: 多项收入；多笔营收（-s 构成复数）
items.example: The group's revenues grew in three of its four markets.
items.exampleCN: 该集团在四个市场中的三个实现了营收增长。

items.meaning: a tax officer or customs agent, in US informal use
items.meaningCN: 税务官员；缉私人员（美式非正式，-er 表示相关的人）
items.example: A revenuer stopped the truck at the border.
items.exampleCN: 一名缉私人员在边境拦下了那辆卡车。

items.meaning: not producing income, or not related to income
items.meaningCN: 不产生收入的；与收入无关的（non- 表否定）
items.example: The library runs several nonrevenue services.
items.exampleCN: 这家图书馆提供几项不产生收入的服务。

items.meaning: an arrangement that divides income between parties
items.meaningCN: 收入分成（把收入在各方之间分配的安排）
items.example: The two airlines signed a revenue-sharing agreement.
items.exampleCN: 两家航空公司签署了收入分成协议。

items.meaning: designed so that total tax income neither rises nor falls
items.meaningCN: 收入中性的（使总税收不增不减的税制设计）
items.example: The reform was sold as revenue-neutral.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革被宣传为收入中性的。

items.meaning: bringing in more money than it costs
items.meaningCN: 收入为正的；收益大于成本的
items.example: The new route became revenue-positive within a year.
items.exampleCN: 这条新航线一年内就实现了正收益。

items.meaning: a person who returns, especially from the dead
items.meaningCN: 归来者；还魂者（-ant 表示人，与 revenir 同根）
items.example: The story is told by a revenant who cannot rest.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事由一个无法安息的还魂者讲述。

items.meaning: the place of origin of an object or work of art
items.meaningCN: 来源；出处（pro-“向前”+ venire“来”，即“从何处而来”）
items.example: The painting's provenance was traced to a private collection.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画的来源被追溯到一处私人收藏。

items.meaning: a way of approach, literally or figuratively
items.meaningCN: 大街；途径（ad-“向”+ venire“来”，即“通往之路”）
items.example: They explored every avenue for funding.
items.exampleCN: 他们探索了每一条筹资途径。

definition_zh: 反转；颠倒；撤销；倒车；相反的；背面
definition_en: to turn something back or the other way, to undo a decision, or the opposite or back side of something
core_image: 倒着转的齿轮：同一个轮子，转向与原来相反
scene: She checked the mirror twice before reversing slowly into the narrow garage.
sceneCN: 这里 reverse 是「倒车」（第 3 个义项：让车向后行驶）；句意：她把后视镜看了两遍，才慢慢倒进狭窄的车库。图中可辨识物件：汽车、后视镜、车库门、倒车灯、地上的轮胎痕。

derivatives.zh: 可逆的；可翻转的；正反两穿的

senses.title: Turn a direction or process the other way
senses.titleCN: 把方向或过程反过来
senses.definition: to make something move, flow, or develop in the opposite direction
senses.definitionCN: 使某物朝相反方向移动、流动或发展
senses.example: A new dam reversed the flow of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 一座新水坝使河流的流向反转了。
senses.why: Latin revertere is re- 'back' plus vertere 'to turn'. The wheel is turned until it faces the other way, so the process runs backwards.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revertere 是 re-“回”加 vertere“转”。轮子被转到相反的方向，过程因此倒着走。

senses.title: Overturn a decision or judgment
senses.titleCN: 撤销决定或判决
senses.definition: to officially cancel or change a decision, ruling, or policy
senses.definitionCN: 正式取消或改变一项决定、裁决或政策
senses.example: The appeal court reversed the earlier ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉法院撤销了先前的裁决。
senses.why: A ruling is turned back on itself: what stood now falls, and the previous position is restored.
senses.whyCN: 裁决被“转回去”：原先立着的现在倒下，之前的状态得以恢复。

senses.title: Drive backwards: reverse gear
senses.titleCN: 倒车：挂倒挡
senses.definition: to drive a vehicle backwards, or the gear that makes a vehicle move backwards
senses.definitionCN: 使车辆向后行驶，或使车辆后退的挡位
senses.example: He put the car in reverse and backed out of the driveway.
senses.exampleCN: 他挂上倒挡，把车倒出了车道。
senses.why: The gearbox turns the wheels in the opposite direction. The vehicle is going one way while its wheels turn the other way.
senses.whyCN: 变速箱让车轮朝相反方向转。车在往一个方向走，轮子却在反着转。

senses.title: Swap roles or positions
senses.titleCN: 互换角色或位置
senses.definition: to exchange the roles, positions, or order of two people or things
senses.definitionCN: 互换两个人或物的角色、位置或次序
senses.example: For one scene, the two actors reversed roles.
senses.exampleCN: 有一场戏里，两位演员互换了角色。
senses.why: Two positions are imagined on a wheel; turning it half a circle puts each side where the other was.
senses.whyCN: 想象两个位置在轮子上；把轮子转半圈，每一边就来到了另一边原先的位置。

senses.title: Reverse charge: turn the cost back
senses.titleCN: 对方付费：把费用转回去
senses.definition: of a phone call, with the cost charged to the person who receives it rather than the caller
senses.definitionCN: 指电话由接听方而非拨打方付费
senses.example: He called reverse charge from the airport and I paid.
senses.exampleCN: 他从机场打来对方付费电话，由我付钱。
senses.why: The charge is turned back along the same line, from the caller to the receiver. This is revertere applied to billing.
senses.whyCN: 费用沿着同一条线路“转回去”，从拨打方转到接听方。这是把 revertere 用在计费上。

senses.title: Reverse engineering: work back from the product
senses.titleCN: 逆向工程：从成品倒推设计
senses.definition: to analyse a finished product in order to understand and reproduce how it was designed
senses.definitionCN: 分析成品，以理解并复现它的设计过程
senses.example: Engineers reverse-engineered the chip to learn its architecture.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师对芯片做逆向工程，以了解其架构。
senses.why: The normal path is design to product; reverse runs it backwards, turning the sequence around at each step.
senses.whyCN: 正常路径是从设计到成品；reverse 把它倒过来，每一步都把顺序翻转。

senses.title: Reverse a transaction: undo the payment
senses.titleCN: 冲销交易：撤销付款
senses.definition: to cancel a payment or transaction and restore the money to the earlier account
senses.definitionCN: 取消一笔付款或交易，把钱退回原账户
senses.example: The bank reversed the charge after the dispute was settled.
senses.exampleCN: 纠纷解决后，银行冲销了这笔扣款。
senses.why: Money that travelled forward is sent back along the same route, so the transaction runs in reverse.
senses.whyCN: 向前走的钱沿原路被送回，于是这笔交易就 reverse 了。

senses.title: Reverse the order: end to start
senses.titleCN: 颠倒顺序：从尾到头
senses.definition: to change the order of items so that the last becomes the first
senses.definitionCN: 改变项目的排列，使最后一个变成第一个
senses.example: Reverse the list before printing it.
senses.exampleCN: 打印之前先把列表顺序反过来。
senses.why: The line of items is turned around its midpoint; the same elements remain, but their direction of reading is opposite.
senses.whyCN: 一排项目以中点为轴转了个身；元素没变，但阅读方向相反了。

senses.title: The opposite or the back side
senses.titleCN: 相反面；背面
senses.definition: the contrary of something, or the side of a coin, cloth, or page that is normally not shown
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的相反情况，或硬币、布料、页面通常不展示的那一面
senses.example: The reverse is also true: silence can protect a secret.
senses.exampleCN: 反过来也成立：沉默也能保护秘密。
senses.why: Every turned object shows two sides. The reverse is simply the side now facing you after the turn.
senses.whyCN: 每个被翻转的物体都有两面。the reverse 就是翻转之后正对着你的那一面。

intro.en: Reverse came into English around 1300 from Old French and Latin. Dates are approximate; the link of vertere to PIE *wer- 'to turn' is generally accepted.
intro.cn: reverse 约于 1300 年经古法语与拉丁语进入英语。年代为大致估计；vertere 与原始印欧语 *wer-“转”的联系为一般接受之说。

items.en: First recorded in English as an adjective and noun meaning 'opposite, contrary; the back side', and soon also as a verb 'to turn backwards'.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录为形容词和名词，意为“相反的、对立的；背面”，很快也作动词“使倒转”。

items.en: From Old French revers 'opposite, reverse', a noun and adjective built on the past participle of reverser 'to turn back'.
items.cn: 来自古法语 revers“相反的、反向的”，是由 reverser“转回去”的过去分词构成的形容词与名词。

items.en: From Latin reversus, past participle of revertere 'to turn back', built from re- 'back' and vertere 'to turn'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 reversus，是 revertere“转回去”的过去分词，由 re-“回”与 vertere“转”构成。

items.en: Vertere 'to turn' is generally traced to PIE *wer- 'to turn, bend'. The same family gives versus, verse, vertex, convert, divert and invert.
items.cn: vertere“转”一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *wer-“转、弯”。同一家族产生 versus、verse、vertex、convert、divert、invert。

items.en: Legal reversal of judgments developed in the 15c.; the sense 'back side of a coin or medal' is also old. The word kept both the physical and the legal branches.
items.cn: 对判决的撤销于 15 世纪发展起来；“硬币或奖章的背面”这一义项也很古老。这个词同时保留了物理与法律两支。

items.en: The industrial and technical senses appear: reverse gear for vehicles, reverse charge for telephone calls, and later reverse engineering and reversing a bank transaction.
items.cn: 工业与技术义项陆续出现：车辆的倒挡、电话的对方付费，之后又有逆向工程和冲销银行交易。

note.en: The first group is formal: words that resemble reverse, including one built on the same Latin verb. The second group is semantic: verbs and nouns of turning something the other way.
note.cn: 第一组看词形：与 reverse 形近的词，其中一个建于同一个拉丁动词。第二组看词义：表示“把某物转向反面”的动词与名词。

entries.definition: strongly opposed or unwilling. It is a- 'away' plus versus 'turned', literally 'turned away from'.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈反对的；不情愿的。它是 a-“离开”加 versus“转”，字面“被转开、不愿面对”。

entries.definition: to respect someone deeply. Its re- is intensive and its root is vereri 'to fear, respect', not vertere.
entries.definitionCN: 深深敬重某人。它的 re- 表加强，词根是 vereri“畏惧、敬重”，不是 vertere。

entries.definition: the noun from reverse: the act of turning something back or the change itself. It is the same word family, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: reverse 派生的名词：反转的行为或反转本身。它是同族词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to turn something upside down or change its order. It is often more technical and narrower than reverse.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物上下颠倒或改变次序。它常更技术化，范围也比 reverse 窄。

entries.definition: to reverse a decision or result, or to turn something over. It stresses the fall of what stood.
entries.definitionCN: 推翻决定或结果，或把某物翻倒。它强调原先立着的东西倒下。

entries.definition: to turn something over quickly with a short movement. It is physical and informal, not used for court rulings.
entries.definitionCN: 用短促动作快速翻转某物。它偏物理、偏口语，不用于法院裁决。

entries.definition: to cancel the effect of an action so that the previous state returns. It focuses on restoring the past, not on direction.
entries.definitionCN: 取消某个动作的效果，使之前的状态恢复。它聚焦于恢复过去，而不是方向。

entries.definition: the opposite fact or quality. It is the stative cousin of reverse: not the act of turning, but the state of being opposed.
entries.definitionCN: 相反的事实或性质。它是 reverse 的静态近亲：不是“转”的动作，而是“相对立”的状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb vertere, its large English family, and real modern compounds such as reverse gear.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁动词 vertere、它庞大的英语家族，以及 reverse gear 等真实现代复合词。

normal.en: re- 'back' + vertere 'turn' = turn back. The picture is a wheel that stops and spins the other way.
normal.cn: re-“回”+ vertere“转”= 转回去。画面是一个轮子停下，然后朝反方向转。

normal.en: The vertere family is everywhere: convert (turn together), divert (turn aside), invert (turn upside down), versus (turned against), verse (a turning of the line).
normal.cn: vertere 家族无处不在：convert（转到一起）、divert（转开）、invert（上下翻转）、versus（转向对立面）、verse（诗句的转折）。

normal.en: Reverse and inverse are not the same: reverse is about direction, inverse is about a reciprocal relation in maths.
normal.cn: reverse 与 inverse 不同：reverse 说的是方向，inverse 说的是数学上的互逆关系。

normal.en: In reverse is a fixed phrase: drive in reverse, count down in reverse, play the tape in reverse.
normal.cn: in reverse 是固定短语：倒车、倒着数、倒带播放。

normal.en: Reverse charge, reverse engineering and reverse a payment all take a forward path and run it backwards.
normal.cn: reverse charge、reverse engineering、reverse a payment，都是把一条向前的路径倒过来走。

abstract.en: Picture a gearbox: the engine still turns one way, but a small extra gear makes the output shaft turn the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象一个变速箱：发动机仍朝一个方向转，但一个额外的小齿轮让输出轴反着转。

abstract.en: A coin has two sides. Turn it and the other side faces you; that other side is the reverse.
abstract.cn: 硬币有两面。把它一翻，另一面朝向你；那一面就是 the reverse。

abstract.en: Any process can be run backwards: a film rewinds, a payment returns, a ruling is undone. Reverse is the direction switch.
abstract.cn: 任何过程都能倒着走：胶片倒回、付款退回、裁决撤销。reverse 就是那个方向开关。

examples.en: The new evidence reversed the conclusion of the first study.
examples.cn: 新证据推翻了第一项研究的结论。

examples.en: The driver reversed out of the space without hitting the wall.
examples.cn: 司机把车倒出车位，没有撞到墙。

examples.en: On the reverse of the medal, his name is engraved in small letters.
examples.cn: 奖牌的背面用小字刻着他的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞沃斯”：瑞沃斯一挂 R 挡，轮子倒着转，车往后走 → reverse 倒转、反向

root: 拉丁 revertere = re-（回）+ vertere（转），过去分词 reversus“转回去的”；核心是“把方向转到反面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of reverse, one motion: something is turned back on itself. A flow, a ruling, a car, a pair of roles, a phone bill, an engineering path, a payment, a list, or a coin can all face the other way.
sensesIntro.cn: reverse 的九个义项共有一个动作：某物被转回自身反面。水流、裁决、汽车、一对角色、电话账单、工程路径、一笔付款、一份列表或一枚硬币，都可以转向另一面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel is turned until it spins the opposite way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个轮子被转到相反的方向。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND ORDER: a flow or a list is turned around, so it runs from the other end.
branches.cn: 方向与次序：水流或列表被调转，于是从另一头开始。

branches.en: UNDOING: a ruling or a payment is sent back along the path it came, restoring the earlier state.
branches.cn: 撤销：裁决或付款沿原路退回，恢复先前的状态。

branches.en: VEHICLE: reverse gear makes the wheels turn opposite to the direction of travel.
branches.cn: 车辆：倒挡让车轮与行进方向相反地转动。

branches.en: TWO FACES: swapping roles is a half-turn, and the reverse is the side that faces you after it.
branches.cn: 两面：互换角色是转半圈；the reverse 就是转过来后面对你的那一面。

branches.en: BACKWARD PATH: a reverse-charge call and reverse engineering both follow a route from its end to its beginning.
branches.cn: 倒行的路径：对方付费电话与逆向工程，都是从终点走向起点。

intro.en: Reverse is re- plus vers-, the participial stem of vertere. The prefix is no longer separable in English; the productive forms are -al, -ible, -ibility and the negative ir-.
intro.cn: reverse 是 re- 加 vers-（vertere 的分词词干）。这个前缀在英语里已不能单独拆用；能产的形式是 -al、-ible、-ibility 以及否定前缀 ir-。

latinIntro.en: Vertere 'to turn' is one of the most productive Latin verbs in English. Its compounds change the direction of the turn: back, aside, together, upside down.
latinIntro.cn: vertere“转”是英语中能产性最强的拉丁动词之一。它的复合词改变“转”的方向：转回、转开、转到一起、上下翻转。

items.meaning: the act of reversing, or a change to the opposite
items.meaningCN: 逆转；反转；撤销（-al 构成行为名词）
items.example: The court's reversal of the ban surprised everyone.
items.exampleCN: 法院撤销禁令，令所有人意外。

items.meaning: able to be reversed, or able to be worn both ways
items.meaningCN: 可逆的；可翻转的；正反两穿的（-ible 表示能够）
items.example: The damage to the wetland is not reversible.
items.exampleCN: 对湿地的破坏是不可逆的。

items.meaning: impossible to reverse or undo
items.meaningCN: 不可逆的；无法挽回的（ir- 表否定）
items.example: The chemical reaction is irreversible once it starts.
items.exampleCN: 这个化学反应一旦开始便不可逆。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to be reversed
items.meaningCN: 可逆性（-ity 构成抽象名词）
items.example: Engineers tested the reversibility of the pump.
items.exampleCN: 工程师测试了这台泵的可逆性。

items.meaning: in a way that can be reversed
items.meaningCN: 可逆地；可翻转地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The protein binds reversibly to the enzyme.
items.exampleCN: 这种蛋白质与酶可逆地结合。

items.meaning: a mechanism that reverses direction, such as a thrust reverser
items.meaningCN: 反转装置；换向器（如飞机反推装置）
items.example: The pilot deployed the thrust reverser on landing.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员在着陆时打开了反推装置。

items.meaning: to turn upside down or change the order of
items.meaningCN: 上下颠倒；使反转（in- + 转）
items.example: Invert the bowl so the water runs out.
items.exampleCN: 把碗倒扣过来，让水流出去。

items.meaning: to change something into another form or use
items.meaningCN: 转变；转换（con- + 转，即“整个转过来”）
items.example: They converted the old factory into apartments.
items.exampleCN: 他们把老工厂改造成了公寓。

items.meaning: to turn something aside from its course
items.meaningCN: 使转向；转移（di-“偏离”+ 转）
items.example: Traffic was diverted around the accident.
items.exampleCN: 车辆被引导绕开事故地点。

definition_zh: 修改；修订；校正；调整；改变（看法）；（英式）复习
definition_en: to look at something again and change or improve it, to change an opinion, estimate, or plan, or to study for an examination
core_image: 再看一眼：把写好的东西重新摊开在眼前，逐行重看并改动
scene: She revised the manuscript in red ink before sending it to the editor.
sceneCN: 这里 revise 是「修改文稿」（第 1 个义项：重新审视并改写文字）；句意：寄给编辑之前，她用红笔修改了手稿。图中可辨识物件：手稿、红笔、批注箭头、咖啡杯、台灯。

derivatives.zh: 修改；修订；修订稿；（英式）复习

senses.title: Look again and change the text
senses.titleCN: 重新审视并改写文字
senses.definition: to read a piece of writing again and make changes to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 重新阅读一份文字并作出改动以改进它
senses.example: She revised the draft three times before it was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 这份草稿她改了三遍才被接受。
senses.why: Latin revisere is re- 'again' plus visere 'to look'. The text is seen a second time, and that second look produces the changes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revisere 是 re-“再”加 visere“看”。文字被第二次看见，正是这第二眼带来了改动。

senses.title: Adjust a plan or estimate
senses.titleCN: 调整计划或估算
senses.definition: to change a plan, schedule, or estimate because the situation has changed
senses.definitionCN: 因情况变化而改变计划、日程或估算
senses.example: We revised the schedule after the supplier announced a delay.
senses.exampleCN: 供应商宣布延期后，我们调整了日程。
senses.why: A plan is looked at again against new facts. The second look shows the mismatch, so the plan is re-seen and rewritten.
senses.whyCN: 计划被拿去对照新事实再看一遍。第二眼看出不匹配，于是计划被重新审视并改写。

senses.title: Change your opinion
senses.titleCN: 改变看法
senses.definition: to change a belief or judgment after considering new information
senses.definitionCN: 在考虑新信息之后改变信念或判断
senses.example: He revised his opinion of the plan after reading the report.
senses.exampleCN: 读完报告后，他改变了对这个计划的看法。
senses.why: An opinion is a way of seeing. To revise it is to look at the same matter again and let the new view replace the old one.
senses.whyCN: 看法就是一种“看”的方式。revise 看法，就是把同一件事再看一遍，让新的视角取代旧的。

senses.title: A revision: the act or result of re-seeing
senses.titleCN: 修订：重看的行为或结果
senses.definition: the process of revising, or a changed version produced by it
senses.definitionCN: 修订的过程，或由此产生的改动版本
senses.example: The revision took two weeks and changed the ending.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修订花了两周，改掉了结尾。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun: each act of looking again leaves a trace, and that trace is a revision.
senses.whyCN: 动词名词化：每一次“再看”都会留下痕迹，这个痕迹就是 revision。

senses.title: British: study for an exam
senses.titleCN: 英式：复习备考
senses.definition: in British English, to study your notes and lessons again before an examination
senses.definitionCN: 在英式英语中，考试前把笔记和课程再学一遍
senses.example: She revised all night before the history exam.
senses.exampleCN: 历史考试前，她复习了一整夜。
senses.why: The same second look, applied to schoolwork: the notes are seen again so that they stay in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 还是同一个“再看”，只是用在功课上：笔记被再看一遍，以便留在脑中。

senses.title: Revise a classification: taxonomic revision
senses.titleCN: 修订分类：生物分类修订
senses.definition: in biology, to re-examine a group of organisms and change its classification or description
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中重新检视一类生物，改变其分类或描述
senses.example: The genus was revised after new specimens were found.
senses.exampleCN: 发现新标本后，该属的分类被修订了。
senses.why: Scientists look at the specimens again with better evidence. The re-seeing reorganises the group, so revision becomes a formal scientific act.
senses.whyCN: 科学家带着更好的证据再看一遍标本。这第二眼重新组织了类群，于是 revision 成为正式的科学行为。

senses.title: Revise figures: change a number
senses.titleCN: 修正数字：上调或下调
senses.definition: to change a statistic or figure, usually after new data or a correction
senses.definitionCN: 更改统计数据或数字，通常因新数据或更正
senses.example: The growth figure was revised down from 2.1% to 1.8%.
senses.exampleCN: 增长数字从 2.1% 下调至 1.8%。
senses.why: The number is looked at again and found to be wrong or out of date. Revision is the corrected second reading.
senses.whyCN: 数字被再看一遍，发现错了或过时了。revise 就是更正后的第二次读数。

senses.title: Revised edition: the book seen again
senses.titleCN: 修订版：重新看过的书
senses.definition: a new published version of a book or standard that has been changed and updated
senses.definitionCN: 经过修改和更新后重新出版的书籍或标准版本
senses.example: The revised edition adds two chapters on climate data.
senses.exampleCN: 修订版增加了两章关于气候数据的内容。
senses.why: The whole book is looked over again and reissued. The second look is now printed and sold as an edition.
senses.whyCN: 整本书被重新审视并再次出版。这第二眼如今被印成书、作为版本出售。

senses.title: Correct errors: fix what the second look finds
senses.titleCN: 校正错误：改掉第二眼发现的问题
senses.definition: to correct mistakes in a text, calculation, or record
senses.definitionCN: 改正文字、计算或记录中的错误
senses.example: Revise the essay for spelling and grammar before you submit it.
senses.exampleCN: 提交前请校正文章的拼写和语法。
senses.why: The first reading misses errors; the second look catches them. Correction is the practical purpose of re-seeing.
senses.whyCN: 第一遍读会漏掉错误，第二眼才抓住它们。校正正是“再看”的实际目的。

intro.en: Revise entered English in the 1560s from Latin revisere 'look at again'. Dates are approximate; the link of videre to PIE *weid- 'see, know' is generally accepted.
intro.cn: revise 于 16 世纪 60 年代从拉丁语 revisere“再看”进入英语。年代为大致估计；videre 与原始印欧语 *weid-“看见、知道”的联系为一般接受之说。

items.en: First recorded in English with the sense 'to look at again, review, examine again', especially for correction.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录为“再看、复审、重新检查”，尤用于校正。

items.en: From Latin revisere 'to look back at, visit again, review', built from re- 'again' and visere, a frequentative form of videre 'to see'.
items.cn: 来自拉丁语 revisere“回看、重访、复审”，由 re-“再”与 visere 构成，后者是 videre“看”的反复形式。

items.en: Videre 'to see' is the source of vision, visible, video, evident and supervise. Visere adds the idea of looking repeatedly or attentively.
items.cn: videre“看”是 vision、visible、video、evident、supervise 的来源。visere 则加上“反复看、仔细看”的意思。

items.en: Videre is generally traced to PIE *weid- 'to see, know', which also underlies wit and wise. Seeing and knowing were one idea in the root.
items.cn: videre 一般认为可追溯到原始印欧语 *weid-“看见、知道”，wit 与 wise 也出自这个词根。在词根层面，“看见”与“知道”是同一个想法。

items.en: The British school sense 'study for an examination' is generally dated to the 19c. and remains chiefly British; American English prefers study or review.
items.cn: 英式“复习备考”义一般认为始于 19 世纪，至今主要限于英式英语；美式英语更常用 study 或 review。

items.en: Modern English revises drafts, plans, estimates, opinions and classifications, and speaks of a revised edition. The noun revision covers both the act and the result.
items.cn: 现代英语会 revise 草稿、计划、估算、看法和分类，也会说 revised edition。名词 revision 同时指行为与结果。

note.en: The first group is formal: revive is the closest trap, devise shares the ending, and revision is the derived noun. The second group is semantic: words for changing a text or a plan.
note.cn: 第一组看词形：revive 是最接近的陷阱，devise 共享词尾，revision 是派生名词。第二组看词义：表示“改动文字或计划”的词。

entries.definition: to bring something back to life or use. Its root is vivere 'to live', not videre 'to see', so it means 're-live', not 're-see'.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物复活或重新流行。它的词根是 vivere“活”，不是 videre“看”，所以意思是“重新活过来”，而非“重新看”。

entries.definition: to invent or plan something. It comes from Old French deviser 'to divide, arrange', a different root despite the shared -vise ending.
entries.definitionCN: 发明或设计某物。它来自古法语 deviser“划分、安排”，虽然词尾同为 -vise，词源却不同。

entries.definition: the noun from revise: the act of revising or the changed version. It is the same family, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: revise 派生的名词：修订行为或修订后的版本。它是同族词，不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: to change a document, law, or agreement formally. It is narrower and more official than revise.
entries.definitionCN: 正式修改文件、法律或协议。它比 revise 更窄、更官方。

entries.definition: to prepare text for publication by correcting, cutting, or rearranging it. It focuses on the finished text rather than a second look.
entries.definitionCN: 通过改正、删减或调整来准备出版文本。它聚焦于成品文本，而非“再看”这个动作。

entries.definition: to change something slightly, often to suit a purpose. It usually implies a smaller change than revise.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物，常为适应某目的。它通常暗示比 revise 更小的改动。

entries.definition: to look at something again to judge or check it. It may involve no change at all, while revise normally does.
entries.definitionCN: 重新查看某物以评判或检查。它可能完全不改动，而 revise 通常会改。

entries.definition: to change something substantially, often by doing much of it again. It is stronger than revise.
entries.definitionCN: 大幅改动某物，常需重做大部分内容。它比 revise 语气更强。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin revisere, the real videre family, and real British and publishing uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁 revisere、真实的 videre 家族，以及真实的英式与出版用法。

normal.en: re- 'again' + visere 'look' = look again. Revise is not 'change' first; it is 'see again' first, and the change follows.
normal.cn: re-“再”+ visere“看”= 再看。revise 的第一步不是“改”，而是“再看”，改动是看的结果。

normal.en: The videre family is about seeing: vision, visible, video, evident, supervise. Revision is a second seeing of the same text.
normal.cn: videre 家族都与“看”有关：vision、visible、video、evident、supervise。revision 就是对同一文本的第二次看。

normal.en: In British schools you revise for an exam; in American English you would usually say study for or review for an exam.
normal.cn: 英式学校里说 revise for an exam；美式英语通常说 study for 或 review for an exam。

normal.en: A revised edition is a book that has been looked over again and reissued, not a different book.
normal.cn: revised edition 是重新审看后再次出版的书，而不是另一本书。

normal.en: Revise figures is the newsroom phrase for corrected numbers: first reported, then looked at again.
normal.cn: revise figures 是新闻编辑室对“更正数字”的说法：先报出，再重新核对。

abstract.en: Picture a manuscript under a lamp. The first reading flows forward; the second reading stops at each line, pen in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象台灯下的一份手稿。第一遍顺流读下去；第二遍在每一行停下，手里握着笔。

abstract.en: The same second look can fall on a sentence, an estimate, an opinion, a species, or a whole edition.
abstract.cn: 同一个“第二眼”可以落在句子上、估算上、看法上、物种上，或整个版本上。

abstract.en: Revision is proof that seeing again is an action: the text is not merely re-read, it is re-made.
abstract.cn: revision 证明“再看”是一种行动：文本不只是被重读，而是被重做。

examples.en: The committee revised the budget after the new cost estimates arrived.
examples.cn: 新的成本估算到达后，委员会修订了预算。

examples.en: She revised her first impression once she heard his side of the story.
examples.cn: 听完他这一方的说法后，她改变了自己的第一印象。

examples.en: British students often revise in the library until midnight.
examples.cn: 英国学生常常在图书馆复习到半夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞歪兹”：瑞把歪掉的字重新看一遍、一个个改直 → revise 修改、修订

root: 拉丁 revisere = re-（再）+ visere（反复看，来自 videre“看”），字面“再看一遍”，核心是“重看之后作出改动”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of revise, one habit: look at the same thing a second time and change it. The object may be a text, a plan, an opinion, a revision itself, exam notes, a species, a number, an edition, or an error.
sensesIntro.cn: revise 的九个义项共有一个习惯：把同一件事再看一遍，然后改动它。对象可以是文本、计划、看法、修订本身、考试笔记、物种、数字、版本或一个错误。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same text is laid out again and read line by line with a pen in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一份文本再次摊开，握着笔逐行重读。

branches.en: TEXT AND ERROR: a second reading of writing finds mistakes and produces a corrected text.
branches.cn: 文本与错误：对文字的第二次阅读发现错误，产出校正后的文本。

branches.en: PLANS AND NUMBERS: a schedule or a statistic is checked against new facts and changed.
branches.cn: 计划与数字：日程或统计被对照新事实重新核对并更改。

branches.en: OPINION: a belief is a way of seeing, so a new look can replace the old view.
branches.cn: 看法：信念是一种“看”的方式，因此新的眼光可以取代旧视角。

branches.en: STUDY AND SCIENCE: exam notes and museum specimens are both looked at again for mastery or classification.
branches.cn: 学习与科学：考试笔记与博物馆标本都被重新检视，目的分别是掌握与分类。

branches.en: PRODUCT: the act of re-seeing leaves a revision, and a book re-seen becomes a revised edition.
branches.cn: 成品：重看的行为留下一个 revision；一本被重看的书成为 revised edition。

intro.en: Revise is Latin re- plus the stem -vise, from videre. The prefix is not separable in English; the productive suffixes are -ion, -er, -ory, -able and the negative un-.
intro.cn: revise 是拉丁语 re- 加来自 videre 的词干 -vise。前缀在英语里不能单独拆用；能产的后缀是 -ion、-er、-ory、-able 以及否定前缀 un-。

latinIntro.en: Videre 'to see' is one of the great Latin roots. Re- adds 'again', so re-seeing is built into the word rather than added by context.
latinIntro.cn: videre“看”是最重要的拉丁词根之一。re- 加上“再”，所以“重看”是词本身自带的，不是语境补出来的。

items.meaning: the act of revising, or a revised version
items.meaningCN: 修订；修订稿；复习（-ion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The final revision removed three whole paragraphs.
items.exampleCN: 最后一次修订删掉了整整三段。

items.meaning: a person who revises a text or a version
items.meaningCN: 修改者；校订者（-er 表示做该动作的人）
items.example: The reviser caught a date error on page forty.
items.exampleCN: 校订者在第四十页发现了一个日期错误。

items.meaning: having the power or function of revising
items.meaningCN: 修订的；有修改权的（-ory 表示功能）
items.example: The committee has a revisory role in the process.
items.exampleCN: 该委员会在这一流程中承担修订职能。

items.meaning: able to be revised
items.meaningCN: 可修订的；可修改的（-able 表示能够）
items.example: The treaty is revisable after ten years.
items.exampleCN: 该条约十年后可以修订。

items.meaning: not yet changed or corrected
items.meaningCN: 未修订的；未校订的（un- 表否定）
items.example: The unrevised manuscript still contains the old figures.
items.exampleCN: 未修订的手稿里仍是旧数字。

items.meaning: having been looked over and changed
items.meaningCN: 修订过的；修改后的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The revised text is shorter and clearer.
items.exampleCN: 修订后的文本更短、更清楚。

items.meaning: in the process of revising
items.meaningCN: 正在修订（-ing 构成进行体）
items.example: She spent the weekend revising the report.
items.exampleCN: 她整个周末都在修订报告。

items.meaning: to watch over work or people to make sure it is done correctly
items.meaningCN: 监督；管理（super-“在上”+ 看，即“从上往下看”）
items.example: A senior editor supervises the new writers.
items.exampleCN: 一位资深编辑指导这些新作者。

items.meaning: relating to seeing or sight
items.meaningCN: 视觉的；与看有关的（-ual 构成形容词）
items.example: The report relies on visual evidence, not just numbers.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告依赖视觉证据，而不只是数字。

latinEntries.meaning: to look at again, revisit, review

definition_zh: 革命；彻底变革；旋转；一圈；（天体的）公转
definition_en: a complete change in a political or social order, a major change in ideas or methods, or one full turn around a centre
core_image: 一只轮子转满一整圈：旧秩序被卷到下面，新秩序在起点上立起来
scene: At dawn the crowd pulls down the old regime's portrait while a freshly printed proclamation of revolution flutters across the square.
sceneCN: 这里 revolution 是「政治革命」（第 1 个义项：推翻旧政权的整体变革）；句意：黎明时分，人群拉下旧政权的画像，一张刚印好的革命宣言飘过广场。图中可辨识物件：旧政权画像、宣言纸张、旗杆、广场上的人群。

derivatives.zh: 革命的；革命性的；革命者
使发生根本变革；彻底改变

senses.title: Political revolution: the old order rolled back
senses.titleCN: 政治革命：旧秩序被卷翻
senses.definition: the overthrow of a government or social order by a mass movement, followed by a new order
senses.definitionCN: 由群众运动推翻政府或社会秩序，并建立新秩序
senses.example: The revolution of 1789 redrew the political map of Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 1789 年的革命重画了欧洲的政治地图。
senses.why: Latin revolvere means 'to roll back'. A political revolution is the old order rolled back on itself until it topples, and the new order settles where the wheel stops.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 revolvere 意为“滚回去”。政治革命就是把旧秩序向后卷，直到它翻倒，而新秩序落在轮子停住的位置。

senses.title: Wholesale change: a whole way of doing something turns over
senses.titleCN: 彻底变革：做事的整套方式翻了个面
senses.definition: a very great change in the way something is done, thought about, or organized
senses.definitionCN: 某事的做法、看法或组织方式发生的巨大变化
senses.example: The internet brought a revolution in how ordinary people shop.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网给普通人的购物方式带来了一场彻底变革。
senses.why: The turn here is not a small adjustment but a full rotation: the previous method ends up underneath and a different method faces up.
senses.whyCN: 这里的转动不是小调整，而是整整一圈：旧方法被转到下面，另一种方法朝上。

senses.title: Orbital or mechanical turning around a centre
senses.titleCN: 绕中心的公转或机械旋转
senses.definition: the movement of a body around a centre or axis, as of a planet or a machine part
senses.definitionCN: 天体或机械部件绕中心或轴的运动
senses.example: One revolution of the moon around Earth takes about 27 days.
senses.exampleCN: 月球绕地球公转一圈约需 27 天。
senses.why: This is the literal picture: volvere is 'to roll', and a body rolling around a fixed centre traces the circle that the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的画面：volvere 就是“滚动”，一个绕固定中心滚动的物体画出的圆，正是这个词所指的东西。

senses.title: Named industrial transformation
senses.titleCN: 被命名的工业变革
senses.definition: a historical period in which production, transport or energy is rebuilt on a new technical basis
senses.definitionCN: 生产、运输或能源以新技术基础重建的历史时期
senses.example: The Industrial Revolution moved work from cottages into factories.
senses.exampleCN: 工业革命把劳动从家庭作坊搬进了工厂。
senses.why: The full turn is applied to an entire economy: the workshop order rolls over and the factory order rises in its place, so the era itself takes the name.
senses.whyCN: 整整一圈的转动被用在整个经济上：作坊秩序被卷过去，工厂秩序在原处升起，于是整个时代获得了这个名字。

senses.title: One complete turn: back to the starting point
senses.titleCN: 完整的一圈：回到起点
senses.definition: a single movement through 360 degrees, ending where it began
senses.definitionCN: 转过 360 度、回到起点的单次运动
senses.example: The wheel makes one revolution per second.
senses.exampleCN: 这个轮子每秒转一圈。
senses.why: re- means 'again' and volvere means 'roll': a roll that comes round again to its own beginning. This is the measured core of the word.
senses.whyCN: re- 意为“再次”，volvere 意为“滚动”：一次又滚回自己起点的滚动。这就是这个词最可度量的核心。

senses.title: Scientific revolution: the accepted model is replaced
senses.titleCN: 科学革命：公认的模型被替换
senses.definition: a shift in which the dominant framework of a science is replaced by a different one
senses.definitionCN: 某一科学的主导框架被另一套框架取代的转变
senses.example: The Scientific Revolution replaced an Earth-centred cosmos with a sun-centred one.
senses.exampleCN: 科学革命用日心宇宙取代了地心宇宙。
senses.why: A paradigm is a position on the wheel. When the wheel turns all the way, the old model is no longer facing up and the new model defines what counts as truth.
senses.whyCN: 范式就是轮子上的一个位置。轮子转满一圈后，旧模型不再朝上，新模型决定了什么算作真理。

senses.title: Cultural revolution: values and habits overturned
senses.titleCN: 文化革命：价值与习俗被掀翻
senses.definition: a deep and rapid change in the values, art, or daily habits of a society
senses.definitionCN: 社会价值、艺术或日常习惯的深刻而迅速的变化
senses.example: A cultural revolution in music followed the spread of the electric guitar.
senses.exampleCN: 电吉他的普及带来了一场音乐文化革命。
senses.why: The wheel of taste turns a full circle: what the older generation treated as proper is rolled away, and what was marginal becomes the centre.
senses.whyCN: 品味的轮子转满一圈：上一代人视为得体的东西被卷走，原本边缘的东西变成了中心。

senses.title: Fashion revolution: the silhouette turns over
senses.titleCN: 时尚剧变：轮廓整个翻面
senses.definition: a sudden, complete change in dress, design, or style
senses.definitionCN: 服装、设计或风格突然而彻底的变化
senses.example: The miniskirt was a revolution in 1960s fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 迷你裙是 20 世纪 60 年代时尚界的一场革命。
senses.why: Hemlines roll up and the previous look is turned under. The change is total rather than gradual, which is why the word fits a single season of style.
senses.whyCN: 裙摆向上卷，旧造型被转到下面。变化是彻底的而不是渐进的，所以这个词也适用于一个季节内的风格翻转。

senses.title: Revolution against: organized resistance to a power
senses.titleCN: 对……的反抗：有组织地对抗权力
senses.definition: in the phrase revolution against, an organized movement refusing the authority of a ruler or system
senses.definitionCN: 用于 revolution against，指拒绝统治者或制度权威的有组织运动
senses.example: The revolution against colonial rule lasted almost a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这场反对殖民统治的革命持续了近十年。
senses.why: The related verb revolt came through Italian rivoltare 'to turn over', from the same Latin revolvere. Turning against an authority is still the picture of a wheel rolled the other way.
senses.whyCN: 相关动词 revolt 经意大利语 rivoltare“翻转”而来，同出拉丁语 revolvere。转而对抗权威，仍然是轮子向另一方向滚动的画面。

intro.en: Revolution is a Latin rolling word that entered English through French. The dates are approximate; the deep Indo-European root is given only as generally accepted.
intro.cn: revolution 是一个经法语进入英语的拉丁“滚动”词。年代为大致估计；最深的印欧词根只按一般说法给出。

items.en: First recorded in English in the late 14c. meaning 'a turning around, rotation', and also 'a course, a round of time'.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“转动、旋转”，也指“历程、一段时间”。

items.en: Borrowed from Old French révolution (13c.), which already had the sense of a turning or a course of events.
items.cn: 借自古法语 révolution（13 世纪），当时已表示“转动”或“事件的过程”。

items.en: Old French came from Late Latin revolutionem (nominative revolutio), a noun of action meaning 'a rolling back, a revolving'.
items.cn: 古法语来自晚期拉丁语 revolutionem（主格 revolutio），这是一个动作名词，意为“滚回、旋转”。

items.en: The Late Latin noun comes from Latin revolvere 'to roll back, unroll, revolve', formed from re- 'back, again' + volvere 'to roll'.
items.cn: 这个晚期拉丁名词来自拉丁语 revolvere“滚回、展开、旋转”，由 re-“回、再”+ volvere“滚动”构成。

items.en: The political sense 'overthrow of a government' is recorded from the 17c., first attached to the English Revolution and later fixed by the French Revolution of 1789.
items.cn: “推翻政府”的政治义自 17 世纪有记录，最早用于英国革命，后来由 1789 年法国大革命固定下来。

items.en: Modern English keeps all three layers: a physical turn, a wholesale change, and a named historical upheaval. Revolve, revolt, evolution and devolve are close relatives.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了三层含义：物理旋转、彻底变革、被命名的历史剧变。revolve、revolt、evolution、devolve 都是近亲。

note.en: The first group checks sound and spelling; the second compares meaning. A shared Latin root does not make two words interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组检查读音与拼写，第二组比较词义。共享拉丁词根并不意味着两个词可以互换。

entries.definition: gradual development, especially the change of living things over generations. It uses the same volvere 'roll' root, but e- means 'out': an unfolding rather than a full turn.
entries.definitionCN: 渐进发展，尤指生物世代演变。它同用 volvere“滚动”词根，但 e- 意为“向外”：是展开，而不是转满一圈。

entries.definition: a strong feeling of disgust. It looks like revolution but comes from revellere 'to pull away', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的厌恶。它看起来像 revolution，却来自 revellere“拉开”，词根不同。

entries.definition: a surprising disclosure of something hidden. It comes from revelare 'to unveil', not from rolling.
entries.definitionCN: 对隐藏之事的惊人揭露。它来自 revelare“揭开面纱”，与“滚动”无关。

entries.definition: an armed protest against a government, usually local and often unsuccessful. Revolution is larger and aims at replacing the order itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对政府的武装反抗，通常是地方性的且往往失败。revolution 规模更大，目标是替换秩序本身。

entries.definition: a refusal to accept authority, which may be smaller than a revolution and need not succeed. It can also be emotional, as in a revolt against convention.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝接受权威，规模可能小于 revolution，也不一定成功。它还可指情绪上的反叛，如对成规的反感。

entries.definition: a great and disruptive change, often social or personal. It stresses disturbance rather than a completed new order.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大而破坏性的变化，常指社会或个人层面。它强调动荡，而不是已经建成的新秩序。

entries.definition: a complete change in form or character. It is neutral and does not imply political overthrow.
entries.definitionCN: 形式或性质的彻底改变。它是中性的，不暗示政治推翻。

entries.definition: the act of turning around an axis. It covers only the mechanical sense of revolution and carries no idea of social change.
entries.definitionCN: 绕轴转动的动作。它只覆盖 revolution 的机械义，不带有社会变革的含义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use real word parts and real historical names, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的构词成分和真实的历史名称，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + volvere 'roll': a revolution is a roll that comes all the way round to its own starting point.
normal.cn: re-“再”+ volvere“滚”：revolution 就是滚回自己起点的一整圈。

normal.en: The same volvere family gives revolve, evolution, devolve and involvement: all of them are 'rolling' words.
normal.cn: 同一个 volvere 家族还给出 revolve、evolution、devolve、involvement：它们都是“滚动”词。

normal.en: In astronomy one revolution is one full orbit, which is why the moon's revolution can be counted in days.
normal.cn: 在天文学里，一次 revolution 就是一整圈轨道，所以月球的公转可以用天数来计。

normal.en: Industrial Revolution and Scientific Revolution are capitalised era names: a whole period rolled over at once.
normal.cn: Industrial Revolution 与 Scientific Revolution 是带大写的时代名称：整个时期一次性翻了过去。

normal.en: To revolutionize a field is to make it change as if the wheel had turned a full circle and nothing was left facing up in the old position.
normal.cn: revolutionize 某个领域，就是让它像轮子转满一圈那样改变，旧位置上再没有东西朝上。

abstract.en: Picture a giant wheel painted with the old order. It turns 360 degrees, and the painted face lands flat on the ground while a clean face comes up.
abstract.cn: 想象一只画着旧秩序的巨大轮子。它转满 360 度，画着旧秩序的那面拍在地上，干净的一面翻上来。

abstract.en: A small correction is reform; a full revolution puts a different order in the same place, which is why the word can name both a wheel and a century.
abstract.cn: 小修小补是改革；完整的 revolution 把另一种秩序放到同一个位置上，所以这个词既能指轮子，也能指一个世纪。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps the circle: politics, industry, science, culture, fashion, and a wheel on an axle all turn until the old side is down.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留这个圆：政治、工业、科学、文化、时尚，以及轴上的轮子，都转到旧的一面朝下为止。

examples.en: The revolution began with a march and ended with a new constitution.
examples.cn: 这场革命从一场游行开始，以一部新宪法结束。

examples.en: Bar codes caused a revolution in how shops track their stock.
examples.cn: 条形码让商店追踪库存的方式发生了彻底变革。

examples.en: The satellite completes one revolution around the planet every ninety minutes.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星每九十分钟绕行星一圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: “热窝路迅”——热窝里的那条路迅速掉头转了一圈 → revolution 革命、彻底转向

root: 拉丁 revolvere“滚回、转回”（re-“回、再”+ volvere“滚动”）；核心是“转满一圈，旧位置被翻到下面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of revolution, all built on one circle: something rolls around a centre, completes the turn, and what was on top is now underneath.
sensesIntro.cn: revolution 的九个义项都建立在一个圆上：某物绕中心滚动，转满一圈，原本在上面的东西现在到了下面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wheel rolls a full circle, carrying the old order away and leaving a new one where it began.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只轮子转满一圈，把旧秩序卷走，并在起点留下新秩序。

branches.en: POLITICAL OVERTHROW: a government or ruling power is rolled back and resistance turns against it.
branches.cn: 政治推翻：政府或统治权力被卷翻，反抗转而针对它。

branches.en: WHOLESALE CHANGE: methods, values and culture turn over completely, not just at the edges.
branches.cn: 彻底变革：方法、价值与文化整体翻面，而不只是边角修补。

branches.en: PHYSICAL ROTATION: the literal circle of an orbit or a wheel, measured as one full 360-degree turn.
branches.cn: 物理旋转：轨道或轮子的字面圆圈，以整整 360 度的一圈来计量。

branches.en: NAMED ERA SHIFTS: industry and science each get a capitalised revolution when their whole framework is rebuilt.
branches.cn: 被命名的时代转折：工业与科学在整体框架重建时各自获得一个大写的 revolution。

branches.en: STYLE OVERTURNED: fashion turns a full circle in a season, and the previous silhouette is left face-down.
branches.cn: 风格翻面：时尚在一季内转满一圈，上一个轮廓被留在下面。

intro.en: Revolution is built from the Latin prefix re- and the verb volvere, then finished with the noun suffix -ion. English adds its own suffixes to the completed word.
intro.cn: revolution 由拉丁前缀 re- 与动词 volvere 构成，再加名词后缀 -ion 完成。英语则在成品词上继续加自己的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere 'to roll' is a productive root: its compounds describe rolling back, out, down and in, and English inherited several of them.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere“滚动”是一个能产的词根：它的复合词分别表示向后、向外、向下、向内滚，英语继承了好几个。

items.meaning: a full turn; a complete change of order
items.meaningCN: 一整圈转动；秩序的彻底改变（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The revolution changed the country for a generation.
items.exampleCN: 这场革命影响了这个国家一代人。

items.meaning: relating to a revolution; a person who takes part in one
items.meaningCN: 革命的；革命性的；革命者（-ary 表示“与……相关”）
items.example: The invention had a revolutionary effect on medicine.
items.exampleCN: 这项发明对医学产生了革命性的影响。

items.meaning: to change something completely
items.meaningCN: 使彻底变革（-ize 表示“使成为”）
items.example: Streaming revolutionized the music business.
items.exampleCN: 流媒体彻底改变了音乐产业。

items.meaning: a person who works for a revolution
items.meaningCN: 革命者；革命家（-ist 表示“从事……的人”）
items.example: The revolutionist spent years in exile.
items.exampleCN: 这位革命者流亡多年。

items.meaning: to turn around a centre
items.meaningCN: 旋转；绕转（re-“再、回”+ volvere“滚”）
items.example: The earth revolves around the sun.
items.exampleCN: 地球绕太阳公转。

items.meaning: a handgun with a revolving cylinder
items.meaningCN: 左轮手枪（revolve + -er，指会转动的物件）
items.example: The cylinder of a revolver turns with each shot.
items.exampleCN: 左轮手枪的弹巢每开一枪就转一格。

items.meaning: a gradual unfolding or development
items.meaningCN: 演化；渐进展开（e-“向外”+ volvere“滚”+ -ion）
items.example: Evolution unfolds over many generations.
items.exampleCN: 演化在许多世代中逐步展开。

items.meaning: to pass power or duty down to another
items.meaningCN: 下放（权力）；移交（de-“向下”+ volvere“滚”）
items.example: The central office devolved budget control to the regions.
items.exampleCN: 中央机构把预算控制权下放给各地区。

items.meaning: the state of being wrapped up in something
items.meaningCN: 卷入；参与（in-“向内”+ volvere“卷”+ -ment）
items.example: Her involvement in the project lasted two years.
items.exampleCN: 她参与这个项目持续了两年。

items.meaning: speaking easily and at length, like words rolling out
items.meaningCN: 滔滔不绝的（volvere + -ble，像话语滚出来一样）
items.example: The voluble guide talked for the whole walk.
items.exampleCN: 这位健谈的向导一路说个不停。

latinEntries.meaning: to roll back, unroll, turn around

definition_zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；死板的；严格的；（价格、工资）固定的；刚性的
definition_en: stiff and hard to bend; unwilling or unable to change; fixed and not adjustable
core_image: 一根绷得笔直、被拉紧绑住的杆：既不弯，也不肯动
scene: On the bridge, a worker leans against a rigid steel beam that will not bend even under the full load.
sceneCN: 这里 rigid 是「坚硬不可弯」（第 1 个义项：硬得无法弯曲）；句意：桥上，一名工人靠在一根即使在满载下也不弯的刚性钢梁上。图中可辨识物件：钢梁、安全帽、桥梁支架、承重标记。

pos.zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；不能弯曲的
固定的；刚性的（价格、工资、结构）

collocations.zh: 刚性价格；不易变动的价格

senses.title: Physically stiff: a thing that will not bend
senses.titleCN: 物理上坚硬：弯不动的物体
senses.definition: hard and stiff, so that it cannot be bent or easily deformed
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬而僵直，无法弯曲或轻易变形
senses.example: The frame is made of rigid aluminium.
senses.exampleCN: 这个框架由刚性铝材制成。
senses.why: Latin rigidus meant 'stiff, hard', from rigere 'to be stiff'. The first picture is a bar held in one shape, with no joint to give way.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rigidus 意为“僵直、坚硬”，来自 rigere“变僵直”。最初的画面是一根保持单一形状的杆，没有可以退让的关节。

senses.title: A rigid person: opinions that will not bend
senses.titleCN: 死板的人：观点不肯弯
senses.definition: unwilling to change one's opinions, habits, or plans
senses.definitionCN: 不愿改变观点、习惯或计划
senses.example: He is too rigid to accept a different approach.
senses.exampleCN: 他太死板，接受不了另一种做法。
senses.why: Stiffness moves from the body to the mind: a rigid person has no mental joint, so a new idea cannot make the old position give way.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬从身体转到心智：死板的人没有“心智关节”，新想法无法让旧立场让开。

senses.title: Rigid prices or wages: values that do not move
senses.titleCN: 刚性价格或工资：不动的数值
senses.definition: in economics, prices or wages that stay fixed instead of adjusting to supply and demand
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中不随供求调整、保持固定的价格或工资
senses.example: Rigid wages can keep unemployment high during a slump.
senses.exampleCN: 在经济低迷时，刚性工资可能使失业率居高不下。
senses.why: A price is a position on a scale. When it is rigid, that position is welded in place and cannot slide with the market.
senses.whyCN: 价格是刻度上的一个位置。当它是 rigid 时，这个位置被焊死，无法随市场滑动。

senses.title: Rigid structure: a frame that keeps its shape
senses.titleCN: 刚性结构：保持形状的框架
senses.definition: in engineering, a structure that carries loads without changing shape
senses.definitionCN: 工程学中承受荷载而形状不变的构造
senses.example: A rigid steel frame kept the roof from twisting in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 刚性钢架使屋顶在风中不致扭转。
senses.why: Here the stiffness is useful: the whole frame behaves like one solid piece, so every load is spread instead of bending one joint.
senses.whyCN: 这里的僵直是有用的：整个框架像一整块固体，荷载被分散，而不是让某个接点弯曲。

senses.title: Rigid body: the physicist's ideal object
