senses.titleCN: 刚体：物理学家的理想物体
senses.definition: in physics, an ideal body in which the distance between any two points never changes
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中任意两点距离永不改变的理想物体
senses.example: A rigid body can rotate but cannot be squashed.
senses.exampleCN: 刚体可以旋转，但不会被压扁。
senses.why: The word is used as an exact definition: perfect stiffness, with zero deformation, is the limiting case of the everyday meaning.
senses.whyCN: 这里把词用作精确定义：完美的僵硬、零形变，就是日常含义的极限情形。

senses.title: Rigid thinking: a mind with locked joints
senses.titleCN: 僵化思维：关节锁死的心智
senses.definition: a way of thinking that cannot absorb new information or change its categories
senses.definitionCN: 无法吸收新信息或改变分类方式的思维方式
senses.example: Rigid thinking made the team repeat the same mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 僵化思维让团队重复同一个错误。
senses.why: The image is the same as S2, but applied to a process rather than a person: a mental procedure with locked joints cannot rotate to a new angle.
senses.whyCN: 画面与 S2 相同，但作用于一个过程而非一个人：关节锁死的心智程序无法转到新角度。

senses.title: Rigid application: rules enforced without exception
senses.titleCN: 严格执行：毫无例外地执行规则
senses.definition: applied strictly and exactly, with no allowance for special cases
senses.definitionCN: 严格而精确地执行，不允许特殊情况
senses.example: The school applies a rigid rule on late arrival.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校对迟到执行一条死规定。
senses.why: A rule that cannot bend to circumstance is rigid in the same physical sense: the line stays straight even when the situation asks it to curve.
senses.whyCN: 不能随情形弯曲的规则，就是同一意义上的 rigid：即使情况要求它弯，这条线仍然笔直。

senses.title: Rigid airship: a dirigible with a stiff frame
senses.titleCN: 刚性飞艇：带硬骨架的飞艇
senses.definition: an airship whose envelope is supported by a fixed metal framework, as opposed to a blimp
senses.definitionCN: 气囊由固定金属骨架支撑的飞艇，与软式飞艇相对
senses.example: The rigid airship was too large for its engines.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘刚性飞艇对它的发动机来说太大了。
senses.why: The technical name comes from the frame: because the girder does not sag or flex, the whole envelope keeps its shape in flight.
senses.whyCN: 这个技术名称来自骨架：因为桁架不下垂、不弯折，整个气囊在飞行中保持形状。

senses.title: Rigid institution: a system that cannot adapt
senses.titleCN: 僵化制度：无法适应的体系
senses.definition: an organization or system whose procedures cannot be changed to meet new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 程序无法为适应新情况而改变的组织或体系
senses.example: A rigid bureaucracy slowed every simple request.
senses.exampleCN: 僵化的官僚体系让每一个简单申请都变慢。
senses.why: An institution is a large body made of procedures. When none of its joints can move, the whole structure transmits shocks instead of absorbing them.
senses.whyCN: 制度是由程序构成的大身体。当它的关节都不能动时，整个结构只会传递冲击，而无法吸收冲击。

intro.en: Rigid comes straight from Latin, with no French stage. The record starts in the 16th century; the oldest Indo-European root is given only as generally believed.
intro.cn: rigid 直接来自拉丁语，没有经过法语阶段。记录始于 16 世纪；最古老的印欧词根只按一般看法给出。

items.en: First recorded in English in the 1530s with the physical sense 'stiff, hard, not pliable'.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 16 世纪 30 年代，取“僵直、坚硬、不易弯”的物理义。

items.en: Borrowed directly from Latin rigidus 'stiff, hard, firm, rigid'.
items.cn: 直接借自拉丁语 rigidus“僵直、坚硬、坚固、不可弯”。

items.en: rigidus is formed from rigere 'to be stiff, to be numb', the state of a limb that will not move.
items.cn: rigidus 由 rigere“变僵直、发僵”构成，指肢体不能活动的状态。

items.en: The earlier root is generally considered to be PIE *reig- 'to stretch, bind tight'. The reconstruction is not certain, so the deepest source is source uncertain.
items.cn: 更早的词根一般认为是原始印欧语 *reig-“拉紧、绑紧”。这一重构并不确定，故最深层来源不确定。

items.en: The figurative sense 'inflexible in opinion or rule' becomes common, alongside technical uses such as rigid body in mechanics.
items.cn: “观点或规则上不肯变通”的比喻义逐渐通行，同时力学中的 rigid body 等技术用法也出现。

items.en: Modern English ranges from a rigid beam and a rigid airship to rigid prices and rigid thinking. Rigor, rigorous and rigidity belong to the same Latin family.
items.cn: 现代英语从刚性梁、刚性飞艇，一直用到刚性价格与僵化思维。rigor、rigorous、rigidity 属于同一个拉丁家族。

note.en: The look-alike group is about form and sound; the near-meaning group is about how much can bend, and in what domain.
note.cn: 形近组看词形与读音；近义组看“能弯多少”以及用在哪个领域。

entries.definition: very thorough, strict, or severe. It comes from rigor, the noun from the same rigere 'be stiff' root, but it describes standards rather than physical hardness.
entries.definitionCN: 非常周密、严格或严酷。它来自同一 rigere“僵直”词根的名词 rigor，但描述的是标准而非物理硬度。

entries.definition: extremely cold, or sexually unresponsive. It comes from Latin frigere 'to be cold', a different root that only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的，或性冷淡的。它来自拉丁语 frigere“冷”，只是看起来相似的另一词根。

entries.definition: the adverb from rigid: in a stiff or strictly unvarying way. It is not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: rigid 的副词：以僵硬或严格不变的方式。它不是另一个词根词。

entries.definition: hard to bend or move. It is the everyday physical word and says nothing about rules or opinions.
entries.definitionCN: 难以弯曲或活动。它是最日常的物理词，不涉及规则或观点。

entries.definition: unable or unwilling to change. It covers both objects and people, but lacks rigid's technical uses in economics and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 不能或不愿改变。它兼指物体和人，但没有 rigid 在经济学与工程学中的技术用法。

entries.definition: demanding exact obedience to rules. It is about enforcement, while rigid is about the rule's inability to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 要求严格遵守规则。它强调执行力度，而 rigid 强调规则本身不能弯。

entries.definition: set and not changing. It fits prices and amounts, but does not carry the image of physical stiffness.
entries.definitionCN: 已设定且不变。它适用于价格和数量，但不带物理僵直的意象。

entries.definition: refusing to give way to pressure. It is more formal and more often used of people than of materials.
entries.definitionCN: 不肯在压力下让步。它更正式，也更常用于人而不是材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use real roots and real collocations, not sound-alike tricks.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词根和真实搭配，而不是谐音把戏。

normal.en: Latin rigere means 'to be stiff', the way a frozen limb will not move. Rigid is that state turned into an adjective.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rigere 意为“发僵”，就像冻僵的肢体不能动。rigid 就是把这种状态变成形容词。

normal.en: The same family gives rigor, rigorous and rigidity: all point to stiffness, whether of a body, a method or a rule.
normal.cn: 同一家族还有 rigor、rigorous、rigidity：它们都指向“僵直”，无论是身体、方法还是规则。

normal.en: Rigid body is an exact physics term: the distance between any two points never changes.
normal.cn: rigid body 是精确的物理术语：任意两点的距离永不改变。

normal.en: Rigid airship is named for its stiff metal frame, which keeps the balloon from sagging.
normal.cn: rigid airship 因其硬金属骨架而得名，骨架让气囊不下垂。

normal.en: Rigid prices and rigid wages are economics terms for values welded in place instead of sliding with the market.
normal.cn: rigid prices 与 rigid wages 是经济学术语，指被焊死在原地、不随市场滑动的数值。

abstract.en: Picture a steel bar with no joints: push it and it does not curve, it only moves as a whole. That is the single image behind every sense.
abstract.cn: 想象一根没有关节的钢条：推它，它不弯，只会整体移动。这就是所有义项背后的同一个画面。

abstract.en: Move the bar into a mind, a rule, a price or an institution: each one becomes a thing whose joints have locked, so it can only transmit pressure, not absorb it.
abstract.cn: 把这根钢条移进心智、规则、价格或制度：每一个都成了关节锁死的东西，只能传递压力，不能吸收压力。

abstract.en: A rigid thing is not weak — it is strong and unbending. The word's criticism is that strength without flexibility breaks instead of adapting.
abstract.cn: rigid 的东西并不弱——它坚固而不弯。这个词的批评意味在于：没有柔性的强度会断裂，而不会适应。

examples.en: The tent poles are rigid, so the canvas stays up in strong wind.
examples.cn: 帐篷杆是刚性的，所以帆布在强风里也能撑住。

examples.en: His rigid schedule left no room for a delayed train.
examples.cn: 他死板的日程没有给列车晚点留任何余地。

examples.en: Economists argued that rigid wages were slowing the recovery.
examples.cn: 经济学家认为刚性工资拖慢了复苏。

dict_mnemonic.text: “瑞吉的”——瑞吉的腰杆挺得笔直、怎么按都不弯 → rigid 僵硬的、死板的

root: 拉丁 rigidus“僵直、坚硬”，来自 rigere“发僵、变硬”；更早一般认为是 *reig-“拉紧、绑紧”，核心是“被绷紧固定，不能弯”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of rigid, all one image: a thing whose joints are locked — a beam, a mind, a price, a rule or an institution.
sensesIntro.cn: rigid 的九个义项都是同一个画面：关节被锁死的东西——钢梁、心智、价格、规则或制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bar stretched tight and bound, with no joint that can give way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被拉紧绷住、没有关节可以退让的杆。

branches.en: MATERIAL STIFFNESS: a beam, a frame, a rigid body and a rigid airship all keep their shape under load.
branches.cn: 材料刚性：钢梁、框架、刚体与刚性飞艇都在荷载下保持形状。

branches.en: MENTAL STIFFNESS: a person or a way of thinking whose joints are locked cannot take in a new angle.
branches.cn: 心智僵化：人或思维方式关节锁死，无法接纳新角度。

branches.en: ECONOMIC STIFFNESS: a price or wage welded in place cannot slide with supply and demand.
branches.cn: 经济刚性：被焊死的价格或工资无法随供求滑动。

branches.en: RULE STIFFNESS: a rule that stays straight even when the case asks it to curve.
branches.cn: 规则僵直：即使个案要求它弯，规则仍然笔直。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL STIFFNESS: a whole system of procedures that can only transmit shocks, not absorb them.
branches.cn: 制度僵化：整套程序只能传递冲击，无法吸收冲击。

intro.en: Rigid is a bare Latin adjective; English does not split it into a living prefix and root. Its suffixes build nouns, adverbs and verbs from the finished word.
intro.cn: rigid 是一个光秃秃的拉丁形容词；英语并不把它拆成活的“前缀＋词根”。它的后缀在成品词上构成名词、副词和动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is rigere 'be stiff', rigidus 'stiff', and rigor 'stiffness'. English also took rigor in the senses of strictness and, in medicine, a chill.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁家族是 rigere“发僵”、rigidus“僵硬的”、rigor“僵硬”。英语还借入 rigor，表示“严格”，医学中也指“寒战”。

items.meaning: the quality of being stiff or unchanging
items.meaningCN: 刚性；僵硬；死板（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The rigidity of the frame kept the bridge steady.
items.exampleCN: 框架的刚性使桥梁保持稳定。

items.meaning: in a stiff or strictly unvarying way
items.meaningCN: 僵硬地；严格地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The rules were rigidly enforced.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则被严格执行。

items.meaning: the state of being rigid
items.meaningCN: 坚硬；僵直（-ness 构成状态名词，较少用）
items.example: The rigidness of the old chair made it uncomfortable.
items.exampleCN: 这把旧椅子的僵硬让它坐着不舒服。

items.meaning: to make or become rigid
items.meaningCN: 使变僵硬；使固定（-ify 表示“使成为”）
items.example: Cold air rigidified the rubber seal.
items.exampleCN: 冷空气使橡胶密封圈变硬。

items.meaning: the process of becoming rigid
items.meaningCN: 僵化过程；硬化（-cation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The rigidification of the policy took years.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策的僵化经历了很多年。

items.meaning: partly stiff, partly flexible
items.meaningCN: 半刚性的（semi-“半”+ rigid）
items.example: A semi-rigid container holds its shape but can flex.
items.exampleCN: 半刚性容器能保持形状，但也可以弯折。

items.meaning: strictness; severity; a sudden chill
items.meaningCN: 严格；严酷；（医学）寒战
items.example: The rigor of the training surprised the recruits.
items.exampleCN: 训练的严格让新兵们吃惊。

items.meaning: thorough and strict
items.meaningCN: 严密的；严格的（rigor + -ous“充满”）
items.example: The study used a rigorous method.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究采用了严密的方法。

items.meaning: the stiffening of a body after death
items.meaningCN: 尸僵（拉丁语“死亡的僵硬”）
items.example: Rigor mortis sets in within a few hours.
items.exampleCN: 尸僵在几小时内出现。

latinEntries.meaning: to be stiff, to be numb

definition_zh: 角色；职能；职位；作用；（社会的）身份
definition_en: a part played by an actor, or the function and position that a person or thing has in a situation or system
core_image: 一卷写着台词的纸卷：谁拿到它，谁就担当那个“部分”
scene: In the rehearsal room, the actor reads his lines from the paper scroll that gave the role its name, then walks on stage as the king.
sceneCN: 这里 role 是「演员角色」（第 1 个义项：演员扮演的人物）；句意：在排练室里，演员照着那卷让 role 得名的纸卷念台词，然后以国王的身份走上舞台。图中可辨识物件：台词纸卷、戏服、舞台、排练用的椅子。

derivatives.zh: 角色扮演；进行角色扮演
扮演角色的人；角色扮演游戏玩家
基于角色的（如权限管理）

senses.title: Theatrical role: the part an actor performs
senses.titleCN: 戏剧角色：演员表演的部分
senses.definition: one of the characters in a play, film or opera, taken by a particular actor
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或歌剧中由某位演员承担的人物
senses.example: She was given the role of the queen.
senses.exampleCN: 她得到了王后这个角色。
senses.why: French rôle meant literally 'roll of paper', the scroll on which an actor's lines were written. The part is what the scroll contains, so the word for the paper became the word for the character.
senses.whyCN: 法语 rôle 字面就是“纸卷”，即写有演员台词的那卷纸。角色就是纸卷里写的内容，于是“纸”的词变成了“人物”的词。

senses.title: Functional role: the job a person fills
senses.titleCN: 职能角色：一个人承担的岗位
senses.definition: the function, position or duty that someone has in an organization or activity
senses.definitionCN: 某人在组织或活动中承担的职能、职位或职责
senses.example: Her role is to keep the accounts in order.
senses.exampleCN: 她的职能是把账目管好。
senses.why: A written part is assigned to a player. In an organization, the same slot is assigned to an employee: the scroll becomes the job description, and the actor becomes the worker.
senses.whyCN: 写好的部分是分配给演员的。在组织里，同一个“位置”分配给员工：纸卷变成岗位说明，演员变成职员。

senses.title: Role model: a part others copy
senses.titleCN: 角色榜样：别人照着演的部分
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase role model, a person whose behaviour is taken as an example by others
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 role model 中指被他人当作行为范例的人
senses.example: Her coach became a role model for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的教练成了全队的榜样。
senses.why: The image turns slightly: the part is no longer performed on a stage but observed and copied. A model is a pattern, and a role model is a part that others take up in their own lives.
senses.whyCN: 画面略有转动：这个“部分”不再在舞台上表演，而是被观察和模仿。model 是范本，role model 就是别人在生活里照着担当的部分。

senses.title: Gender role: the part society assigns
senses.titleCN: 性别角色：社会指派的部分
senses.definition: the set of social expectations attached to being a man or a woman in a particular culture
senses.definitionCN: 特定文化中附加于男性或女性身份的一套社会期待
senses.example: Gender roles have changed greatly in the last century.
senses.exampleCN: 性别角色在过去一个世纪里发生了巨大变化。
senses.why: Here the scroll is written by society rather than by a playwright. The part is handed to a whole group, and people are expected to perform it whether or not they chose it.
senses.whyCN: 这里纸卷不是剧作家写的，而是社会写的。这个部分被交给整整一群人，无论他们是否愿意，都被期待照着演。

senses.title: Role-play: performing a part as practice
senses.titleCN: 角色扮演：为练习而演一个部分
senses.definition: an activity in which people act out a situation or character, often for training or therapy
senses.definitionCN: 人们演出某个情境或人物、常用于培训或治疗的活动
senses.example: The class did a role-play of a job interview.
senses.exampleCN: 班上做了一次求职面试的角色扮演。
senses.why: The scroll is used without a stage: the part is taken on temporarily so that the player can practise what the real situation demands.
senses.whyCN: 纸卷被用在没有舞台的地方：这个部分被临时担当，以便扮演者练习真实情境所要求的东西。

senses.title: Leading role: the part that carries the story
senses.titleCN: 主角：撑起故事的那个部分
senses.definition: the principal part in a play or film, or the most important position in an effort
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧或电影中的主要角色，或某项工作中最重要的位置
senses.example: He took the leading role in the rescue effort.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这次救援行动中起了主导作用。
senses.why: One scroll carries more lines than the others. The leading role is the largest part in the script, so it naturally becomes the most visible position.
senses.whyCN: 有一卷纸写的台词比别的多。leading role 就是剧本里最大的那部分，于是自然成了最显眼的位置。

senses.title: Technical role: a slot defined by permissions
senses.titleCN: 系统角色：由权限定义的位置
senses.definition: in computing, a named set of permissions or functions assigned to a user or process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域中指派给用户或进程的一组具名权限或功能
senses.example: An administrator role can change every setting.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员角色可以更改所有设置。
senses.why: The word keeps its 'assigned part' meaning but strips out the human being: the role is a written set of rights, and whoever holds the role can do exactly what it lists.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了“被指派的部分”之义，但抽掉了人：角色是一组写好的权利，谁持有这个角色，就能做它列出的那些事。

senses.title: Title role: the part named in the title
senses.titleCN: 同名角色：写在剧名里的部分
senses.definition: the character whose name is the title of a play, film or opera
senses.definitionCN: 名字成为戏剧、电影或歌剧标题的那个角色
senses.example: The young singer sang the title role in Carmen.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻歌手演唱了《卡门》的同名角色。
senses.why: The script's cover carries the name of its largest part. The title role is the part that gives the whole work its name, so the scroll and the character share one label.
senses.whyCN: 剧本封面写着它最大那个部分的名字。title role 就是给整部作品命名的部分，纸卷和人物共用一个标签。

senses.title: Play a role: to have an influence
senses.titleCN: 起作用：产生影响
senses.definition: in the phrase play a role in, to be one of the factors that produce a result
senses.definitionCN: 用于 play a role in，表示是产生某结果的因素之一
senses.example: Diet plays a role in heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食在心脏病中起作用。
senses.why: On stage, a part contributes to the whole play. Off stage, any factor that takes up a part in an outcome is said to play a role, even when there is no actor at all.
senses.whyCN: 在舞台上，一个部分对整出戏有所贡献。离开舞台后，任何在结果中“担当一部分”的因素，都被说成 play a role，即使根本没有演员。

intro.en: Role is a French theatre word whose literal sense is 'roll of paper'. It reached English in the 17th century; the Latin chain is well documented.
intro.cn: role 是一个法语戏剧词，字面义为“纸卷”。它在 17 世纪进入英语；其拉丁语链条有清楚的记载。

items.en: First recorded in English in the 1600s, at first in the theatre, for the part written for an actor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 17 世纪，最初用于戏剧，指为演员写好的那个部分。

items.en: Borrowed from French rôle 'part, character', which also meant literally 'roll of paper'.
items.cn: 借自法语 rôle“部分、人物”，其字面义同样是“纸卷”。

items.en: French rôle goes back to Old French rolle 'roll, scroll', a sheet rolled up for handling.
items.cn: 法语 rôle 可追到古法语 rolle“卷、卷轴”，即卷起来便于携带的纸。

items.en: Old French rolle comes from Latin rotulus 'little roll', a diminutive of rota 'wheel'. A rolled sheet is literally a small wheel.
items.cn: 古法语 rolle 来自拉丁语 rotulus“小卷”，是 rota“轮子”的指小形式。卷起的纸 literally 就是一只小轮子。

items.en: Actors' lines were written on such a scroll, so the paper that held the words came to name the character those words belonged to.
items.cn: 演员的台词就写在这种纸卷上，于是“写有台词的纸”开始指代那些台词所属的人物。

items.en: From the stage the word spread to jobs and functions. Role model is a 20c. phrase; role-play and computer roles extend the same 'assigned part' idea.
items.cn: 这个词从舞台扩散到职位与职能。role model 是 20 世纪的说法；role-play 与计算机中的 role 延续同一个“被指派的部分”观念。

note.en: The look-alike group checks spelling and sound; the near-meaning group compares what kind of 'part' each word names.
note.cn: 形近组检查拼写与读音；近义组比较每个词指的是哪一种“部分”。

entries.definition: to turn over and over, or a rolled-up sheet. It shares the Latin rotulus 'little roll' source but kept the physical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 滚动；卷起的东西。它与 role 同出拉丁语 rotulus“小卷”，但保留了物理含义。

entries.definition: a principle or regulation. It comes from Latin regula 'straight stick', a different root despite the similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 原则或规则。它来自拉丁语 regula“直尺”，读音虽近但词根不同。

entries.definition: the activity of acting out a part. It is a compound of role + play, not an independent root word.
entries.definitionCN: 角色扮演活动。它是 role + play 的复合词，不是独立的词根词。

entries.definition: a character in a play, or a share in an activity. It is the everyday word and overlaps role most closely on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧中的人物，或活动中的一份。它是最日常的词，在舞台语境中与 role 重叠最多。

entries.definition: the purpose or job that something is designed to perform. It stresses what a thing does, not who fills the position.
entries.definitionCN: 某物被设计来完成的目的或功能。它强调“做什么”，而不是“谁占这个位置”。

entries.definition: a job in an organization. It is the formal employment word and does not carry the theatrical image.
entries.definitionCN: 组织中的一个职位。它是正式的雇佣用语，不带戏剧意象。

entries.definition: a person in a story or play. It names the fictional person, while role names the part as something an actor takes on.
entries.definitionCN: 故事或戏剧中的人物。它指的是虚构的人，而 role 指演员所承担的那个部分。

entries.definition: in the phrase in one's capacity as, the official position in which someone acts. It is formal and limited to official contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 用于 in one's capacity as，指某人以某官方身份行事。它较正式，限于官方语境。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real paper-scroll image and real compounds, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的纸卷意象和真实复合词，而不是编造的谐音。

normal.en: rôle literally meant 'roll of paper': the actor's lines were written on a scroll, and the scroll named the part.
normal.cn: rôle 字面就是“纸卷”：演员的台词写在卷上，这卷纸就成了那个部分的名称。

normal.en: Latin rotulus is a little rota 'wheel'. A sheet rolled up for carrying really is a small wheel shape.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rotulus 是 rota“轮子”的指小形式。卷起来便于携带的纸，形状确实像一只小轮子。

normal.en: The same rota family gives rotate, rotation, rotary and round: all are turning or wheel words.
normal.cn: 同一个 rota 家族还有 rotate、rotation、rotary、round：它们都是“转”或“轮”的词。

normal.en: Play a role moves the image from the stage to life: the part you perform in a situation is your contribution.
normal.cn: play a role 把画面从舞台移进生活：你在某个情境中演的那一部分，就是你的贡献。

normal.en: Role model, role-play and title role are fixed phrases built on the same idea of an assigned part.
normal.cn: role model、role-play、title role 都是建立在同一个“被指派的部分”观念上的固定短语。

abstract.en: Picture a scroll with lines written on it. Whoever holds the scroll takes on the part written inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷写满台词的纸。谁拿到这卷纸，谁就承担里面写着的那个部分。

abstract.en: Now imagine the scroll as a shaped slot: in a company, a family or a computer system, a role is the slot a person or process fills.
abstract.cn: 再把纸卷想象成一个有形状的凹槽：在公司、家庭或计算机系统里，role 就是人或进程填进去的那个槽。

abstract.en: Every sense is a part written for someone — an actor, an employee, a parent, a database user — and the writing comes before the performance.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是“为某人写好的一个部分”——演员、员工、父母、数据库用户——而“写”总在“演”之前。

examples.en: She won an award for her role in the film.
examples.cn: 她因在这部电影中的角色获奖。

examples.en: Teachers have an important role in shaping confidence.
examples.cn: 教师在塑造自信方面起着重要作用。

examples.en: The database gives each user a different role.
examples.cn: 数据库给每个用户分配不同的角色。

dict_mnemonic.text: “罗欧”——罗欧一上台就换成国王的角色 → role 角色、职能

root: 法语 rôle“角色”，字面“纸卷”，源自拉丁 rotulus“小卷轴”（rota“轮”的指小形式）；核心是“写有台词的纸卷＝一个人要担当的部分”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of role, all from one scroll: a part is written down, handed to someone, and then performed — on a stage, in a job, in society or in a system.
sensesIntro.cn: role 的九个义项都来自同一卷纸：一个部分被写下来、交给某人，然后被演出来——在舞台上、职位上、社会里或系统中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scroll of lines handed to one player, who must take up the part written on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷写着台词的纸交给一个表演者，他必须承担上面写着的部分。

branches.en: THEATRICAL PART: an actor's part, the largest part, and the part that names the whole work.
branches.cn: 戏剧部分：演员的角色、最大的角色，以及给整部作品命名的角色。

branches.en: POSITION IN A SYSTEM: the scroll becomes a job description or a set of permissions attached to a slot.
branches.cn: 系统位置：纸卷变成岗位说明，或附加在某个槽位上的一组权限。

branches.en: SOCIAL EXPECTATION: society writes the part and hands it to a group, as with role models and gender roles.
branches.cn: 社会期待：社会写好部分并交给一群人，如 role model 与 gender role。

branches.en: ENACTMENT: the part is taken on temporarily for practice, without a real stage.
branches.cn: 演练：部分被临时承担用于练习，没有真正的舞台。

branches.en: INFLUENCE: any factor that takes up a part in an outcome is said to play a role.
branches.cn: 影响：任何在结果中担当一份的因素，都被说成 play a role。

intro.en: Role is a borrowing, not an affixed formation. English builds compounds with role (role-play, role model) and adds only plural -s directly to it.
intro.cn: role 是借词，不是加缀构词。英语用 role 构成复合词（role-play、role model），直接加在它上面的只有复数 -s。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is rota 'wheel' and its derivatives: rotulus 'little roll', rotare 'to turn', rotatio 'a turning'. The 'paper scroll' sense grew out of the shape of a rolled sheet.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁家族是 rota“轮”及其派生词：rotulus“小卷”、rotare“转动”、rotatio“旋转”。“纸卷”义正是从卷起纸张的形状长出来的。

items.meaning: a part played or a function held
items.meaningCN: 扮演的角色；承担的职能
items.example: He took the role of narrator.
items.exampleCN: 他担任了叙述者的角色。

items.meaning: more than one part or function
items.meaningCN: 多个角色或职能（复数后缀）
items.example: The two roles overlap in practice.
items.exampleCN: 这两个角色在实践中互相重叠。

items.meaning: to act out a part or situation
items.meaningCN: 角色扮演；演一个部分或情境（复合词）
items.example: Students role-play a customer complaint.
items.exampleCN: 学生们角色扮演一起顾客投诉。

items.meaning: the activity of acting out parts
items.meaningCN: 角色扮演活动（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: Role-playing helps trainees practise difficult talks.
items.exampleCN: 角色扮演帮助受训者练习困难的谈话。

items.meaning: a person who takes part in role-play
items.meaningCN: 参与角色扮演的人（-er 表示施动者）
items.example: Each role-player received a short brief.
items.exampleCN: 每位扮演者都拿到一份简短说明。

items.meaning: a person whose behaviour others copy
items.meaningCN: 榜样；被他人模仿行为的人（复合词）
items.example: A captain should be a role model for the squad.
items.exampleCN: 队长应当是球队的榜样。

items.meaning: organized according to roles
items.meaningCN: 基于角色的（复合形容词）
items.example: The system uses role-based access control.
items.exampleCN: 该系统使用基于角色的访问控制。

items.meaning: to turn around a centre
items.meaningCN: 旋转；轮换（同一 rota 词根）
items.example: The staff rotate between the two offices.
items.exampleCN: 员工在两个办公室之间轮换。

items.meaning: a turning around, or a regular order of taking turns
items.meaningCN: 旋转；轮换（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The rotation of the shifts keeps work fair.
items.exampleCN: 班次轮换让工作保持公平。

items.meaning: turning around an axis
items.meaningCN: 旋转的；转动的（rota + -ary）
items.example: A rotary engine spins instead of pumping pistons.
items.exampleCN: 转子发动机靠旋转而不是活塞往复。

definition_zh: 路线；路径；航线；途径；路由；（按路线）发送
definition_en: a way from one place to another, a fixed line of travel or transport, the path by which something spreads, or to send something along a chosen way
core_image: 在密林或荒原里被“砍开”的一条通路：障碍被破除后留下的那道缝
scene: A hiker traces a red line across the map, marking the only route through the mountain pass.
sceneCN: 这里 route 是「从 A 到 B 的路线」（第 1 个义项：两点之间的走法）；句意：徒步者在地图上画出一条红线，标出穿过山口唯一的一条路线。图中可辨识物件：地图、红线、山口、背包与登山杖。

pos.zh: 按特定路线发送；为……安排路线

derivatives.zh: 路由器；按路线发送的人或设备
路径选择；路由（routing 也写作 routeing）
已按路线发送的；被安排走某路的

senses.title: A way from A to B: the line you travel
senses.titleCN: 从 A 到 B 的路线：你走的那条线
senses.definition: the path or way taken to get from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方到另一个地方所走的路径
senses.example: We took the mountain route to avoid the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走山路以避开拥堵。
senses.why: Latin rupta (via) meant 'a broken or cut road', from rumpere 'to break'. A route is first a way cut through whatever blocks the way, so the word begins with an opening rather than with a line on a map.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 rupta (via) 意为“被切断的路”，来自 rumpere“打破”。route 起初是穿过障碍被“砍开”的路，所以这个词的起点是“开路”，而不是地图上的一条线。

senses.title: Fixed service route: a bus or air line
senses.titleCN: 固定线路：公交或航空线
senses.definition: a regular line travelled by a bus, train, aircraft or ship, usually with fixed stops
senses.definitionCN: 公交、火车、飞机或船只定期行走的线路，通常有固定站点
senses.example: The airport bus route stops at the central station.
senses.exampleCN: 机场巴士线路在中央车站停靠。
senses.why: Once a cut way is walked regularly, its shape hardens into a schedule. The route becomes an institution with stops and numbers, not just a direction.
senses.whyCN: 一条被砍开的路一旦被定期行走，它的形状就固化成时刻表。route 于是成了带站点和编号的制度，而不只是一个方向。

senses.title: Route of transmission: the path something spreads along
senses.titleCN: 传播途径：某物扩散所走的路径
senses.definition: the way a disease, substance, signal or influence travels from one point to another
senses.definitionCN: 疾病、物质、信号或影响从一点传到另一点的路径
senses.example: Mosquitoes are the main route of transmission for the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是该疾病的主要传播途径。
senses.why: The cut way is used by something invisible. What matters is not the road but the channel it provides, so route becomes a technical word for any path of spread.
senses.whyCN: 被砍开的路由某种看不见的东西来走。重点不在路本身，而在它提供的通道，于是 route 成了任何扩散路径的技术词。

senses.title: En route: already on the way
senses.titleCN: 在途中：已经上路
senses.definition: in the phrase en route, on the way or during the journey
senses.definitionCN: 用于 en route，表示在路上或旅途中
senses.example: The plane is en route to Tokyo.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机正在飞往东京的途中。
senses.why: The French phrase en route is literally 'in (the) way'. The traveller is placed inside the cut path, between the start and the end, so the noun becomes a statement of position.
senses.whyCN: 法语短语 en route 字面是“在路中”。旅行者被放进那条被砍开的路径里，位于起点与终点之间，于是名词变成了位置陈述。

senses.title: March route: the line an army follows
senses.titleCN: 行军路线：军队走的那条线
senses.definition: the planned line of movement for a military unit or a large group
senses.definitionCN: 军事单位或大型队伍计划行走的线路
senses.example: The column moved along a route that kept it off the main roads.
senses.exampleCN: 纵队沿一条避开主干道的路线行进。
senses.why: This is the oldest practical sense: an army must cut or choose a passable way, and the route is the plan for that way before the march begins.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的实用义：军队必须开出一条或选出一条能走的路，而 route 就是行军开始前对这条路的计划。

senses.title: Escape route: the way out of danger
senses.titleCN: 逃生路线：脱离危险的出口
senses.definition: a planned way of leaving a dangerous place or situation
senses.definitionCN: 离开危险地点或处境的一条预定路径
senses.example: The building has two escape routes from every floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼每层都有两条逃生路线。
senses.why: A route cut through a wall or a crowd is defined by the barrier it defeats. Escape route keeps that literal force: the value of the path is the opening it makes.
senses.whyCN: 穿过墙或人群的路线，由它所突破的障碍来定义。escape route 保留了这种字面力量：这条路的价值就是它开出的缺口。

senses.title: Mail route: a delivery circuit
senses.titleCN: 邮路：投递环线
senses.definition: a regular circuit along which mail or goods are carried and delivered
senses.definitionCN: 邮件或货物被运送、投递所走的固定环线
senses.example: The old mail route crossed three villages before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 这条老邮路在中午前穿过三个村庄。
senses.why: A delivery route is a cut way turned into a loop: the same opening is used again and again, so the path becomes a named service with its own history.
senses.whyCN: 投递路线是被砍开的路变成了一个环：同一个开口被反复使用，于是这条路径成了带自己历史的具名服务。

senses.title: Verb: to send by a chosen way
senses.titleCN: 动词：按选定路线发送
senses.definition: to send someone or something along a particular way, or to direct traffic through a chosen path
senses.definitionCN: 沿特定路径发送人或物，或指挥交通走选定路线
senses.example: The shipment was routed through a smaller port.
senses.exampleCN: 这批货物被安排走一个较小的港口。
senses.why: The noun turns into an action: someone takes the cut way and puts a thing on it. Routing is the act of deciding which opening the traffic will use.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动作：有人选好那条被砍开的路，把东西放上去。routing 就是决定车流走哪一个开口的行为。

senses.title: Network route: the path a packet takes
senses.titleCN: 网络路由：数据包走的路径
senses.definition: in computing, the path that data follows through a network, chosen by a router
senses.definitionCN: 计算机领域中数据在网络上行走、由路由器选择的路径
senses.example: The router chose a faster route for the video stream.
senses.exampleCN: 路由器为视频流选择了一条更快的路径。
senses.why: The image survives fully: data are cut a way through a mesh of nodes, and the router is the device that picks the opening. Nothing physical is dug, but the path is still 'cut'.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象完整地保留下来：数据在节点网中被“砍”出一条路，而路由器就是挑选开口的设备。没有真的挖土，但路径仍然是被“切开”的。

intro.en: Route is a French word for a road, built on a Latin participle meaning 'broken, cut'. The chain is well recorded; the date is approximate.
intro.cn: route 是一个法语“道路”词，建立在意为“被打破、被切断”的拉丁分词上。这条链有清楚记载；年代为大致估计。

items.en: Old French rute 'road, way, path' is recorded in the 12c., and English borrows it as route in the Middle English period.
items.cn: 古法语 rute“道路、路径”在 12 世纪有记录，英语在中古英语时期把它借入为 route。

items.en: The Old French form also appears as route, meaning a way or a course, including a military line of march.
items.cn: 古法语形式也写作 route，表示道路或行程，包括军队的行军路线。

items.en: It comes from Latin rupta (via) 'a broken or cut road', the feminine participle of rumpere 'to break, burst, cut'.
items.cn: 它来自拉丁语 rupta (via)“被切断的路”，即 rumpere“打破、爆裂、切断”的阴性分词。

items.en: The original picture is not a drawn line but an opening: a way forced through woods, rock or a hostile line.
items.cn: 最初的画面不是画出的线，而是一个开口：在树林、岩石或敌阵中被强行开出的通路。

items.en: With scheduled transport, route hardens into fixed lines: mail routes, coach routes, bus routes and later air routes.
items.cn: 随着定期交通的发展，route 固化为固定线路：邮路、马车路线、公交线路，后来还有航空线路。

items.en: The verb 'to send by a route' develops, and 20c. networking gives route and router a technical sense. Routine and rout are close relatives.
items.cn: 动词义“按路线发送”发展出来，20 世纪网络技术又给 route 与 router 技术含义。routine 与 rout 是近亲。

note.en: The look-alike group is about spelling and sound, including two words from the same Latin source. The near-meaning group compares how each word describes a way.
note.cn: 形近组看拼写与读音，其中两个词同出拉丁语源；近义组比较每个词如何描述“路”。

entries.definition: a decisive defeat, or to defeat utterly. It comes from the same Latin rupta 'broken' image, originally a broken and scattered army.
entries.definitionCN: 溃败；彻底击败。它同出拉丁语 rupta“被打破”的意象，原指被打散溃逃的军队。

entries.definition: a device or person that directs traffic along routes. It is route + -er, not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 沿路线引导车流或数据的设备或人。它是 route + -er，不是独立词根词。

entries.definition: a fixed way of doing things. French routine is a diminutive of route 'way', so it literally means 'a little way'.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的做事方式。法语 routine 是 route“道路”的指小形式，字面就是“小路”。

entries.definition: a narrow way made by feet or laid for walkers. It is smaller and more physical than route.
entries.definitionCN: 由脚步踩出或为行人铺设的窄路。它比 route 更小、更具体。

entries.definition: a road, direction, or method. It is the broad everyday word and can also mean 'manner'.
entries.definitionCN: 道路、方向或方法。它是最宽泛的日常词，也可表示“方式”。

entries.definition: the direction in which something moves, especially a ship, plane or river. It stresses heading rather than the line itself.
entries.definitionCN: 某物移动的方向，尤指船、飞机或河流。它强调航向，而不是线路本身。

entries.definition: a detailed plan of a journey, including places and times. It is a document about a route, not the route itself.
entries.definitionCN: 包含地点与时间的详细行程计划。它是关于路线的文件，而不是路线本身。

entries.definition: a way through or across something, or the act of travelling through. It keeps the 'opening' idea more strongly than route.
entries.definitionCN: 穿过某物的通道，或穿行的行为。它比 route 更强烈地保留“开口”的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the real Latin image of a road cut through an obstacle, and real transport phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着真实的拉丁意象——在障碍中砍出一条路——以及真实的交通短语展开。

normal.en: Latin rupta via means 'a broken road': the way exists because something was cut through. Route still carries that opening.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 rupta via 意为“被切断的路”：这条路之所以存在，是因为有东西被切开了。route 仍带着这个“开口”。

normal.en: rumpere 'to break' also gives rupture and interrupt: all three are about a break, and route is the break that becomes a passage.
normal.cn: rumpere“打破”还给出 rupture 与 interrupt：三者都与“断裂”有关，而 route 是变成通道的那道断口。

normal.en: En route is French for 'in the way': the traveller is placed inside the path, between departure and arrival.
normal.cn: en route 是法语“在路中”：旅行者被放进路径内部，位于出发与到达之间。

normal.en: A bus route, a mail route and a trade route are all fixed lines: the cut way is walked so often that it becomes a schedule.
normal.cn: bus route、mail route、trade route 都是固定线路：那条被砍开的路被走得太频繁，于是变成了时刻表。

normal.en: A router does to data exactly what the old word did to travellers: it chooses which opening the traffic will take.
normal.cn: router 对数据做的事，正是这个老词对旅人做的事：它决定车流走哪一个开口。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of thorns. Someone hacks a gap through it, and that gap is the route. The word starts from the cut, not from the map line.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵荆棘墙。有人从中砍出一个缺口，那个缺口就是 route。这个词从“切口”开始，而不是从地图上的线开始。

abstract.en: Once the gap is used regularly, it hardens into a bus line, a mail circuit or a march plan: the same opening repeated until it looks like an institution.
abstract.cn: 缺口一旦被定期使用，就固化成公交线、邮路或行军计划：同一个开口被反复使用，直到看起来像一项制度。

abstract.en: Data packets, diseases and armies all travel the same way in the word's logic: something is cut open, and whatever follows that opening is said to take the route.
abstract.cn: 数据包、疾病与军队在这个词的逻辑里走同一条路：某处被切开，凡是沿着这个开口走的东西，都叫“走这条 route”。

examples.en: Cyclists were advised to take a quieter route into town.
examples.cn: 骑行者被建议走一条更安静的进城路线。

examples.en: The river was once the main trade route to the coast.
examples.cn: 这条河曾是通往海岸的主要贸易路线。

examples.en: All incoming calls are routed to the support desk.
examples.cn: 所有来电都被转接到支持台。

dict_mnemonic.text: “路特”——“路特”别直，砍开一条直通的路 → route 路线、路径

root: 古法语 rute“道路”，源自拉丁 rupta (via)“被切断的路”，来自 rumpere“打破、切断”；核心是“在障碍中开出的通路”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of route, all from one opening: a way is cut through an obstacle, then repeated until it becomes a line, a service, a path of spread or a network choice.
sensesIntro.cn: route 的九个义项都来自同一个开口：一条路在障碍中被切开，然后被反复使用，直到成为线路、服务、传播路径或网络选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap cut through a barrier — the cut itself is the way.
core.cn: 核心意象：在障碍上砍出的一个缺口——切口本身就是路。

branches.en: PHYSICAL WAY: the general line from A to B, the army's march plan and the way out of danger all depend on a passable opening.
branches.cn: 物理通路：从 A 到 B 的普通路线、军队的行军计划、脱离危险的出口，都依赖一个能走通的开口。

branches.en: FIXED PUBLIC LINE: the repeated opening becomes a bus route, an air route or a mail circuit with stops and schedules.
branches.cn: 固定公共线路：被反复使用的开口变成公交线、航空线或带站点与时刻的邮路。

branches.en: PATH OF SPREAD: the channel is used by disease, signals or influence rather than by feet.
branches.cn: 传播路径：使用这条通道的不是脚，而是疾病、信号或影响。

branches.en: POSITION ON THE WAY: en route places the traveller inside the cut path, between departure and arrival.
branches.cn: 途中位置：en route 把旅行者放进那条被砍开的路径里，介于出发与到达之间。

branches.en: DISPATCH AND NETWORK: the noun becomes a verb, and the router chooses the opening that traffic or data will take.
branches.cn: 调度与网络：名词转为动词，路由器挑选车流或数据要走的开口。

intro.en: Route is a borrowed noun with no living prefix in English. Its endings are plural -s, past -ed and the -ing form; most new words are compounds or re- formations.
intro.cn: route 是借入的名词，在英语里没有活的前缀。它的词尾是复数 -s、过去 -ed 和 -ing 形式；新词大多是复合词或 re- 结构。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is rumpere 'to break'. Its family includes rupta 'broken (road)', ruptura 'a breaking' and irrumpere 'to break in'; English has rupture, interrupt, erupt and corrupt from the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源是 rumpere“打破”。其家族包括 rupta“被切断的路”、ruptura“断裂”、irrumpere“闯入”；英语的 rupture、interrupt、erupt、corrupt 都出自同一动词。

items.meaning: a way from one place to another
items.meaningCN: 从一地到另一地的路线
items.example: This route avoids the city centre.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线避开市中心。

items.meaning: more than one way, or he/she sends along a way
items.meaningCN: 多条路线；或第三人称单数“按路线发送”
items.example: Two routes lead to the summit.
items.exampleCN: 有两条路线通往山顶。

items.meaning: sent along a chosen way
items.meaningCN: 被安排走某条路线（过去式或分词）
items.example: The buses were routed around the flooded street.
items.exampleCN: 公交车被安排绕开被淹的街道。

items.meaning: the choosing of paths for traffic or data
items.meaningCN: 路径选择；路由（动名词）
items.example: Routing decides how quickly a message arrives.
items.exampleCN: 路由决定一条消息多快到达。

items.meaning: to change the way something travels
items.meaningCN: 改道；重新规划路线（re-“再”+ route）
items.example: The airline rerouted the flight around the storm.
items.exampleCN: 航空公司让航班改道绕开风暴。

items.meaning: the act of changing a route
items.meaningCN: 改道；重新路由（-ing 构成名词）
items.example: Rerouting added two hours to the journey.
items.exampleCN: 改道让行程多了两个小时。

items.meaning: a device that forwards data or traffic
items.meaningCN: 路由器；按路线发送的设备（route + -er）
items.example: The router forwards each packet along the best path.
items.exampleCN: 路由器把每个数据包沿最佳路径转发。

items.meaning: a fixed, repeated way of doing things
items.meaningCN: 常规；惯例（法语 route 的指小形式，字面“小路”）
items.example: A morning routine saves time.
items.exampleCN: 一套晨间惯例能节省时间。

items.meaning: a broken, scattered army; a decisive defeat
items.meaningCN: 溃败；彻底击败（同出“被打断”的意象）
items.example: The cavalry was put to rout.
items.exampleCN: 骑兵被彻底击溃。

items.meaning: a break or burst
items.meaningCN: 断裂；破裂（同一 rumpere 词根）
items.example: A rupture in the pipe caused the leak.
items.exampleCN: 管道破裂导致了泄漏。

latinEntries.meaning: broken, cut (as in rupta via, a cut road)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 被切断的（如 rupta via“被切断的路”）

definition_zh: 情景；设想；剧情提纲；剧本大纲；方案
definition_en: a described sequence of possible events, a sketch of a plot, or a projected situation used for planning
core_image: 舞台后方那顶棚屋与布景板：剧情被一幕一幕写在一块板上
scene: In a darkened theatre, the director sketches the opening scenario on a board while the actors wait behind the stage wall.
sceneCN: 这里 scenario 是「戏剧剧情提纲」（第 5 个义项：分幕写下的剧情概要）；句意：在昏暗的剧场里，导演在板子上勾出开场剧情提纲，演员们在舞台墙后等候。图中可辨识物件：布景板、导演的笔、剧本、幕布、后台的演员。

pos.zh: 情景；设想；可能发生的一系列事件
剧情提纲；剧本大纲；（规划的）方案

derivatives.zh: 风景的；舞台布景的（同 scaena 词根）

senses.title: Imagined sequence: a possible chain of events
senses.titleCN: 设想的事件序列：可能发生的一串事
senses.definition: a described or imagined series of events that could happen
senses.definitionCN: 被描述或想象出来、可能发生的一连串事件
senses.example: We outlined three scenarios for the coming year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们为来年勾画了三种情景。
senses.why: Italian scenario first meant a sketch of a play's scenes. An imagined future is written the same way: a sequence of scenes laid out on a board before anything happens.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 scenario 最初指一部戏各场次的提纲。想象的未来也用同样的方式写：事情发生前，一串场景先被排在板上。

senses.title: Screenplay outline: the film's scenes on paper
senses.titleCN: 电影剧本大纲：纸上的各场戏
senses.definition: a written outline of the scenes and action of a film or television programme
senses.definitionCN: 电影或电视节目各场次与情节的书面概要
senses.example: The director rejected the first scenario as too slow.
senses.exampleCN: 导演否决了第一版剧本大纲，认为它太拖沓。
senses.why: This is the Italian sense carried into film: before dialogue, there is a list of scenes. The scenario is the skeleton of the story, not yet the flesh of the script.
senses.whyCN: 这是意大利语含义进入电影后的用法：在对白之前，先有一份场次清单。scenario 是故事的骨架，还不是剧本的血肉。

senses.title: Worst-case scenario: the scene you fear
senses.titleCN: 最坏情况：你最怕的那一幕
senses.definition: in the phrase worst-case scenario, the most unfavourable outcome that could reasonably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 worst-case scenario，指在合理范围内可能发生的最不利结果
senses.example: In the worst-case scenario, the whole plant would shut down.
senses.exampleCN: 最坏的情况下，整座工厂会停工。
senses.why: A scenario is a scene you can rehearse in the mind. The worst case is the darkest scene in that rehearsal, written out so that it can be prepared for instead of merely feared.
senses.whyCN: scenario 是可以在脑中预演的一幕。worst case 就是这场预演里最暗的一幕，把它写出来，才能做准备，而不只是害怕。

senses.title: Scenario planning: rehearsing several futures
senses.titleCN: 情景规划：预演几种未来
senses.definition: a planning method in which an organization works out several possible futures and prepares for each
senses.definitionCN: 组织推演若干种可能未来并为每一种做准备的方法
senses.example: Scenario planning helped the company survive the oil shock.
senses.exampleCN: 情景规划帮助公司挺过了石油危机。
senses.why: The stage image becomes a method: several scenes are written instead of one script, and the planner keeps all of them ready because no single scene is guaranteed.
senses.whyCN: 舞台意象变成一种方法：不是写一个剧本，而是写好几幕，规划者把每一幕都准备好，因为没有哪一幕是被保证的。

senses.title: Dramatic scenario: the outline of the plot
senses.titleCN: 戏剧剧情提纲：情节的概要
senses.definition: the original sense: a brief outline of the scenes and plot of an opera, play or ballet
senses.definitionCN: 最初的含义：歌剧、戏剧或芭蕾各场次与情节的简要提纲
senses.example: The opera's scenario was printed in the programme.
senses.exampleCN: 这部歌剧的剧情提纲印在节目单上。
senses.why: The Italian word was born in the opera house: scenario is the scene-by-scene plan from which the libretto and music were built.
senses.whyCN: 这个意大利词诞生于歌剧院：scenario 是逐场的计划，剧本与音乐都从它搭建起来。

senses.title: Climate scenario: a projected physical future
senses.titleCN: 气候情景：被推演出的物理未来
senses.definition: a scientifically modelled set of future climate conditions based on stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 基于明确假设、由科学模型推演的一套未来气候条件
senses.example: The high-emission climate scenario predicts a two-metre rise.
senses.exampleCN: 高排放气候情景预测海平面上升两米。
senses.why: The 'scene' is now drawn with data rather than words: a scenario is a coherent picture built from assumptions, so that its consequences can be examined.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“场景”用数据而不是文字画成：scenario 是由假设构建的一幅自洽图景，以便检查它的后果。

senses.title: Scenario analysis: comparing the scenes
senses.titleCN: 情景分析：把几幕放在一起比较
senses.definition: a method of comparing outcomes under different stated assumptions
senses.definitionCN: 在不同明确假设下比较结果的方法
senses.example: Scenario analysis showed that both plans carried similar risk.
senses.exampleCN: 情景分析显示两个方案承担的风险相近。
senses.why: The word shifts from a single scene to the act of lining scenes up side by side. Analysis is possible because each scenario is a closed, self-consistent picture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从单独一幕转到把几幕并排摆放的动作。之所以能分析，是因为每个 scenario 都是一个封闭而自洽的图景。

senses.title: Best-case scenario: the brightest scene
senses.titleCN: 最好情况：最亮的那一幕
senses.definition: in the phrase best-case scenario, the most favourable outcome that could reasonably happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于 best-case scenario，指在合理范围内可能发生的最有利结果
senses.example: The best-case scenario still leaves us short of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 最好的情况仍然让我们缺人手。
senses.why: The same rehearsal, lit from the other side: the best case is the scene where every assumption goes right, written out to test whether even success would be enough.
senses.whyCN: 同一场预演，从另一侧打光：best case 是每个假设都顺利的那一幕，写出来是为了检验“即使成功是否也够”。

senses.title: Hypothetical situation: the scene you suppose
senses.titleCN: 假设情境：你设想出来的那一幕
senses.definition: a supposed situation used to explain a point, as in 'imagine a scenario where...'
senses.definitionCN: 为说明某个观点而设想的处境，如“设想这样一个情景……”
senses.example: Imagine a scenario in which the power fails during the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 设想手术过程中停电的情景。
senses.why: Here no future is predicted; a scene is simply staged in the imagination so that a rule or an argument can be tested inside it.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不预测未来，只是在想象中搭起一幕，让某条规则或某个论证能在这个场景里被检验。

intro.en: Scenario is an Italian theatre word, borrowed in the 19th century. Its Greek-Latin chain is well documented; only the later extensions are approximate in date.
intro.cn: scenario 是一个意大利语戏剧词，19 世纪被借入英语。它的希腊—拉丁链条有清楚记载；只有后来的引申年代是约略的。

items.en: First recorded in English in 1878, borrowed from Italian, for the outline of an opera's plot.
items.cn: 英语最早记录于 1878 年，借自意大利语，指歌剧情节的提纲。

items.en: Italian scenario meant 'scene, outline', built from scena 'scene' plus the suffix -ario.
items.cn: 意大利语 scenario 意为“场景、提纲”，由 scena“场景”加后缀 -ario 构成。

items.en: Italian scena goes back to Latin scaena 'stage, scene', the backdrop against which action was played.
items.cn: 意大利语 scena 可追溯到拉丁语 scaena“舞台、场景”，即动作表演所依靠的背景。

items.en: Latin scaena was borrowed from Greek skene, originally a tent or hut, then the wooden stage building behind the actors.
items.cn: 拉丁语 scaena 借自希腊语 skene，原指帐篷或棚屋，后来指演员身后那座木制舞台建筑。

items.en: The word spreads from opera to film and then to futures work: scenario planning and worst-case scenarios become standard in business and policy.
items.cn: 这个词从歌剧扩散到电影，再进入未来研究：情景规划与最坏情况在商业和政策中成为标准说法。

items.en: Modern English uses scenario for imagined futures, film outlines, climate projections and planning exercises. Scene, scenic and scenography share the same stage root.
items.cn: 现代英语用 scenario 指想象未来、电影大纲、气候推演与规划练习。scene、scenic、scenography 共享同一个“舞台”词根。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stage root or a derived form; the near-meaning group compares what kind of imagined or written outline each word names.
note.cn: 形近组共享“舞台”词根或是派生形式；近义组比较每个词指的是哪一种想象或书面概要。

entries.definition: the painted backdrops of a stage, or the natural landscape of a place. It shares scaena 'stage' but means the visible setting, not the plot.
entries.definitionCN: 舞台的绘景，或某地的自然风景。它同出 scaena“舞台”，但指可见的布景，而不是情节。

entries.definition: a single division of a play, or a place where something happens. Scenario is the outline of several scenes; scene is one of them.
entries.definitionCN: 戏剧中的一个场次，或事件发生的地点。scenario 是若干场次的提纲，scene 是其中一场。

entries.definition: a person who writes scenarios or screenplays. It is scenario + -ist and not a separate root word.
entries.definitionCN: 写剧本大纲或电影剧本的人。它是 scenario + -ist，不是独立词根词。

entries.definition: the set of circumstances existing at a particular time. It is usually actual, while a scenario is imagined or projected.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻实际存在的一组情况。它通常是现实的，而 scenario 是想象或推演出来的。

entries.definition: the connected events of a story. It is the finished chain of action, while a scenario is the outline written before it.
entries.definitionCN: 故事中相互关联的事件。它是完成的行动链，而 scenario 是它之前写下的提纲。

entries.definition: a short summary of the main points of something. It is general and can describe any plan, not only scenes.
entries.definitionCN: 某事要点的简短概括。它是通用词，可指任何计划，不限场景。

entries.definition: a particular instance or set of circumstances, as in worst case. It is more neutral and less narrative than scenario.
entries.definitionCN: 某个特定实例或一组情况，如 worst case。它比 scenario 更中性、叙事性更弱。

entries.definition: an estimate of a future value based on current data. It is numerical, while a scenario may be a whole qualitative story.
entries.definitionCN: 基于现有数据对未来数值的估计。它是数字化的，而 scenario 可以是完整的定性故事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Italian stage word and real planning phrases, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的意大利语舞台词和真实规划短语，而不是编造的谐音。

normal.en: Italian scenario is scena 'scene' + -ario: literally 'a set of scenes'. That is why an outline and a future plan share the word.
normal.cn: 意大利语 scenario 是 scena“场景”+ -ario：字面就是“一组场景”。这就是提纲与未来计划共用这个词的原因。

normal.en: Greek skene was the hut behind the actors; Latin scaena was the stage; Italian scena was the scene. The whole chain is about what stands behind the action.
normal.cn: 希腊语 skene 是演员身后的棚屋；拉丁语 scaena 是舞台；意大利语 scena 是场景。整条链都关于“动作背后的那个东西”。

normal.en: Worst-case and best-case scenario are fixed phrases: the darkest and brightest scenes in the same mental rehearsal.
normal.cn: worst-case 与 best-case scenario 是固定短语：同一场脑内预演里最暗与最亮的两幕。

normal.en: Scenario planning writes several scripts instead of one, so that no single future can take the planner by surprise.
normal.cn: 情景规划写好几个剧本而不是一个，好让任何一种未来都不能让规划者措手不及。

normal.en: Climate scenario is the same stage image drawn with data: a coherent picture built from stated assumptions.
normal.cn: climate scenario 是用数据画出的同一舞台意象：由明确假设构建的一幅自洽图景。

abstract.en: Picture a board behind the stage with the scenes numbered on it. Before any actor speaks, the whole sequence already exists as a sketch.
abstract.cn: 想象舞台后方一块板，上面标着编号的场次。在任何演员开口之前，整个序列已经以草图的形式存在。

abstract.en: Move that board from the theatre to a meeting room, and the numbered scenes become possible futures; the sketch becomes a plan.
abstract.cn: 把这块板从剧场搬到会议室，编号的场次就变成可能的未来；草图就变成了方案。

abstract.en: A scenario is always a closed little world: it can be entered, compared with another and tested, which is why the word suits both plots and policy.
abstract.cn: scenario 永远是一个封闭的小世界：可以走进去、与另一个比较、被检验，所以这个词既适合情节，也适合政策。

examples.en: The report sets out three scenarios for the next decade.
examples.cn: 报告提出了未来十年的三种情景。

examples.en: In the worst-case scenario, the bridge would be closed for a year.
examples.cn: 最坏的情况下，这座桥会封闭一年。

examples.en: The film's scenario was rewritten four times before shooting.
examples.cn: 这部电影的剧本大纲在开拍前改了四次。

dict_mnemonic.text: “斯纳里欧”——斯纳里欧在台上演了一幕设想的戏 → scenario 情景、剧情提纲

root: 意大利语 scenario“场景、提纲”，来自 scena“场景”+ -ario；拉丁 scaena 源自希腊 skene“舞台、帐篷、棚屋”；核心是“把一串场景预先排在一块板上”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of scenario, all from one board of scenes: first a plot outline, then any imagined sequence, then a future that planners rehearse.
sensesIntro.cn: scenario 的九个义项都来自同一块“场次板”：先是剧情提纲，再是任何被想象的事件序列，最后是规划者预演的未来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board behind the stage on which the scenes of a story are numbered before they are performed.
core.cn: 核心意象：舞台后方一块板，故事的各场次在表演之前就被编号排好。

branches.en: DRAMATIC OUTLINE: the opera scenario and the film scenario are the same written list of scenes before dialogue exists.
branches.cn: 戏剧提纲：歌剧 scenario 与电影 scenario 都是对白出现之前写好的场次清单。

branches.en: IMAGINED SEQUENCE: the numbered scenes become any supposed chain of events, whether predicted or merely used to test an argument.
branches.cn: 想象序列：编号的场次变成任何设想的事件链，无论是预测，还是仅用来检验论证。

branches.en: CASE EXTREMES: worst-case and best-case are the darkest and brightest scenes of the same mental rehearsal.
branches.cn: 情况两端：worst-case 与 best-case 是同一场脑内预演里最暗与最亮的两幕。

branches.en: PLANNING METHODS: scenario planning and scenario analysis compare several written futures side by side.
branches.cn: 规划方法：scenario planning 与 scenario analysis 把几个写好的未来并排比较。

branches.en: MODELLED FUTURE: a climate scenario draws the same scene with data, so its consequences can be examined.
branches.cn: 模型化未来：climate scenario 用数据画出同一场景，以便检查其后果。

intro.en: Scenario is an Italian borrowing, not an English prefixed word. English adds plural -s and builds compounds such as scenario-based and scenario planning.
intro.cn: scenario 是意大利语借词，不是英语加前缀构成的词。英语加复数 -s，并构成 scenario-based、scenario planning 等复合词。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin scaena 'stage', from Greek skene 'tent, stage building'. English keeps scene, scenic, scenery and scenography from the same family, all pointing to what is visible on or behind a stage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 scaena“舞台”，来自希腊语 skene“帐篷、舞台建筑”。英语从同一家族保留 scene、scenic、scenery、scenography，都指向舞台上或舞台后可见的东西。

items.meaning: a set of scenes; an outline or projected situation
items.meaningCN: 一组场景；提纲或推演出的情境（scena + -ario）
items.example: The scenario describes a city without private cars.
items.exampleCN: 这个情景描述了一座没有私家车的城市。

items.meaning: more than one imagined sequence
items.meaningCN: 多个设想的情景（复数后缀）
items.example: The team compared four scenarios.
items.exampleCN: 团队比较了四种情景。

items.meaning: a writer of scenarios or screenplays
items.meaningCN: 剧本作者；编剧（-ist 表示从事者）
items.example: The scenarist adapted the novel for the screen.
items.exampleCN: 编剧把这部小说改编成了电影。

items.meaning: organized around imagined scenarios
items.meaningCN: 基于情景的（复合形容词）
items.example: The course uses a scenario-based approach.
items.exampleCN: 这门课程采用基于情景的方法。

items.meaning: the method of preparing for several possible futures
items.meaningCN: 情景规划（复合名词）
items.example: Scenario planning began in the oil industry.
items.exampleCN: 情景规划始于石油行业。

items.meaning: a division of a play, or a place of action
items.meaningCN: 戏剧场次；事件发生的地点（同 scaena 词根）
items.example: The last scene takes place in a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 最后一幕发生在一家医院里。

items.meaning: relating to scenery or a stage
items.meaningCN: 风景的；舞台布景的（-ic 表示“与……相关”）
items.example: The route is famous for its scenic views.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线以风景优美著称。

items.meaning: painted stage backdrops, or landscape
items.meaningCN: 舞台绘景；风景（-ery 构成集合名词）
items.example: The scenery changed at every act.
items.exampleCN: 每一幕的布景都换了。

items.meaning: the art of designing stage sets
items.meaningCN: 舞台布景术；场景设计（-graphia 表示描绘）
items.example: Her scenography turned the stage into a forest.
items.exampleCN: 她的舞台设计把舞台变成了一片森林。
